Enumeration of logging severities used by the HTSlib logging API. Values range from completely disabled (HTS_LOG_OFF) through increasingly verbose levels up to HTS_LOG_TRACE. HTS_LOG_WARNING is the library default (via hts_verbose).

Value container used by the expression engine. Represents a tri-state value: string, numeric, or unknown (null string or NaN). It is used by the wrapper functions in this header to manage a string-to-int dictionary. Opaque handle type used by the wrapper functions in this header to pass around a khash_t(str2int) instance without exposing its concrete type to callers that might not include khash.h. Resizable bitset representing a subset of integers in [0, N). Stores bits in an array of unsigned long words. Fields: n is the current number of words in use, n_max is the allocated capacity in words, and b is the bit storage with an extra sentinel word at index n holding a mask of valid bits for the final data word. Use the provided kbs_* inline functions to construct, resize, modify, iterate, and destroy.

Iterator state for traversing elements set in a kbitset_t. Fields: mask is the current bit mask within the current word, elt is the index of the current word in the bit array, and i is the current element index. Initialize with kbs_start and advance with kbs_next.

Stack frame used internally by the introsort implementation to store subrange bounds (left/right pointers cast to the array element type when used) and the remaining recursion depth. Intended for managing iterative quicksort/introsort partition processing.

objects.definition: typedef const char *ksstr_t;

Auxiliary state holder for kstrtok() tokenization. Maintains separator configuration, progress flags, small lookup table, and a pointer to the end of the current token. Used across successive kstrtok() calls; not constructed by any factory API.

Buffered low-level I/O stream handle used by htslib. Although the full struct layout is exposed here for inline helpers, it should be treated as opaque by user code. Use hopen/hdopen to construct, hclose/hflush to finalize, and hread/hwrite-style functions for I/O. Many details of the fields are internal and may change across releases.

Opaque-ish handle and state for BGZF (Blocked GZIP) I/O. Contains flags, compression level, block buffers and sizes, file position (both physical and virtual), optional cache and multithreading state, optional gzip stream pointer, and an optional on-the-fly index. Used by all bgzf_* functions to read, write, seek, and manage BGZF streams.

Option-bit enumeration controlling index caching/creation when loading. Currently defines FAI_CREATE to request automatic index creation if missing. Other flags may exist in other headers (e.g., FAI_CACHE) but are not defined here.

Tabix configuration describing column layout and parsing behavior for generic, SAM, VCF, GAF, etc. files. Fields: preset (format preset), sc (sequence column), bc (begin column), ec (end column), meta_char (lines starting with this char are meta and skipped), line_skip (number of header lines to skip). Used when building/loading tbx indexes.

Tabix index handle owning an htslib index (idx) and associated configuration (conf) and auxiliary dictionary (dict). Represents a loaded or newly built .tbi/.csi-style index for line-oriented, coordinate-sorted text formats.
Header record representing a single VCF/BCF header line, either generic (key=value) or structured (TAG=<...>). Holds parsed key/value pairs for structured lines. Used to build and query bcf_hdr_t.
Per-tag metadata for header dictionaries (FILTER/INFO/FORMAT and contigs). Encodes number, variability, type, and column type plus links to header records and a numeric ID.
Key/value pair used in header dictionaries, mapping a string key (ID or sample/contig name) to its bcf_idinfo_t metadata.
Top-level VCF/BCF header object. Owns dictionaries for IDs, contigs, and samples, plus the list of header records and sample names. Must be created and destroyed via the API.
Computed per-allele variant classification with type bitmask and length delta; populated when variant typing helpers are invoked.
Represents a single FORMAT field’s raw storage within a bcf1_t record, including type, per-sample element counts, and backing byte buffer.
Represents one INFO field’s decoded/encoded content for a bcf1_t record. Provides typed access and references into shared storage.
Internal decoded view of a bcf1_t record holding parsed ID, alleles, FILTERs, INFO array, FORMAT array, and cached variant typing. Managed as part of bcf1_t.

Top-level synced reader controller that manages multiple per-file readers, user-configurable logic (pairing/collapse, filters, indexes), sample selection, regions/targets, threading, and temporary storage. functions.name: hts_srand48
functions.description: Seeds the htslib-provided POSIX-compatible 48-bit PRNG used by the *rand48 family wrappers. Use this instead of srand48 to obtain a consistent, deterministic sequence across platforms. Typically called once before using hts_drand48/hts_lrand48 (or hts_erand48 with an implicit internal state). Exact seeding semantics follow POSIX srand48 behavior; platform differences are abstracted.
requirements: May be called at program start to initialize the PRNG state for deterministic results across platforms (inferred from comment).
Argument seed is a signed long; any value is accepted by POSIX srand48 semantics (inferred).
If deterministic output is required when using drand48/lrand48, call this before those functions (inferred).
Thread-safety/async-signal safety not documented; assume non-thread-safe unless external synchronization is used (unknown, inferred).

functions.name: hts_erand48
functions.description: Generates a double-precision pseudo-random number using the supplied 48‑bit state (xseed). Mirrors POSIX erand48 semantics, returning a value uniformly distributed in [0.0, 1.0). Intended for callers that manage their own PRNG state array to avoid global-state interactions. The xseed array is typically updated in place to the next state (POSIX pattern; exact update behavior is not explicitly documented here).
requirements: xseed must be a non-null pointer to an array of exactly 3 unsigned short elements representing a 48-bit PRNG state (inferred from signature/posix naming).
Each element of xseed is treated as 16 bits; callers should initialize xseed before first use (inferred).
Function may modify xseed to advance the PRNG state (POSIX convention; not explicitly documented—assumed).
Return value is a double in the half-open interval [0.0, 1.0) (POSIX convention; inferred).
Thread-safety depends on caller’s management of xseed; the function itself requires xseed not to be concurrently modified by other threads (inferred).

functions.name: hts_drand48
functions.description: Returns a double-precision pseudo-random number from the htslib-provided POSIX-compatible 48-bit PRNG, equivalent to POSIX drand48. Use hts_srand48 to seed for deterministic cross-platform sequences. The distribution is expected to be uniform on [0.0, 1.0).
requirements: If deterministic results are required, call hts_srand48 before first use to seed the generator (inferred).
Return value is expected to be in [0.0, 1.0) (POSIX convention; inferred).
Uses internal global PRNG state; avoid concurrent calls without synchronization if thread-safety is a concern (unknown, inferred).

functions.name: hts_lrand48
functions.description: Returns a non-negative long pseudo-random integer from the htslib-provided POSIX-compatible 48-bit PRNG, equivalent to POSIX lrand48. Use hts_srand48 to seed for deterministic cross-platform sequences. Range is expected to match POSIX lrand48 (typically 31-bit non-negative values).
requirements: If deterministic results are required, call hts_srand48 before first use to seed the generator (inferred).
Return value is a non-negative long; typical POSIX range is 0 to 2^31-1, but exact limits are not documented here (inferred and partially unknown).
Uses internal global PRNG state; avoid concurrent calls without synchronization if thread-safety is a concern (unknown, inferred).

functions.name: hts_set_log_level
functions.description: Sets the global logging verbosity for HTSlib. Call this to configure which severities are enabled for logging. Typical usage is at program initialization to choose one of the HTS_LOG_* levels (e.g., HTS_LOG_WARNING, HTS_LOG_DEBUG). The default level (if not changed) is HTS_LOG_WARNING as documented near hts_verbose. Exact filtering behavior relative to the selected level is not described here but is implied by conventional logging levels.
requirements: level must be a valid value of enum htsLogLevel (e.g., HTS_LOG_OFF, HTS_LOG_ERROR, HTS_LOG_WARNING, HTS_LOG_INFO, HTS_LOG_DEBUG, HTS_LOG_TRACE).
May be called at any time; no ordering requirement is specified, but typically set before logging.
No return value; there is no explicit error reporting.

functions.name: hts_get_log_level
functions.description: Returns the currently selected global logging level. Use this to query the current verbosity previously set via hts_set_log_level or left at its default.
requirements: No arguments required.
Returns one of the enum htsLogLevel values.
No side effects or error reporting specified.

functions.name: hts_log
functions.signature: void hts_log(enum htsLogLevel severity, const char *context, const char *format, ...) HTS_FORMAT(HTS_PRINTF_FMT, 3, 4);
functions.description: Logs an event at the given severity with a caller-supplied context string and printf-style formatting. Intended for emitting error, warning, info, debug, or trace messages. The message emission may depend on the current global log level set via hts_set_log_level; exact filtering semantics are not detailed here. The HTS_FORMAT attribute indicates printf-like format checking with the format at parameter 3 and variadic arguments starting at parameter 4.
requirements: severity must be a valid enum htsLogLevel value (HTS_LOG_ERROR, HTS_LOG_WARNING, HTS_LOG_INFO, HTS_LOG_DEBUG, or HTS_LOG_TRACE).
context should be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string describing the call site (commonly "__func__").
format must be a non-NULL printf-style format string; subsequent variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.
No return value; callers cannot directly detect logging errors from this function.
Behavior (whether a message is emitted) depends on the currently selected log level set by hts_set_log_level.

functions.name: hts_expr_val_exists
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the hts_expr_val_t represents a defined value. Treats a null string (s.s == NULL) and a NaN number as undefined; everything else is defined. Safe to call with NULL (returns 0). Useful to test whether an expression-produced value exists, irrespective of its truthiness.
requirements: v may be NULL; in that case the function returns 0 (undefined).
If non-NULL, v must point to a valid hts_expr_val_t with a properly initialized kstring_t member (e.g., via HTS_EXPR_VAL_INIT or produced by library functions).

functions.name: hts_expr_val_existsT
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the value exists or is explicitly marked as true (is_true). This extends hts_expr_val_exists() by treating is_true as existence. Safe to call with NULL (returns non-zero only if v is non-NULL and is_true is set).
requirements: v may be NULL; in that case the function behaves as if the value does not exist unless is_true would have been set (but v is NULL so returns 0).
If non-NULL, v must point to a valid hts_expr_val_t with a properly initialized kstring_t member.

functions.name: hts_expr_val_undef
functions.description: Marks an hts_expr_val_t as undefined by clearing its string, resetting is_true and is_str, and setting the numeric value to NaN. Use to reset a value to an unknown state before reuse.
requirements: v must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid hts_expr_val_t.
v->s (kstring_t) must have been initialized before (e.g., via HTS_EXPR_VAL_INIT or by prior library calls), as ks_clear() will be invoked on it.

functions.name: hts_expr_val_free
functions.description: Releases dynamic memory held by the kstring_t inside an hts_expr_val_t. Call when finished with a value that may contain an allocated string.
requirements: f must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid hts_expr_val_t.
f->s (kstring_t) must have been initialized before (e.g., via HTS_EXPR_VAL_INIT or by prior library calls), as ks_free() will be invoked on it.
After calling, the kstring_t inside f is freed; do not use previously held string pointers.

functions.name: hts_filter_init
functions.description: Parses the given filter expression and creates an opaque hts_filter_t that can later be evaluated. Returns NULL on failure (e.g., invalid expression or allocation failure).
requirements: str should be a valid NUL-terminated C string containing the filter expression.
The returned hts_filter_t* must be freed with hts_filter_free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: hts_filter_free
functions.description: Frees an hts_filter_t created by hts_filter_init. After this call, the filter pointer must not be used.
requirements: filt must be a pointer previously returned by hts_filter_init().
Do not use filt after freeing it.

functions.name: hts_filter_eval2
functions.description: Evaluates a compiled filter expression. On success, writes the result into res (either numeric or string as indicated by res->is_str; res may also be explicitly true via is_true). Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure. sym_func/data are an optional callback and user data for resolving variables in the expression.
requirements: filt must be created by hts_filter_init().
res must be initialized with HTS_EXPR_VAL_INIT before passing it to this function for the first time.
sym_func and data may be NULL if no variable lookup is needed; otherwise sym_func must match the hts_expr_sym_func signature and write the looked-up value to res appropriately.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: hts_filter_eval
functions.description: Deprecated API. Evaluates a compiled filter expression, similar to hts_filter_eval2(). Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure. Unlike hts_filter_eval2(), this function requires manual cleanup of res between repeated uses.
requirements: filt must be created by hts_filter_init().
sym_func and data may be NULL if no variable lookup is needed; otherwise sym_func must match the hts_expr_sym_func signature and write the looked-up value to res appropriately.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure.
If calling this function more than once with the same res, the caller must call hts_expr_val_free(res) between invocations to clear any allocated memory prior to reuse.

functions.name: kf_lgamma
functions.description: Computes the natural logarithm of the gamma function, log(Gamma(z)), using the AS245 (2nd) algorithm. Intended for numerical/statistical computations where the gamma function is needed in log form to avoid overflow.
requirements: Input z should avoid gamma function poles (non-positive integers), where Gamma(z) is undefined and may overflow numerically (inferred from the mathematical definition).
For stable, real-valued results, z > 0 is typically expected (inferred).
Return is a finite double when computation succeeds; behavior for arguments at/near poles or far into negative reals is implementation-dependent/unknown.

functions.name: kf_erfc
functions.description: Computes the complementary error function erfc(x) = 2/sqrt(pi) ∫_x^∞ e^(−t^2) dt, using AS66 (2nd) algorithm. Useful for normal tail probabilities and statistical calculations.
requirements: Input x is any finite double (erfc is defined for all real x).
Return value lies in [0, 2] for finite inputs (property of erfc).

functions.name: kf_gammap
functions.description: Computes the regularized lower incomplete gamma function P(s, z). Per the header notes, formulas follow Numerical Recipes and AS245; P(s,z) + Q(s,z) = 1.
requirements: s > 0 (standard domain for the regularized incomplete gamma function; inferred).
z ≥ 0 (typical usage domain; inferred).
Return value is in [0, 1] for valid-domain inputs (property of the regularized function).
For large s or z, numerical precision limits may apply (inferred from numerical methods).

functions.name: kf_gammaq
functions.description: Computes the regularized upper incomplete gamma function Q(s, z). The product Q(s,z) * tgamma(s) equals the upper incomplete gamma function commonly found in references.
requirements: s > 0 (standard domain; inferred).
z ≥ 0 (typical usage domain; inferred).
Return value is in [0, 1] for valid-domain inputs (property of the regularized function).
Satisfies kf_gammap(s,z) + kf_gammaq(s,z) = 1 for valid-domain inputs.

functions.name: kf_betai
functions.signature: double kf_betai(double a, double b, double x);
functions.description: Computes the regularized incomplete beta function I_x(a, b). As noted, the (unregularized) incomplete beta equals kf_betai(a,b,x) * gamma(a) * gamma(b) / gamma(a+b). Implementation follows Numerical Recipes 2nd ed., §6.4.
requirements: a > 0 and b > 0 (standard domain for beta and incomplete beta; inferred).
x ∈ [0, 1] (definition domain; inferred).
Return value lies in [0, 1] for valid-domain inputs (property of the regularized function).
Numerical accuracy may degrade when a and/or b are very small or very large (inferred from typical implementations).

functions.name: kt_fisher_exact
functions.signature: double kt_fisher_exact(int n11, int n12, int n21, int n22, double *_left, double *_right, double *two);
functions.description: Computes Fisher’s exact test on a 2×2 contingency table with counts n11, n12, n21, n22. Returns the (likely) p-value corresponding to the observed table and writes tail probabilities to *_left and *_right, and a two-sided p-value to *two.
requirements: n11, n12, n21, n22 should be non-negative integers (counts in a contingency table; inferred).
The 2×2 table totals are implicitly defined; extremely large totals may cause numerical issues (inferred).
Pointers _left, _right, and two must be valid, non-null pointers to writable doubles (required by the signature to store outputs; nullability not documented).
Returned and output probabilities should be within [0, 1] (probability range; inferred).
Caller must ensure the table is meaningful (e.g., sum > 0) to avoid degenerate tests (inferred).

functions.name: __ac_X31_hash_string
functions.description: Computes a hash of a NUL-terminated C string using a multiplicative (X31) scheme. Intended for hashing ASCII/byte strings as keys in khash tables. Returns a khint_t hash value. Pure function with no side effects.
requirements: s must be a valid, non-null pointer to a NUL-terminated string
The memory referenced by s must be readable up to and including the terminating NUL
Input bytes are used as-is; hashing is byte-wise and case-sensitive

functions.name: __ac_FNV1a_hash_string
functions.description: Computes an FNV-1a hash of a NUL-terminated C string. Suitable for hashing strings as khash keys. Returns a khint_t hash value. Pure function with no side effects.
requirements: s must be a valid, non-null pointer to a NUL-terminated string
The memory referenced by s must be readable up to and including the terminating NUL
Hashing is byte-wise and case-sensitive

functions.name: __ac_X31_hash_kstring
functions.description: Computes a hash of a kstring_t using a multiplicative (X31) scheme. Uses ks.l bytes from ks.s (does not require NUL termination). Returns a khint_t hash value. Pure function with no side effects.
requirements: ks.s must point to a readable buffer of at least ks.l bytes
ks.l may be zero; in that case the hash of an empty sequence is returned
ks is passed by value and not modified

functions.name: __ac_FNV1a_hash_kstring
functions.description: Computes an FNV-1a hash of a kstring_t. Processes exactly ks.l bytes from ks.s (no NUL required). Returns a khint_t hash value. Pure function with no side effects.
requirements: ks.s must point to a readable buffer of at least ks.l bytes
ks.l may be zero; in that case the hash of an empty sequence is returned
ks is passed by value and not modified

functions.name: __ac_Wang_hash
functions.description: Applies Wang’s integer mix function to scramble an integer key into a hash value. Useful for hashing integer keys. Returns a khint_t hash value. Pure function with no side effects.
requirements: key may be any khint_t value (no range restrictions)

functions.name: khash_str2int_init
functions.description: Creates and returns a new khash map that associates C strings with int values. The caller owns the returned handle and must destroy it with khash_str2int_destroy() or khash_str2int_destroy_free() when finished.
requirements: Must be called before using the returned hash with other khash_str2int_* functions.
Return value is a hash handle to be passed as the _hash parameter to other functions.
On allocation failure, underlying kh_init may return NULL; callers should check for NULL before further use.

functions.name: khash_str2int_destroy
functions.description: Destroys the hash table structure without freeing any key strings. Use when key strings are managed elsewhere. Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: _hash may be NULL (no-op).
_hash, if non-NULL, must be a hash created by khash_str2int_init().
Do not use the hash after this call.
Keys are not freed; the caller remains responsible for their lifetime and deallocation.

functions.name: khash_str2int_destroy_free
functions.description: Destroys the hash table and also frees all stored key strings using free(). Safe to call with NULL. Use when the hash owns dynamically allocated keys.
requirements: _hash may be NULL (no-op).
_hash, if non-NULL, must be a hash created by khash_str2int_init().
All keys must have been allocated with a malloc-compatible allocator suitable for free().
Do not use the hash after this call.
Do not reuse any freed key pointers elsewhere (avoid double-free or use-after-free).

functions.name: khash_str2int_has_key
functions.signature: static inline int khash_str2int_has_key(void *_hash, const char *str)
functions.description: Checks whether the given C-string key exists in the hash. Returns 1 if present, 0 otherwise.
requirements: _hash must be a valid, non-NULL hash returned by khash_str2int_init().
str must be a valid, non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string that remains readable for the duration of the call.

functions.name: khash_str2int_get
functions.signature: static inline int khash_str2int_get(void *_hash, const char *str, int *value)
functions.description: Looks up a key and, if found, optionally stores its associated int value into *value. Returns 0 on success and -1 if the hash is NULL or the key is not present.
requirements: _hash should be a valid hash created by khash_str2int_init(); if NULL, the function returns -1.
str must be a valid, non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string that remains readable for the duration of the call.
value may be NULL to ignore the retrieved value; if non-NULL, it must be a valid pointer to writable int storage.

functions.name: khash_str2int_inc
functions.signature: static inline int khash_str2int_inc(void *_hash, const char *str)
functions.description: Inserts the key if absent and assigns it an auto-incremented integer id; if the key already exists, returns its current id. On success returns the id (>=0), on error returns -1. Keys are not copied; the pointer is stored.
requirements: _hash must be a valid, non-NULL hash created by khash_str2int_init().
str must be a valid, non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string.
The key string memory must remain valid and unchanged for the entire lifetime of the hash (keys are not duplicated).
Do not pass stack- or temporary-lifetime strings unless their lifetime extends until the hash is destroyed; prefer heap-allocated or otherwise persistent strings.
Check the return value for -1 to detect insertion errors.

functions.name: khash_str2int_set
functions.signature: static inline int khash_str2int_set(void *_hash, const char *str, int value)
functions.description: Sets (inserts or updates) the key’s associated integer value. Returns the internal bin index (non-negative) on success, or -1 on error. Keys are not copied; the pointer is stored.
requirements: _hash must be a valid, non-NULL hash created by khash_str2int_init().
str must be a valid, non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string.
The key string memory must remain valid and unchanged for the entire lifetime of the hash (keys are not duplicated).
Callers should treat the returned bin index as an opaque internal value; only the success (>=0) or failure (-1) matters.
Check the return value for -1 to detect insertion errors.

functions.name: khash_str2int_size
functions.description: Returns the number of keys currently stored in the hash.
requirements: _hash must be a valid, non-NULL hash created by khash_str2int_init().

functions.name: kbs_init2
functions.signature: static inline kbitset_t *kbs_init2(size_t ni, int fill)
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a bitset capable of representing integers in the range [0, ni). If fill == 0, the set is initialized empty; otherwise it is initialized to contain all elements in [0, ni). Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: Caller must pass ni > 0 when fill != 0 to avoid out-of-bounds access in the implementation.
Returned pointer must be checked for NULL to handle allocation failure.
The returned kbitset_t* must later be released with kbs_destroy() or resized with kbs_resize()/kbs_resize2() as appropriate.
The resulting bitset supports indices 0 <= i < ni.

functions.name: kbs_init
functions.description: Allocates and initializes an empty bitset capable of representing integers in the range [0, ni). Returns NULL on allocation failure. This is a convenience wrapper for kbs_init2(ni, 0).
requirements: Returned pointer must be checked for NULL to handle allocation failure.
The resulting bitset supports indices 0 <= i < ni.
The returned kbitset_t* must later be released with kbs_destroy() or resized with kbs_resize()/kbs_resize2().

functions.name: kbs_resize2
functions.signature: static inline int kbs_resize2(kbitset_t **bsp, size_t ni_new, int fill)
functions.description: Resizes an existing bitset to represent integers in the range [0, ni_new). If *bsp is NULL or capacity is insufficient, reallocates the bitset. Newly added range [ni_old, ni_new) is inserted into the set if fill != 0; otherwise those bits are cleared. Returns 0 on success, -1 on allocation failure.
requirements: bsp must be a valid non-NULL pointer to a kbitset_t* storage location.
*bsp may be NULL; on success it will be set to a newly allocated bitset.
ni_new must be > 0 to avoid out-of-bounds access in the implementation (the code accesses index n_new-1).
On return -1, *bsp is unchanged (realloc failure semantics in this implementation’s usage).
After successful resize, valid indices are 0 <= i < ni_new.
If fill != 0, caller should expect bits in [ni_old, ni_new) to be set (added to the set).

functions.name: kbs_resize
functions.signature: static inline int kbs_resize(kbitset_t **bsp, size_t ni_new)
functions.description: Resizes an existing bitset to represent integers in the range [0, ni_new). Newly added range is cleared. Returns 0 on success, negative on error. Convenience wrapper for kbs_resize2(bsp, ni_new, 0).
requirements: bsp must be a valid non-NULL pointer to a kbitset_t* storage location.
*bsp may be NULL; on success it will be set to a newly allocated bitset.
ni_new should be > 0 to avoid out-of-bounds access in the implementation (the code accesses index n_new-1).
Caller must check the return value and handle negative return as an error.
After successful resize, valid indices are 0 <= i < ni_new.

functions.name: kbs_destroy
functions.description: Frees a bitset previously allocated by kbs_init/kbs_init2 or allocated/resized by kbs_resize/kbs_resize2. Safe to call with NULL (free(NULL) is a no-op).
requirements: bs must point to a bitset allocated by the corresponding allocation/resizing functions or be NULL.
After this call, the bs pointer (if non-NULL) becomes invalid and must not be used.

functions.name: kbs_clear
functions.description: Resets all bits in the bitset to zero, making the set empty while retaining current capacity.
requirements: bs must be a valid, initialized bitset (non-NULL).
The bitset must have been initialized/resized correctly so that internal sizing fields are consistent.

functions.name: kbs_insert_all
functions.description: Sets all valid bits in the bitset, making the set contain every element in [0, current_ni). Excess bits in the last storage word are masked off.
requirements: bs must be a valid, initialized bitset (non-NULL).
The bitset must have capacity for at least one element (bs->n >= 1), as the implementation accesses bs->b[bs->n-1].

functions.name: kbs_insert
functions.signature: static inline void kbs_insert(kbitset_t *bs, int i)
functions.description: Inserts element i into the bitset by setting the corresponding bit.
requirements: bs must be a valid, initialized bitset (non-NULL).
i must be within the current representable range: 0 <= i < current_ni used to initialize/resize the bitset; otherwise behavior is undefined due to out-of-bounds access.

functions.name: kbs_delete
functions.signature: static inline void kbs_delete(kbitset_t *bs, int i)
functions.description: Removes element i from the bitset by clearing the corresponding bit.
requirements: bs must be a valid, initialized bitset (non-NULL).
i must be within the current representable range: 0 <= i < current_ni used to initialize/resize the bitset; otherwise behavior is undefined due to out-of-bounds access.

functions.name: kbs_exists
functions.signature: static inline int kbs_exists(const kbitset_t *bs, int i)
functions.description: Tests whether element i is present in the bitset. Returns nonzero if present, zero otherwise.
requirements: bs must be a valid, initialized bitset (non-NULL).
i must be within the current representable range: 0 <= i < current_ni used to initialize/resize the bitset; otherwise behavior is undefined due to out-of-bounds access.

functions.name: kbs_start
functions.description: Initializes or resets an iterator for traversing set elements with kbs_next(). Must be called before the first kbs_next() on an iterator.
requirements: itr must be a valid non-NULL pointer to a kbitset_iter_t.
Call this before the first use of itr with kbs_next(), or to restart an iteration.

functions.name: kbs_next
functions.signature: static inline int kbs_next(const kbitset_t *bs, kbitset_iter_t *itr)
functions.description: Returns the next set element index via the iterator and advances the iterator. Returns -1 when there are no more elements. Relies on the bitset’s internal sentinel word set by initialization/resizing.
requirements: bs must be a valid, initialized bitset (non-NULL), created or resized using these APIs so that the sentinel word bs->b[bs->n] is properly set.
itr must be a valid non-NULL pointer previously initialized with kbs_start().
The bitset must not be concurrently modified in a way that invalidates iteration state during traversal.

functions.name: hts_drand48
functions.description: Returns a pseudo-random double, intended as a portable replacement for drand48() (used by ks_shuffle in this header). Typical use is to obtain a uniform random value in [0.0, 1.0) for shuffling or other randomized algorithms. Link-time symbol is provided by HTSlib.
requirements: Call with no arguments.
Caller must link against the library providing hts_drand48 (HTSlib).
Range and distribution are not documented here; by convention drand48-style functions return a uniform value in [0.0, 1.0).

functions.name: ks_mergesort_##name
functions.signature: int ks_mergesort_##name(size_t n, type_t array[], type_t temp[])
functions.description: Macro-generated stable mergesort over an array of type_t, in ascending order per the instantiation comparator. If temp is NULL, a temporary buffer is allocated internally and freed before return. Returns 0 on completion. Provided by KSORT_INIT_* macros; actual symbol is produced when you instantiate with a concrete element type and comparator.
requirements: Must be instantiated via KSORT_INIT/KSORT_INIT_STATIC/KSORT_INIT2 before use (type_t and comparator defined).
array must point to at least n elements unless n==0.
temp must either be NULL (function will malloc and free its own buffer) or point to a buffer of at least n elements of type_t.
Comparator used at instantiation must impose a strict weak ordering for correct sorting.
n may be 0; in that case array may be NULL.

functions.name: ks_heapadjust_##name
functions.signature: void ks_heapadjust_##name(size_t i, size_t n, type_t l[])
functions.description: Macro-generated sift-down (heap-adjust) operation for a max-heap over l[0..n-1] with comparator-defined ordering. Adjusts the element at index i downward to restore the heap property.
requirements: Must be instantiated via KSORT_INIT/KSORT_INIT_STATIC/KSORT_INIT2 before use.
l must point to at least n elements unless n==0.
i must satisfy i < n when n>0.
n must be > 0 to have any effect; with n==0 or n==1, no adjustment needed.
Comparator used at instantiation must be consistent with the heap that callers intend to maintain.

functions.name: ks_heapmake_##name
functions.description: Macro-generated heap builder that transforms l[0..lsize-1] into a max-heap with respect to the instantiated comparator.
requirements: Must be instantiated via KSORT_INIT/KSORT_INIT_STATIC/KSORT_INIT2 before use.
l must point to at least lsize elements unless lsize==0.
lsize must be > 0 to avoid underflowing the internal loop index; passing 0 is not supported by the implementation.
Comparator used at instantiation must be strict weak ordering.

functions.name: ks_heapsort_##name
functions.description: Macro-generated in-place heapsort of l[0..lsize-1] into ascending order per the instantiated comparator. Builds/uses a max-heap and repeatedly extracts the maximum.
requirements: Must be instantiated via KSORT_INIT/KSORT_INIT_STATIC/KSORT_INIT2 before use.
l must point to at least lsize elements.
lsize must be > 0; the implementation dereferences l and uses lsize-1.
Comparator used at instantiation must impose a strict weak ordering for correct sorting.

functions.name: ks_combsort_##name
functions.description: Macro-generated combsort (with final insertion sort pass) over a[0..n-1] in ascending order per the instantiated comparator. Useful as a fallback or for small arrays.
requirements: Must be instantiated via KSORT_INIT/KSORT_INIT_STATIC/KSORT_INIT2 before use.
a must point to at least n elements unless n==0.
Comparator used at instantiation must impose a strict weak ordering.
n may be 0; the function is a no-op in that case (array may be NULL when n==0).

functions.name: ks_introsort_##name
functions.description: Macro-generated introsort (quicksort with depth limit switching to combsort and final insertion sort) that sorts a[0..n-1] in ascending order per the instantiated comparator. Returns 0 on completion.
requirements: Must be instantiated via KSORT_INIT/KSORT_INIT_STATIC/KSORT_INIT2 before use.
a must point to at least n elements unless n==0.
n may be 0; function returns 0 immediately. For n==2, it swaps if out of order.
Comparator used at instantiation must impose a strict weak ordering for correctness and termination.

functions.name: ks_ksmall_##name
functions.signature: type_t ks_ksmall_##name(size_t n, type_t arr[], size_t kk)
functions.description: Macro-generated selection (k-th smallest) algorithm adapted from ndevilla’s median code. Partitions in place and returns the value of the element that would be at index kk if arr[0..n-1] were sorted ascending per the instantiated comparator.
requirements: Must be instantiated via KSORT_INIT/KSORT_INIT_STATIC/KSORT_INIT2 before use.
arr must point to at least n elements.
kk must satisfy 0 <= kk < n (explicitly documented in the header).
Comparator used at instantiation must impose a strict weak ordering.
The function reorders elements of arr in place; callers must not rely on original order.

functions.name: ks_shuffle_##name
functions.description: Macro-generated in-place Fisher–Yates shuffle of a[0..n-1], using hts_drand48() as the RNG source. Produces a uniform random permutation under ideal RNG behavior.
requirements: Must be instantiated via KSORT_INIT/KSORT_INIT_STATIC/KSORT_INIT2 before use.
a must point to at least n elements unless n<=1.
n <= 1 is permitted and results in a no-op (a may be NULL in that case).
Relies on external double hts_drand48(void); this must be linked and provide values in [0,1).

functions.name: ks_mergesort
functions.signature: int ks_mergesort_name(size_t n, type_t array[], type_t temp[])
functions.description: Stable in-place mergesort for arrays generated via KSORT_INIT. This is invoked through the macro ks_mergesort(name, n, array, temp) and dispatches to the instantiated symbol ks_mergesort_name for the element type and comparator bound by KSORT_INIT/KSORT_INIT_STATIC/KSORT_INIT2. If temp is NULL, an auxiliary buffer of n elements is allocated internally and freed before return. Returns 0.
requirements: Before calling, you must instantiate the sorter with KSORT_INIT (or variant) using a tag ‘name’, an element type ‘type_t’, and a strict-weak-order comparator; this generates ks_mergesort_name.
array must point to at least n elements of type_t; if n == 0 the function is a no-op and returns 0.
If temp is not NULL, it must point to a separate buffer of at least n elements of type_t and must not overlap array.
If temp is NULL, the function will allocate a temporary buffer of n elements; allocation must succeed (no error is reported if it fails).
The comparator supplied at instantiation must be consistent (strict weak ordering) to ensure correct sorting.

functions.name: ks_introsort
functions.description: In-place introspective sort (quicksort with fallback) generated via KSORT_INIT. Call via ks_introsort(name, n, a) which dispatches to ks_introsort_name. Uses combsort/insertion sort for small/deep cases. Not stable. Returns 0.
requirements: Must be instantiated beforehand with KSORT_INIT (or variant) to define ks_introsort_name for the chosen type_t and comparator.
a must point to at least n elements of type_t; safe for n == 0.
Comparator supplied at instantiation must implement a strict weak ordering for correctness.

functions.name: ks_combsort
functions.description: In-place combsort for arrays generated via KSORT_INIT. Call via ks_combsort(name, n, a) which dispatches to ks_combsort_name. Not stable; finishes with insertion sort for final pass.
requirements: Must be instantiated beforehand with KSORT_INIT (or variant) to define ks_combsort_name.
a must point to at least n elements of type_t; safe for n == 0.
Comparator supplied at instantiation must implement a strict weak ordering.

functions.name: ks_heapsort
functions.description: In-place heapsort for arrays generated via KSORT_INIT. Call via ks_heapsort(name, lsize, l) which dispatches to ks_heapsort_name. Not stable.
requirements: Must be instantiated beforehand with KSORT_INIT (or variant) to define ks_heapsort_name.
l must point to at least lsize elements of type_t.
lsize must be >= 1 (function loops from lsize - 1 down to 1; lsize == 0 would underflow and is invalid).
Comparator supplied at instantiation must implement a strict weak ordering.

functions.name: ks_heapmake
functions.description: Transforms an array into a max-heap in-place (heap construction) generated via KSORT_INIT. Call via ks_heapmake(name, lsize, l) which dispatches to ks_heapmake_name. Used as a building block for heapsort.
requirements: Must be instantiated beforehand with KSORT_INIT (or variant) to define ks_heapmake_name.
l must point to at least lsize elements of type_t; safe for lsize == 0.
Comparator supplied at instantiation must implement a strict weak ordering.

functions.name: ks_heapadjust
functions.signature: void ks_heapadjust_name(size_t i, size_t n, type_t l[])
functions.description: Sifts down the element at index i within an n-element array to maintain the max-heap property, generated via KSORT_INIT. Call via ks_heapadjust(name, i, n, l) which dispatches to ks_heapadjust_name.
requirements: Must be instantiated beforehand with KSORT_INIT (or variant) to define ks_heapadjust_name.
l must point to at least n elements of type_t.
i must satisfy 0 <= i < n; n may be 0 only if not called.
Comparator supplied at instantiation must implement a strict weak ordering.

functions.name: ks_ksmall
functions.signature: type_t ks_ksmall_name(size_t n, type_t arr[], size_t kk)
functions.description: Selects and returns the k-th smallest element (0-based) using an in-place selection algorithm (Quickselect variant). Generated via KSORT_INIT; call via ks_ksmall(name, n, arr, kk). May reorder elements in arr.
requirements: Must be instantiated beforehand with KSORT_INIT (or variant) to define ks_ksmall_name.
arr must point to at least n elements of type_t.
kk must satisfy 0 <= kk < n (as stated in the source comment).
The function modifies arr in-place; callers must not rely on the original order after the call.
Comparator supplied at instantiation must implement a strict weak ordering.

functions.name: ks_shuffle
functions.description: In-place Fisher–Yates shuffle using hts_drand48() for randomness. Generated via KSORT_INIT; call via ks_shuffle(name, n, a).
requirements: Must be instantiated beforehand with KSORT_INIT (or variant) to define ks_shuffle_name.
a must point to at least n elements of type_t.
n must be representable as an int (the implementation uses int loop counters); require n <= INT_MAX.
Randomness is sourced from hts_drand48(); quality and thread-safety characteristics of hts_drand48 are outside this header and thus unknown.

functions.name: kvsprintf
functions.signature: int kvsprintf(kstring_t *s, const char *fmt, va_list ap)
functions.description: Formats text per printf-style format string and appends it to the kstring buffer using a supplied va_list. Intended as a vsprintf-like helper for kstring_t. Exact return semantics are not documented here; typically such functions return the number of characters written or a negative value on error.
requirements: s must point to a valid kstring_t (initialized with KS_INITIALIZE, ks_initialize(), or otherwise in a valid state).
fmt should be a valid printf-style format string; behavior is undefined if it is NULL.
ap must be an initialized va_list corresponding to fmt and valid for the duration of the call.
On allocation failure the function may return an error (exact errno/return not documented here).

functions.name: ksprintf
functions.description: Formats text per printf-style format string and appends it to the kstring buffer. Varargs equivalent of kvsprintf.
requirements: s must point to a valid kstring_t.
fmt should be a valid printf-style format string; behavior is undefined if it is NULL.
The variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in fmt.
On allocation failure the function may return an error (exact errno/return not documented here).

functions.name: kputd
functions.description: Appends a textual representation of the double d to the kstring using a custom %g-only formatter.
requirements: s must point to a valid kstring_t.
No specific range constraints on d are documented.
Returns an error code on failure (e.g., memory allocation failure); precise return convention beyond that is not documented here.

functions.name: ksplit_core
functions.signature: int ksplit_core(char *s, int delimiter, int *_max, int **_offsets)
functions.description: Splits the mutable C string s by the given delimiter and records component start offsets into *_offsets, growing the offsets array as needed. Returns the number of components found. Commonly used internally by ksplit().
requirements: s must be a mutable, NUL-terminated string; the function may modify s (typical splitters replace delimiters with NUL).
delimiter is treated as a byte value (0..255) indicating the separator character.
_max must point to an int tracking the current allocated size of *_offsets; it will be updated as the array grows.
_offsets must point to an int* that may be realloc()'d; on success it points to an array of at least the returned count.
Caller is responsible for eventual deallocation of *_offsets if dynamically allocated (inferred from typical API; exact ownership not documented here).

functions.name: kstrstr
functions.description: Finds the first occurrence of pattern pat in string str, optionally using and/or producing a prepared search table via _prep for efficiency. Returns a pointer to the match within str or NULL if not found.
requirements: str must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
pat must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
_prep may be NULL or may point to an int* cache pointer used internally for faster repeated searches; exact preparation/ownership semantics are not documented here.
Returned pointer, if non-NULL, aliases memory within str and must not be freed.

functions.name: kstrnstr
functions.signature: char *kstrnstr(const char *str, const char *pat, int n, int **_prep)
functions.description: Finds the first occurrence of pattern pat within the first n bytes of str, optionally using/producing a prepared table via _prep. Returns a pointer to the match within str or NULL if not found.
requirements: str must reference at least n bytes; if not NUL-terminated within n, the search is bounded by n.
pat must be a valid NUL-terminated pattern.
n must be non-negative; behavior for negative values is undefined (parameter is int).
_prep may be NULL or may point to an int* cache pointer used internally; exact ownership semantics are not documented.
Returned pointer, if non-NULL, aliases memory within str and must not be freed.

functions.name: kmemmem
functions.signature: void *kmemmem(const void *_str, int n, const void *_pat, int m, int **_prep)
functions.description: Searches for binary pattern _pat of length m within the memory block _str of length n, optionally using/producing a prepared search table via _prep. Returns a pointer to the first occurrence or NULL if not found.
requirements: _str must point to a buffer of at least n bytes.
_pat must point to a buffer of at least m bytes.
n and m must be non-negative; behavior for negative values is undefined (parameters are int).
_prep may be NULL or may point to an int* cache pointer used internally; exact ownership semantics are not documented.
Returned pointer, if non-NULL, aliases memory within _str and must not be freed.

functions.name: kstrtok
functions.description: Tokenizes str on any of the separator characters in sep without modifying str. Similar to strtok_r(), but str and sep can be NULL on subsequent calls for efficiency (if sep is unchanged). Returns a pointer to the next token within str, or NULL when finished.
requirements: aux must be non-NULL and persist across calls to maintain state.
On the first call, str should be the string to tokenize; subsequent calls can pass str=NULL to continue tokenization of the same string.
sep may be NULL on subsequent calls if unchanged; on the first call, pass the desired separator set (as a NUL-terminated string).
Returned pointer aliases memory within str and must not be freed; it is valid until str’s storage changes.
str is not modified by this function.

functions.name: kgetline
functions.description: Appends a single line read from the source described by fp using the supplied fgets()-like function. Line terminators "\n" or "\r\n" are not included in the appended data. Returns 0 on success, or EOF at end of file or on error (as detected via the fgets_fn/fp).
requirements: s must point to a valid kstring_t to which data can be appended.
fgets_fn must be a function with signature char *(char *, int, void *) that behaves like fgets(), reading from fp.
fp is passed through to fgets_fn and must be valid per that function’s expectations.
On success, appended data is not NUL-terminated by this function’s contract description; however kstring functions typically maintain a trailing NUL after appends.

functions.name: kgetline2
functions.description: Appends a single line read from the source described by fp using the supplied hgetln()-like function (ssize_t returning). Line terminators "\n" or "\r\n" are not included in the appended data. Returns 0 on success, or EOF at end of file or on error (as detected via the supplied function).
requirements: s must point to a valid kstring_t to which data can be appended.
fgets_fn must be a function with signature ssize_t (char *, size_t, void *) that behaves like an hgetln()-like getter for fp.
fp is passed through to fgets_fn and must be valid per that function’s expectations.

functions.name: ks_initialize
functions.description: Initializes a kstring_t by zeroing its length and capacity and setting its buffer pointer to NULL. Equivalent to assigning KS_INITIALIZE.
requirements: s must be non-NULL.

Should only be called on an uninitialized kstring_t or one whose buffer ownership has been relinquished (e.g., via ks_release() or ks_free()); calling it on a live kstring_t with an allocated buffer will leak that buffer.

functions.name: ks_resize
functions.description: Ensures the kstring has capacity at least size bytes (not including any implicit assumptions about the trailing NUL). Grows the buffer (via realloc) if needed and updates s->m.
requirements: s must be non-NULL.
On success, s->s may be reallocated; any previous pointers into s->s become invalid.
Returns 0 on success; returns -1 on allocation failure (leaving s in its prior valid state).
Passing a very large size may overflow internal growth heuristics; the function attempts to handle this but behavior is allocation-dependent.

functions.name: ks_expand
functions.description: Ensures capacity for appending expansion bytes beyond the current length s->l. Computes a new required size of s->l + expansion and calls ks_resize().
requirements: s must be non-NULL and in a valid state.
expansion must be such that s->l + expansion does not overflow size_t; if it would, the function sets errno=EOVERFLOW and returns -1.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on error.

functions.name: ks_str
functions.description: Returns the underlying mutable buffer pointer s->s. May be NULL if the kstring has no buffer.
requirements: s must be non-NULL.
The returned pointer is owned by the kstring; do not free it directly unless obtained via ks_release().

functions.name: ks_c_str
functions.description: Returns a C-string view of the kstring. If the kstring is empty or has no buffer, returns a pointer to a read-only empty string ""; otherwise returns s->s.
requirements: s must be non-NULL.
The returned pointer may be to read-only storage when the string is empty; do not attempt to modify it.

functions.name: ks_len
functions.description: Returns the current length (number of bytes of data) stored in the kstring.
requirements: s must be non-NULL.

functions.name: ks_clear
functions.description: Resets the kstring length to zero (does not free or shrink capacity) and returns s. Typically used to reuse an existing buffer.
requirements: s must be non-NULL.
Any existing buffer remains allocated; subsequent appends will overwrite prior contents.

functions.name: ks_release
functions.description: Releases ownership of the underlying buffer from the kstring and returns it to the caller. Resets s to an empty, uninitialized state (l=m=0 and s->s=NULL). The caller becomes responsible for freeing the returned pointer.
requirements: s must be non-NULL.
If s->s is non-NULL, the returned pointer must be freed by the caller when no longer needed (e.g., with free()).
After this call, the kstring_t is empty and can be reused or allowed to go out of scope without leaking.

functions.name: ks_free
functions.description: Safely frees the underlying buffer of a kstring (if any) and reinitializes the structure to an empty state.
requirements: s may be NULL; if non-NULL, s->s is freed and the structure is reset via ks_initialize().
Do not use any previously obtained pointers into s->s after calling this.

functions.name: kputsn
functions.signature: int kputsn(const char *p, size_t l, kstring_t *s)
functions.description: Appends l bytes from p to the kstring and then appends a terminating NUL. Returns l on success or EOF on error. Sets errno=EOVERFLOW if size addition would overflow.
requirements: s must be non-NULL and valid.
If p is NULL, behavior is undefined; pass a valid pointer when l>0.
l may be zero; in this case, the function ensures a NUL terminator exists.
Returns EOF on allocation failure or on overflow; errno may be set to EOVERFLOW for size wrap-around.

functions.name: kputs
functions.description: Appends the NUL-terminated string p to the kstring (including adding a trailing NUL in the kstring). Returns the number of bytes appended (strlen(p)) on success, or -1 with errno=EFAULT if p is NULL, or EOF on allocation/overflow errors propagated from kputsn.
requirements: s must be non-NULL and valid.
p must be a valid NUL-terminated string; if p is NULL, the function returns -1 and sets errno=EFAULT.

functions.name: kputc
functions.description: Appends a single byte (low 8 bits of c) to the kstring and appends a trailing NUL. Returns the appended character value (as unsigned char) on success or EOF on error.
requirements: s must be non-NULL and valid.
On allocation failure returns EOF; otherwise ensures there is room for the character and a NUL terminator.

functions.name: kputc_
functions.description: Appends a single byte (low 8 bits of c) to the kstring without appending a NUL terminator. Returns 1 on success or EOF on error.
requirements: s must be non-NULL and valid.
Use when building data without relying on NUL-termination; caller is responsible for any later termination if needed.

functions.name: kputsn_
functions.signature: int kputsn_(const void *p, size_t l, kstring_t *s)
functions.description: Appends l bytes from p to the kstring without appending a NUL terminator. Returns l on success or EOF on error. Sets errno=EOVERFLOW if size addition would overflow.
requirements: s must be non-NULL and valid.
p must point to at least l bytes (may be NULL when l==0 only if tolerated by memcpy behavior is avoided; the code copies only when l>0).
Returns EOF on allocation failure or overflow; errno may be set to EOVERFLOW for size wrap-around.

functions.name: kputuw
functions.description: Appends the decimal string representation of the unsigned integer x to the kstring, maintaining a trailing NUL. Optimized to write digits two at a time. Returns 0 on success or EOF on error.
requirements: s must be non-NULL and valid.
On allocation failure returns EOF.
Handles x in full unsigned int range.

functions.name: kputw
functions.description: Appends the decimal string representation of the signed integer c to the kstring, adding a leading '-' for negatives, and maintains a trailing NUL. Returns 0 on success or EOF on error.
requirements: s must be non-NULL and valid.
On allocation failure returns EOF.

functions.name: kputll
functions.description: Appends the decimal string representation of the signed long long c to the kstring, adding a leading '-' for negatives, and maintains a trailing NUL. Optimized for large values. Returns 0 on success or EOF on error.
requirements: s must be non-NULL and valid.
On allocation failure returns EOF.

functions.name: kputl
functions.description: Appends the decimal string representation of the signed long c to the kstring. Thin wrapper over kputll(). Returns 0 on success or EOF on error.
requirements: s must be non-NULL and valid.
On allocation failure returns EOF.

functions.name: ksplit
functions.description: Splits the kstring’s underlying C-string buffer s->s by delimiter using ksplit_core(). Returns a newly (re)allocated array of offsets into s->s and sets *n to the number of components; returns NULL on failure.
requirements: s must be non-NULL, and s->s must be a valid mutable NUL-terminated string.
n must be non-NULL; on success it is set to the number of components.
The returned offsets array is dynamically allocated via ksplit_core() and should be freed by the caller when no longer needed (inferred; exact ownership not explicitly documented here).
ksplit_core() may modify s->s (typical split behavior).

functions.name: kinsert_char
functions.signature: int kinsert_char(char c, size_t pos, kstring_t *s)
functions.description: Inserts character c at byte position pos in the kstring, shifting existing data right, and updates the trailing NUL. Returns 0 on success or EOF on failure.
requirements: s must be non-NULL and valid.
pos must be in the range 0..s->l inclusive; otherwise returns EOF.
On allocation failure returns EOF.

functions.name: kinsert_str
functions.signature: int kinsert_str(const char *str, size_t pos, kstring_t *s)
functions.description: Inserts the NUL-terminated string str at byte position pos in the kstring, shifting existing data right, and maintains a single trailing NUL. An empty input string performs no update and returns 0. Returns 0 on success or EOF on failure.
requirements: s must be non-NULL and valid.
str must be non-NULL; if NULL the function returns EOF.
pos must be in the range 0..s->l inclusive; otherwise returns EOF.
On allocation failure returns EOF.
If str is empty (strlen(str)==0), no modification is made and 0 is returned.

functions.name: ks_getuntil2
functions.signature: int ks_getuntil2(kstream_t *ks, int delimiter, kstring_t *str, int *dret, int append);
functions.description: Reads bytes from the buffered stream ks into str until a delimiter is encountered or EOF/error occurs. Supports delimiter modes: KS_SEP_SPACE (any isspace), KS_SEP_TAB (isspace except space), KS_SEP_LINE (line ending '\n' or CRLF is handled by trimming trailing '\r'), or a specific byte value (> KS_SEP_MAX). If dret is non-NULL, it is set to the delimiter byte encountered. If append is non-zero, new data is appended to the existing contents of str; otherwise str is reset. Returns the number of bytes placed in str on success, -1 on EOF with no data read, -3 on stream read error. Note: This function and its types are generated by KSTREAM_INIT/KSTREAM_DECLARE macros; type_t and kstream_t are macro-defined.
requirements: ks must be a valid pointer to a kstream_t created by ks_init and not yet destroyed.
str must be a valid kstring_t; it may be zero-initialized (s==NULL,m==0,l==0) and will be grown as needed; the function may allocate or reallocate str->s.
delimiter must be one of: KS_SEP_SPACE, KS_SEP_TAB, KS_SEP_LINE, or a non-negative byte value (> KS_SEP_MAX) to search for.
If dret is non-NULL, the pointed-to int will be written with the delimiter encountered when the function stops.
On return, str->s is NUL-terminated and str->l is the string length (without the NUL).
Caller should check for return values -1 (EOF, no data) and -3 (stream error) and handle accordingly.
This function depends on a macro-provided read callback (__read) bound by KSTREAM_INIT; that must be correctly defined for the chosen type_t.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are not guaranteed; do not use the same kstream_t concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: ks_init
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a buffered streaming reader for an underlying data source f using a macro-supplied read function. Returns a new kstream_t configured with an internal buffer of implementation-defined size (as provided to KSTREAM_INIT). Note: type_t and kstream_t are generated via KSTREAM_INIT/KSTREAM_DECLARE for a specific IO backend (e.g., FILE*, gzFile).
requirements: Must be used in a translation unit where KSTREAM_INIT or KSTREAM_DECLARE has been invoked to define type_t, kstream_t, and bind the __read function.
f must be a valid handle/object of type type_t compatible with the read function (e.g., an open file/stream).
Caller is responsible for eventually calling ks_destroy on the returned kstream_t to free resources.
On allocation failure, ks_init may return NULL; caller should check for NULL before use.

functions.name: ks_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a kstream_t previously created by ks_init, freeing its internal buffer and the stream object itself. Safe to call with NULL (no effect).
requirements: ks must either be NULL or a kstream_t returned by ks_init and not previously destroyed.
After ks_destroy returns, ks must not be used again.

functions.name: ks_getc
functions.description: Gets the next byte from the buffered stream ks. Refills the buffer as needed using the macro-supplied read function. Returns the byte as an unsigned char cast to int on success, -1 on EOF, or -3 on stream error. Advances the internal seek_pos.
requirements: ks must be a valid pointer to a kstream_t created by ks_init and not yet destroyed.
Caller must handle special return values: -1 indicates EOF; -3 indicates a read error (ks_err(ks) will be true).
Do not call concurrently on the same kstream_t from multiple threads.

functions.name: ks_getuntil
functions.signature: int ks_getuntil(kstream_t *ks, int delimiter, kstring_t *str, int *dret);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper over ks_getuntil2 that reads into str until delimiter is encountered, not appending to existing contents (append=0). Follows the same behavior and return codes as ks_getuntil2. If dret is non-NULL, it receives the delimiter byte encountered.
requirements: Same as ks_getuntil2, with append behavior fixed to clear str (str->l reset to 0) before reading.
Caller must check for return values -1 (EOF, no data) and -3 (stream error) and handle accordingly.

functions.name: kseq_init
functions.description: Creates a FASTA/FASTQ parser state around an existing kstream created for an input handle fd. Internally wraps fd by constructing a kstream_t via ks_init and initializes sequence, name, comment, and quality buffers. Note: kseq_t and type_t are generated via KSEQ_INIT/KSEQ_DECLARE for a chosen IO backend.
requirements: Must be used in a translation unit where KSEQ_INIT or KSEQ_DECLARE (which also implies KSTREAM_INIT/DECLARE) has been invoked to define type_t, kstream_t, and kseq_t and to bind the read function.
fd must be a valid handle/object of type type_t appropriate for the underlying read function (e.g., an open compressed or uncompressed file).
Caller must eventually call kseq_destroy on the returned kseq_t to free resources.
On allocation failure, may return NULL; caller should check for NULL before use.

functions.name: kseq_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a kseq_t created by kseq_init, freeing its kstring_t buffers (name, comment, seq, qual), destroying the embedded kstream_t, and freeing the kseq_t itself. Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: ks must either be NULL or a kseq_t previously returned by kseq_init and not already destroyed.
After kseq_destroy returns, ks and its embedded strings become invalid and must not be used.

functions.name: kseq_read
functions.description: Reads the next record from a FASTA or FASTQ stream into seq. On success returns the sequence length (>= 0) and fills seq->name, seq->comment (optional), seq->seq, and for FASTQ also seq->qual. Handles multi-line sequences, skips empty lines, and trims CR in CRLF line endings for KS_SEP_LINE. Return codes: >=0 length; -1 end of file; -2 truncated or mismatched quality string; -3 error reading stream; -4 internal overflow when growing buffers. For FASTA (no '+' line), quality is not read and the function returns after sequence is read.
requirements: seq must be a valid pointer to a kseq_t created by kseq_init and not destroyed.
Input data must be in valid FASTA or FASTQ format. For FASTQ, the number of quality characters must equal the sequence length; otherwise -2 is returned.
Caller must check and handle negative return codes: -1 (EOF), -2 (FASTQ quality error), -3 (stream error), -4 (allocation/overflow error).
kseq_read is stateful: it maintains seq->last_char to track headers; do not interleave other reads on the underlying kstream_t without using the kseq_* API.
Do not use concurrently on the same kseq_t from multiple threads.
Buffers in seq (name, comment, seq, qual) are managed by the function and may be reallocated; any external pointers to their data may be invalidated after subsequent calls.

functions.name: knet_open
functions.description: Opens a path/URL for I/O via the legacy knet interface, returning an opaque knetFile handle. Supports local files and (historically) FTP/HTTP backends. Deprecated in favor of hopen. Typical usage mirrors fopen-style open followed by knet_read/knet_seek and knet_close. Details of supported mode strings and access types are not fully documented here.
requirements: fn must be a non-null C string naming a local file or network resource understood by this library (local/FTP/HTTP are implied by KNF_TYPE_*).
mode must be a non-null C string in fopen-like format (exact accepted values are not specified here; write support is unknown).
Caller must check the return value for NULL and handle failure.
The returned knetFile* must be closed with knet_close when no longer needed.
Function is deprecated; new code should use hopen instead.

functions.name: knet_dopen
functions.description: Wraps an existing file descriptor for I/O via the legacy knet interface. This only works with local files. Deprecated in favor of hdopen. Intended for cases where the caller already has an open OS-level file descriptor and wants a knetFile* handle for reading/seeking via knet_read/knet_seek.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open file descriptor referring to a local file (not a network socket).
mode must be a non-null C string in fopen-like format (exact accepted values are not specified here; write support is unknown).
Caller must check the return value for NULL and handle failure.
The returned knetFile* must be closed with knet_close when no longer needed.
Function is deprecated; new code should use hdopen instead.
Ownership/lifetime of the underlying fd on knet_close is not specified here; verify in implementation if double-closing must be avoided (unknown).

functions.name: knet_read
functions.description: Reads up to len bytes from the knetFile stream into buf. If the handle is not yet ready for I/O (is_ready==0), the function performs any necessary setup (e.g., connecting/positioning) before reading; otherwise it reads directly. Semantics resemble POSIX read. Deprecated in favor of hread.
requirements: fp must be a non-null knetFile* previously returned by knet_open or knet_dopen and not yet closed.
buf must be a non-null pointer to a writable memory region of at least len bytes.
len may be zero; larger values must fit in size_t.

Caller must handle the return value: a non-negative value indicates the number of bytes read; a negative value indicates an error (typical read-like semantics; exact error reporting beyond the sign is not documented here).
May be called after knet_seek to realize a lazy seek on the next read.
Function is deprecated; new code should use hread instead.

functions.name: knet_seek
functions.signature: off_t knet_seek(knetFile *fp, off_t off, int whence);
functions.description: Adjusts the logical file position for subsequent I/O on the knetFile handle. This function only updates internal offset state and marks the stream as not ready; it does not contact remote servers. The next knet_read will perform any necessary repositioning. Deprecated in favor of hseek.
requirements: fp must be a non-null knetFile* previously returned by knet_open or knet_dopen and not yet closed.
whence must be a valid seek origin constant (e.g., SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR, SEEK_END).
off must be representable in off_t for the platform; interpretation follows standard seek semantics.

Caller should check the return value to confirm the new offset or detect failure (exact error convention is not specified here; typical behavior is to return the resulting offset, with failure indicated by a negative value).
Function is deprecated; new code should use hseek instead.

functions.name: knet_close
functions.description: Closes a knetFile handle and releases associated resources. After return, the handle must not be used. Deprecated in favor of hclose.
requirements: fp must be a valid knetFile* previously returned by knet_open or knet_dopen; passing NULL is invalid (behavior not specified).
Must not be called more than once on the same handle.
Caller must check the return value for success/failure (exact success/error codes are not documented here).
Function is deprecated; new code should use hclose instead.

functions.name: hts_lib_shutdown
functions.description: Explicitly releases HTSlib global resources before a caller dlcloses the library. Use only when HTSlib was dlopened and must be cleanly unloaded before process exit.
requirements: Call only if the process intends to unload HTSlib before exit (e.g., via dlclose).
Do not use any HTSlib APIs after calling this; behavior is undefined.

functions.name: hts_free
functions.description: Wrapper around free() to safely deallocate memory across DLL boundaries when memory was allocated by HTSlib but freed by an application with a different C runtime.
requirements: ptr may be NULL (no effect).
Only pass pointers allocated/owned by HTSlib that require cross-DLL-safe free.

functions.name: hts_resize_array_
functions.signature: int hts_resize_array_(size_t, size_t, size_t, void *, void **, int, const char *);
functions.description: Internal helper used by the hts_resize macro to grow an array (optionally clearing new memory). Returns 0 on success, negative on error.
requirements: Parameters must match the macro’s expectations (element size, requested count, size storage pointer, data pointer location, flags, caller name).
Callers should prefer the hts_resize() macro; this function is intended for internal use.

functions.name: hts_opt_add
functions.description: Parses a single option string and appends it to an hts_opt linked list for later application to a file/format.
requirements: opts must be a valid pointer to an hts_opt* (may point to NULL to start a new list).
c_arg must be a non-NULL C string in key[=value] form as accepted by HTSlib.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure; caller must handle errors.
Free the list with hts_opt_free() when done.

functions.name: hts_opt_apply
functions.description: Applies an hts_opt list of options to an open htsFile (format-specific settings, compression, thread pool, reference, etc.).
requirements: fp must be a valid, open htsFile*.
opts may be NULL (no effect) or a valid list created by hts_opt_add/hts_parse_format/hts_parse_opt_list.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure; caller must check and handle errors.

functions.name: hts_opt_free
functions.description: Frees an hts_opt linked list previously created (e.g., by hts_opt_add).
requirements: opts may be NULL (no effect).
Do not use the list after freeing.

functions.name: hts_parse_format
functions.description: Parses a format string like "bam,option=value,..." into an htsFormat structure (category/format/compression/options).
requirements: opt must be a non-NULL pointer to htsFormat to receive parsed data.
str must be a non-NULL C string; accepted keys/values are HTSlib-defined.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure; caller must check the return.

functions.name: hts_parse_opt_list
functions.description: Tokenizes an option list string "key(=value)?" separated by commas and populates fields in htsFormat.
requirements: opt must be non-NULL.
str must be a non-NULL C string; values cannot contain commas (no escaping supported).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: hts_version
functions.description: Returns the HTSlib version string (e.g., "N.N[.N]" for releases or git-describe output for development builds).
requirements: Returned pointer is valid for read-only use; the caller must not free it.

functions.name: hts_features
functions.description: Returns a bitfield of HTS_FEATURE_* flags describing compile-time features of the HTSlib build.
requirements: None.

functions.name: hts_test_feature
functions.description: Returns a string describing a specific feature id from hts_features() or build parameters.
requirements: id should be a valid HTS_FEATURE_* bit or related identifier; unspecified ids may return a string but are library-defined.
Returned pointer is read-only; do not free.

functions.name: hts_feature_string
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string summarizing HTSlib build features.
requirements: Returned pointer is read-only; do not free.

functions.name: hts_detect_format
functions.description: Inspects the start of an input stream to determine its file format, filling an htsFormat structure. Equivalent to hts_detect_format2(fp, NULL, fmt).
requirements: fp must be opened for reading and positioned at the beginning.
fmt must be non-NULL to receive results.
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: hts_detect_format2
functions.signature: int hts_detect_format2(struct hFILE *fp, const char *fname, htsFormat *fmt);
functions.description: Determines file format by peeking at the stream and optionally using filename/extension to disambiguate certain formats (e.g., FASTA/Q indexes).
requirements: fp must be opened for reading and positioned at the beginning.
fmt must be non-NULL.
fname may be NULL or a filename C string; certain formats require correct extensions.
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: hts_format_description
functions.description: Returns a newly-allocated human-readable description string for the given htsFormat.
requirements: format must be non-NULL.
Return must be freed by the caller after use.

functions.name: hts_open
functions.description: Opens a sequence/variant or line-oriented file (possibly compressed) for reading, writing, or appending, inferring or specifying format via mode letters.
requirements: fn must be a valid filename or "-" for stdin/stdout; may include HTS_IDX_DELIM to specify a non-standard index name.
mode must match the documented pattern [rwa][bcefFguxz0-9]* and appropriate for intended operation.
On success returns an htsFile*; on failure returns NULL; caller must check.
Close with hts_close().

functions.name: hts_open_format
functions.signature: htsFile *hts_open_format(const char *fn, const char *mode, const htsFormat *fmt);
functions.description: Opens a file like hts_open(), with an optional htsFormat that can override mode and apply additional options.
requirements: fn and mode follow hts_open() rules.
fmt may be NULL or point to a struct containing desired overrides/options.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check and later close with hts_close() on success.

functions.name: hts_hopen
functions.signature: htsFile *hts_hopen(struct hFILE *fp, const char *fn, const char *mode);
functions.description: Wraps an existing hFILE stream as an htsFile with the specified mode and optional filename for context.
requirements: fp must be a valid, already-open hFILE* with appropriate access for mode.
fn may be a context name or "-"; may be used for auxiliary behavior.
Returns NULL on failure; close the resulting htsFile* with hts_close() (which will manage underlying stream as per library semantics).

functions.name: hts_flush
functions.description: Flushes buffered data on an output htsFile.
requirements: fp must be a valid output stream opened for writing or appending.
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: hts_close
functions.description: Closes an htsFile, flushing any buffered output and releasing resources.
requirements: fp must be a valid htsFile* previously opened by hts_open/hts_open_format/hts_hopen.
Returns 0 on success; negative on error. After return, fp is invalid.

functions.name: hts_get_format
functions.description: Returns a read-only pointer to the file’s htsFormat.
requirements: fp must be a valid, open htsFile*.
Returned pointer is owned by the htsFile; do not free; lifetime tied to fp.

functions.name: hts_format_file_extension
functions.description: Returns the canonical file extension for the given format (e.g., "sam", "bam"), or "?" if unknown.
requirements: format must be non-NULL.
Returned pointer is not owned by caller; do not free.

functions.name: hts_set_opt
functions.description: Sets a format/file-specific option (CRAM/general/FASTQ options) on an open htsFile. The varargs depend on the option.
requirements: fp must be a valid, open htsFile*.
opt must be one of enum hts_fmt_option values; the following varargs must match the type expected by that option (see option docs).
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: hts_getline
functions.description: Reads a line (terminated by '\n' or '\r\n') from fp into str, excluding the terminator.
requirements: fp must be a valid, open htsFile* positioned for reading.
delimiter must be '\n' (or KS_SEP_LINE).
str must be a valid kstring_t*; its buffer will be resized as needed.
Returns length (capped at INT_MAX), -1 on EOF, <= -2 on error.

functions.name: hts_readlines
functions.description: Reads all lines from a text file into a newly allocated array of C strings.
requirements: fn must be a valid filename.
_n must be non-NULL to receive the count.
Returns NULL on failure; on success, returns an array of malloc’d strings; caller must free each string and the array.

functions.name: hts_readlist
functions.description: Parses either a comma-separated list or reads items from a file into a new array of strings.
requirements: If is_file!=0, fn is treated as a filename to read; otherwise fn is a comma-separated list.
_n must be non-NULL to receive item count.
Returns NULL on failure; on success, caller must free the returned array and strings.

functions.name: hts_set_threads
functions.description: Creates per-handle compression/decompression worker threads for fp. Non-shared; hts_set_thread_pool is recommended instead.
requirements: fp must be a valid, open htsFile*.
n must be the number of worker threads to create (implementation-defined valid range).
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: hts_set_thread_pool
functions.description: Associates a shared thread pool (and optional queue size) with fp to aid compression/decompression.
requirements: fp must be a valid, open htsFile*.
p must point to a valid htsThreadPool with pool set; qsize may be zero to auto-select.
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: hts_set_cache_size
functions.description: Enables a cache of decompressed blocks (currently BGZF only), potentially speeding random access.
requirements: fp must be a valid htsFile*.
n is the cache size in bytes; non-negative per implementation expectations.

functions.name: hts_set_fai_filename
functions.description: Sets an associated .fai filename on a file opened for reading, to supply reference list if headers lack @SQ.
requirements: Call before reading the header (e.g., before *_hdr_read()).
fp must be a valid input htsFile*.
fn_aux must be a valid path to a .fai file.
Returns 0 on success; negative on failure.

functions.name: hts_set_filter_expression
functions.description: Sets or clears a filter expression on the file handle, affecting subsequent reads.
requirements: fp must be a valid htsFile*.
expr may be NULL to clear the filter, or a valid expression string; expression syntax is library-defined.
Returns 0 on success; negative on failure.

functions.name: hts_check_EOF
functions.description: Checks whether a file has a valid EOF marker when applicable (e.g., BGZF EOF block).
requirements: fp must be a valid htsFile*.
