Interpreting return: 3 non-EOF-checkable type; 2 unseekable so cannot check; 1 valid EOF marker; 0 missing required EOF; -1 on failure with errno set.

functions.name: hts_idx_init
functions.signature: hts_idx_t *hts_idx_init(int n, int fmt, uint64_t offset0, int min_shift, int n_lvls);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new index structure (BAI/CSI/TBI types) for building an index.
requirements: n is initial number of targets (>=0).
fmt must be one of HTS_FMT_CSI, HTS_FMT_BAI, or HTS_FMT_TBI.
offset0 is the initial file offset for the first record/container.
min_shift and n_lvls define the binning scheme; must be consistent with target format.
On success, free with hts_idx_destroy(). Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: hts_idx_destroy
functions.description: Frees an index created by hts_idx_init() or loaded via hts_idx_load*().
requirements: idx may be NULL (no effect).
Do not use idx after destroying it.

functions.name: hts_idx_push
functions.signature: int hts_idx_push(hts_idx_t *idx, int tid, hts_pos_t beg, hts_pos_t end, uint64_t offset, int is_mapped);
functions.description: Adds an index entry for a record/range and updates mapped/unmapped counts as appropriate.
requirements: idx must be a valid index created by hts_idx_init().
tid must be a valid target id for this index.
beg/end are 0-based half-open coordinates; end>=beg per data convention.
offset must be the file offset of the record/container.
is_mapped indicates mapping status to update meta-data.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.

functions.name: hts_idx_finish
functions.description: Finishes index construction, sealing structures and writing any final state.
requirements: idx must be a valid index in building state.
final_offset must be the last file offset for the dataset.
Returns 0 on success; non-zero on failure.

functions.name: hts_idx_fmt
functions.description: Returns the index format code (HTS_FMT_CSI, HTS_FMT_BAI, or HTS_FMT_TBI).
requirements: idx must be a valid index pointer.
Return value is one of the HTS_FMT_* constants.

functions.name: hts_idx_tbi_name
functions.signature: int hts_idx_tbi_name(hts_idx_t *idx, int tid, const char *name);
functions.description: Adds a target name to TBI index meta-data and returns its index in the names list.
requirements: idx must be a valid TBI index.
tid must be the target identifier.
name must be a non-NULL C string.
Returns index on success; -1 on failure.

functions.name: hts_idx_save
functions.signature: int hts_idx_save(const hts_idx_t *idx, const char *fn, int fmt);
functions.description: Saves an index to a file named by deriving the index name from the data file name (fn) and fmt.
requirements: idx must be a valid built index.
fn must be the associated data filename; the index filename will be derived (adds/substitutes .csi/.bai/.tbi).
fmt must be HTS_FMT_* index format.
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: hts_idx_save_as
functions.signature: int hts_idx_save_as(const hts_idx_t *idx, const char *fn, const char *fnidx, int fmt);
functions.description: Saves an index to a specific file path fnidx (or derives if NULL) for data file fn.
requirements: idx must be valid.
fn must be the data filename; fnidx may be NULL to derive.
fmt must be an HTS_FMT_* index format.
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: hts_idx_load
functions.description: Loads an index by deriving its filename from fn (or using HTS_IDX_DELIM), optionally downloading a remote index and saving a local copy. Equivalent to hts_idx_load3(fn, NULL, fmt, HTS_IDX_SAVE_REMOTE).
requirements: fn must be the data filename and may contain HTS_IDX_DELIM to explicitly specify index path.
fmt must be an HTS_FMT_* index format.
Returns NULL on error. Free with hts_idx_destroy() on success.

functions.name: hts_idx_load2
functions.description: Loads a specific index file fnidx for data file fn. Equivalent to hts_idx_load3(fn, fnidx, 0, 0).
requirements: fn is the data filename; fnidx is the index filename (non-NULL for this variant).
Returns NULL on error. Free with hts_idx_destroy() on success.
This function will not attempt to save index files locally.

functions.name: hts_idx_load3
functions.signature: hts_idx_t *hts_idx_load3(const char *fn, const char *fnidx, int fmt, int flags);
functions.description: Loads an index, deriving name from fn if fnidx is NULL; optional flags control behavior (HTS_IDX_SAVE_REMOTE, HTS_IDX_SILENT_FAIL).
requirements: fn must be the data filename.
If fnidx is not NULL, fmt is ignored and that path is loaded.
flags may include HTS_IDX_SAVE_REMOTE and/or HTS_IDX_SILENT_FAIL.
Returns NULL on error or per silent-fail policy. Free with hts_idx_destroy() on success.

functions.name: hts_idx_get_meta
functions.description: Returns a pointer to raw extra meta-data stored in the index (tabix .tbi/.csi), and sets its length.
requirements: idx must be valid.
l_meta must be non-NULL to receive length.
Returned pointer refers to memory owned by the index; caller must not free and must interpret content (including endianness) themselves.

functions.name: hts_idx_set_meta
functions.signature: int hts_idx_set_meta(hts_idx_t *idx, uint32_t l_meta, uint8_t *meta, int is_copy);
functions.description: Sets the extra meta-data block in the index. If is_copy!=0, data is copied; otherwise ownership of meta transfers to the index.
requirements: idx must be valid.
If is_copy==0, meta must be dynamically allocated and will be owned (and later freed) by the index.
l_meta is the byte length of meta.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure (e.g., out of memory).

functions.name: hts_idx_get_stat
functions.signature: int hts_idx_get_stat(const hts_idx_t* idx, int tid, uint64_t* mapped, uint64_t* unmapped);
functions.description: Retrieves the counts of mapped and unmapped reads for a given target from BAI/CSI indexes (not available for CRAI).
requirements: idx must be a valid BAI/CSI index (CRAI lacks this info).
tid is the target ID.
mapped and unmapped must be non-NULL output pointers.
Returns 0 on success; -1 if data not available.

functions.name: hts_idx_get_n_no_coor
functions.description: Returns the count of unplaced reads (not linked to any reference) from the index.
requirements: idx must be valid.

functions.name: hts_idx_seqnames
functions.signature: const char **hts_idx_seqnames(const hts_idx_t *idx, int *n, hts_id2name_f getid, void *hdr);
functions.description: Returns an array of pointers to target names from an index using a callback to map IDs to names. Only the array should be freed; names point into hdr.
requirements: idx must be valid.
n must be non-NULL to receive the count.
getid must be a valid callback that maps (hdr, id) to name strings.
hdr must be valid per callback.
On success, caller must free only the returned array; not the individual strings. Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: hts_idx_nseq
functions.description: Returns the number of targets (sequences) described by the index.
requirements: idx must be valid.

functions.name: hts_parse_decimal
functions.signature: long long hts_parse_decimal(const char *str, char **strend, int flags);
functions.description: Parses a numeric string (supports thousands separators, decimal point, k/M/G suffixes, and scientific notation) according to flags.
requirements: str must be non-NULL.
If strend is non-NULL, it will be set to the first unused character (or str if parsing failed).
flags is an OR of HTS_PARSE_THOUSANDS_SEP and/or HTS_PARSE_LIST; semantics as documented.
Returns parsed value or 0 if no valid number; may warn if strend is NULL and extra characters remain.

functions.name: hts_parse_reg64
functions.description: Compatibility helper for parsing "CHR:START-END" region strings into 0-based beg and 1-based end using 64-bit positions. Returns pointer to colon or string end after reference name.
requirements: str must be non-NULL; must contain a region-like token.
beg and end must be non-NULL.
Returns NULL if parsing fails.

functions.name: hts_parse_reg
functions.description: Parses a "CHR:START-END" region into int beg (0-based) and end (1-based). Returns pointer to colon or string end after reference name.
requirements: str must be non-NULL.
beg and end must be non-NULL.
Returns NULL on parse failure.

functions.name: hts_parse_region
functions.signature: const char *hts_parse_region(const char *s, int *tid, hts_pos_t *beg, hts_pos_t *end, hts_name2id_f getid, void *hdr, int flags);
functions.description: Parses a possibly complex region string (supports braces, lists, comma rules, and one-coordinate modes) with reference-ID validation via callback.
requirements: s must be non-NULL.
tid may be NULL; if non-NULL, it will be set to reference index or error codes (-2, -1, or >=0 as documented on failure).
beg and end must be non-NULL (0-based beg, 1-based end).
getid may be NULL (less validation) or a valid callback; hdr is user data for getid.
flags is a bitmask of HTS_PARSE_* (THOUSANDS_SEP, LIST, ONE_COORD).
Returns pointer to the byte after the region (including any trailing comma) on success, or NULL on failure.

functions.name: hts_itr_query
functions.signature: hts_itr_t *hts_itr_query(const hts_idx_t *idx, int tid, hts_pos_t beg, hts_pos_t end, hts_readrec_func *readrec);
functions.description: Creates an iterator over records in a single region [beg,end) for a given target using a provided record-reading callback.
requirements: idx must be a valid index for the opened file.
tid must be a valid target id.
beg/end specify the query interval; end is exclusive.
readrec must be a valid callback compatible with the file type.
On success, free with hts_itr_destroy(); returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: hts_itr_destroy
functions.description: Frees an iterator created by hts_itr_query/hts_itr_querys/hts_itr_regions.
requirements: iter may be NULL (no effect).
Do not use iter after destroying.

functions.name: hts_itr_querys
functions.signature: hts_itr_t *hts_itr_querys(const hts_idx_t *idx, const char *reg, hts_name2id_f getid, void *hdr, hts_itr_query_func *itr_query, hts_readrec_func *readrec);
functions.description: Creates a single-region iterator from a textual region specification by resolving name to id and delegating to a type-specific iterator factory.
requirements: idx must be valid.
reg must be a non-NULL region string.
getid must be a valid callback to map name to id; hdr is its user data.
itr_query must be a valid type-specific function returning an iterator for numeric tid/beg/end.
readrec must be a valid file-specific read function.
Returns NULL on error; free with hts_itr_destroy() on success.

functions.name: hts_itr_next
functions.description: Fetches the next record within the iterator’s regions using the given BGZF stream and read callback context.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* corresponding to the opened file stream used with this iterator (per file-type wrappers).
iter must be a valid iterator created by the hts iterator APIs.
r must point to a record holder appropriate for the readrec callback.
data is user data passed to readrec and may be NULL per callback needs.
Returns >=0 on success; -1 when iteration is complete; < -1 on error.

functions.name: hts_itr_multi_bam
functions.description: Filetype-specific initializer used by multi-region iterators for BAM.
requirements: idx must be a valid BAM index.
iter must be an allocated iterator being configured for multi-region use.
Returns int status (0 on success implied by convention; header does not state).

functions.name: hts_itr_multi_cram
functions.description: Filetype-specific initializer used by multi-region iterators for CRAM.
requirements: idx must be a valid CRAM index.
iter must be an allocated iterator being configured for multi-region use.
Returns int status (0 on success implied by convention; header does not state).

functions.name: hts_itr_regions
functions.signature: hts_itr_t *hts_itr_regions(const hts_idx_t *idx, hts_reglist_t *reglist, int count, hts_name2id_f getid, void *hdr, hts_itr_multi_query_func *itr_specific, hts_readrec_func *readrec, hts_seek_func *seek, hts_tell_func *tell);
functions.description: Creates a multi-region iterator over many regions using type-specific configuration and I/O callbacks.
requirements: idx must be valid.
reglist must point to count hts_reglist_t entries; each entry must be initialized.
getid must map names to ids; hdr is its user data.
itr_specific must be a valid function (e.g., hts_itr_multi_bam or hts_itr_multi_cram).
readrec/seek/tell must be valid callbacks for the file type/stream.
Returns NULL on failure; free with hts_itr_destroy() on success.

functions.name: hts_itr_multi_next
functions.description: Returns the next record from a multi-region iterator using the given htsFile.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open htsFile* compatible with iter.
iter must be a valid multi-region iterator.
r must point to a record holder of the correct type.
Returns >=0 on success, -1 on end, < -1 on error.

functions.name: hts_reglist_create
functions.signature: hts_reglist_t *hts_reglist_create(char **argv, int argc, int *r_count, void *hdr,  hts_name2id_f getid);
functions.description: Builds a region list from an array of region strings (e.g., chr1:2500-3600, chr2) using a header and name-to-id callback.
requirements: argv must point to argc C strings describing regions.
argc must match the number of items in argv.
r_count must be non-NULL to receive the number of items in the resulting list.
hdr and getid must be valid for mapping names to ids.
Returns NULL on failure; free result with hts_reglist_free() on success.

functions.name: hts_reglist_free
functions.description: Frees a region list created by hts_reglist_create().
requirements: reglist may be NULL (no effect).
count must match the number of items allocated for proper cleanup.

functions.name: hts_file_type
functions.description: Deprecated convenience function that guesses a file type; superseded by hts_detect_format().
requirements: fname must be a non-NULL filename string.
Returns FT_* bitmask; use hts_detect_format() instead for new code.

functions.name: errmod_init
functions.description: Initializes the revised MAQ error model context with a dependency-correlation parameter.
requirements: depcorr must be a valid double per model expectations.
Returns NULL on failure; free with errmod_destroy() on success.

functions.name: errmod_destroy
functions.description: Destroys an error model context created by errmod_init().
requirements: em may be NULL (no effect).

functions.name: errmod_cal
functions.signature: int errmod_cal(const errmod_t *em, int n, int m, uint16_t *bases, float *q);
functions.description: Computes phred-scaled likelihoods q[i*m+j] for observed bases using the revised MAQ error model.
requirements: em must be a valid context from errmod_init().
n is number of bases; m is maximum base (dimensions for q).
bases must point to n entries encoded as qual:6, strand:1, base:4 per comment.
q must point to an output array sized at least n*m floats.
Returns int status (exact success value not specified in header).

functions.name: probaln_glocal
functions.signature: int probaln_glocal(const uint8_t *ref, int l_ref, const uint8_t *query, int l_query, const uint8_t *iqual, const probaln_par_t *c, int *state, uint8_t *q);
functions.description: Performs probabilistic banded glocal alignment between ref and query sequences, producing per-base alignment state and posterior error probabilities.
requirements: ref must point to l_ref bases encoded 0:A,1:C,2:G,3:T,4:N.
query must point to l_query similarly encoded bases.
iqual must point to l_query base qualities.
c must be a valid pointer to alignment parameters (d,e,bw).
state and q must be output arrays of length l_query (state int, q uint8_t).
Returns a phred-scaled likelihood score, or INT_MIN on failure; errno set to EINVAL for invalid lengths or ENOMEM on allocation failure.

functions.name: hts_md5_init
functions.description: Allocates and initializes an MD5 context for incremental hashing.
requirements: Returns NULL on allocation failure; free with hts_md5_destroy() when finished.

functions.name: hts_md5_update
functions.signature: void hts_md5_update(hts_md5_context *ctx, const void *data, unsigned long size);
functions.description: Updates the MD5 context with size bytes from data.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer from hts_md5_init().
data may be NULL only if size==0 (by conventional semantics).

functions.name: hts_md5_final
functions.description: Finalizes the MD5 computation, writing the 16-byte digest to digest.
requirements: digest must point to at least 16 bytes of writable memory.
ctx must be a valid MD5 context; after final, context can be reset or destroyed.

functions.name: hts_md5_reset
functions.description: Resets an MD5 context back to its initial state.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context pointer from hts_md5_init().

functions.name: hts_md5_hex
functions.description: Converts a 16-byte MD5 digest into a 33-byte null-terminated lowercase hexadecimal string.
requirements: hex must point to a writable buffer of at least 33 bytes.
digest must point to a 16-byte MD5 digest.

functions.name: hts_md5_destroy
functions.description: Deallocates resources associated with an MD5 context.
requirements: ctx may be NULL (no effect).
Do not use ctx after destroying.

functions.name: hts_crc32
functions.signature: uint32_t hts_crc32(uint32_t crc, const void *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Computes CRC-32 over buf[0..len-1] starting from initial crc (from zlib or libdeflate implementation exposed by HTSlib).
requirements: buf may be NULL only if len==0 (typical constraint).
Pass 0 or a previous CRC as crc for rolling computation.

functions.name: hopen
functions.signature: HTSLIB_EXPORT hFILE *hopen(const char *filename, const char *mode, ...) HTS_RESULT_USED;
functions.description: Opens a file path or URL as a buffered hFILE stream. Supports fopen-like mode letters (r/w/a and optional +, e, x). If mode contains ':', scheme-specific variable arguments may follow in the varargs depending on the URL/file scheme. Returns an hFILE* on success or NULL with errno set on failure.
requirements: filename must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated path or URL
mode must be a valid fopen-style mode string; may include '+', 'e', 'x', and ':' for scheme-specific options
If ':' is present in mode, additional varargs may be required and are scheme-specific (details unknown)
Caller must check for NULL return and examine errno on failure

functions.name: hdopen
functions.signature: HTSLIB_EXPORT hFILE *hdopen(int fd, const char *mode) HTS_RESULT_USED;
functions.description: Wraps an existing open file (or socket) descriptor as a buffered hFILE stream. By default takes ownership and closes fd on hclose(); include 'S' in mode to keep fd open. On Windows sockets, include 's' in mode. Returns hFILE* or NULL with errno set.
requirements: fd must refer to a valid open descriptor
The underlying file must be opened in binary mode on platforms where text/binary differ
Include 'S' in mode to prevent hclose() from closing fd (shared descriptor)
On Windows, include 's' in mode when wrapping a socket descriptor
mode must be a valid mode string compatible with the access intended (read/write)
Caller must check for NULL return and errno on failure

functions.name: hisremote
functions.description: Reports whether a filename or URL refers to remote storage (e.g., requires network access). Returns 1 if remote, 0 if local.
requirements: filename must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated path or URL

functions.name: haddextension
functions.signature: HTSLIB_EXPORT char *haddextension(struct kstring_t *buffer, const char *filename, int replace, const char *extension) HTS_RESULT_USED;
functions.description: Appends an extension to a filename or replaces the existing extension if replace is non-zero. For URLs, alters the hier-part only, leaving any ?query or #fragment intact. Writes the result into buffer (a kstring) and returns buffer->s or NULL on error.
requirements: buffer must be a valid pointer to a kstring_t to receive the modified name
filename must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string
extension should be a valid extension string (e.g., ".csi"); may not be NULL (unknown behavior if NULL)
If replace is non-zero, one existing extension (if any) is removed before appending
Caller must check for NULL return value

functions.name: hclose
functions.description: Flushes (for output streams) and closes an hFILE stream, releasing associated resources. Returns 0 on success, or EOF with errno set on error.
requirements: fp must be a valid hFILE pointer previously returned by hopen/hdopen (and not already closed)
Caller must check the return value and errno on failure

functions.name: hclose_abruptly
functions.description: Closes an hFILE stream without flushing or propagating errors. Intended for cleanup after an error. Preserves errno.
requirements: fp must be a valid hFILE pointer; use only for cleanup after an error condition
Do not expect buffered output to be flushed

functions.name: herrno
functions.description: Returns the stream’s error indicator (non-zero errno value) if an error has occurred on the hFILE. Provided instead of a boolean ferror-style call due to name collision with networking herror(3).
requirements: fp must be a valid hFILE pointer

functions.name: hclearerr
functions.description: Clears the stream’s error indicator for the given hFILE.
requirements: fp must be a valid hFILE pointer

functions.name: hseek
functions.signature: HTSLIB_EXPORT off_t hseek(hFILE *fp, off_t offset, int whence) HTS_RESULT_USED;
functions.description: Repositions the stream offset similar to lseek(2). Returns the resulting offset on success, or a negative value on error.
requirements: fp must be a valid hFILE pointer associated with a seekable stream (non-seekable streams will cause an error)
whence must be a valid lseek(2) origin (e.g., SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR, SEEK_END)
offset value must be appropriate for the chosen whence and within representable range for off_t
Caller must check for negative return indicating error

functions.name: htell
functions.description: Reports the current logical stream offset from the start (0-based) of the hFILE.
requirements: fp must be a valid hFILE pointer

functions.name: hgetc
functions.description: Reads one byte from the stream and returns it as an unsigned char cast to int, or EOF on end-of-file or error.
requirements: fp must be a valid hFILE pointer opened for reading
Caller must handle EOF or error (EOF return value)

functions.name: hgetdelim
functions.signature: HTSLIB_EXPORT ssize_t hgetdelim(char *buffer, size_t size, int delim, hFILE *fp) HTS_RESULT_USED;
functions.description: Reads from the stream into buffer up to and including the specified delimiter, until EOF, or until size-1 bytes have been written. NUL-terminates the result. Returns the number of bytes read, or negative on error.
requirements: buffer must point to a writable memory region of at least size bytes
size should be > 0; to be useful, size should be >= 2 if any data and terminator are expected
delim is interpreted as an unsigned char
fp must be a valid hFILE pointer opened for reading
Caller must check for negative return for errors

functions.name: hgetln
functions.signature: static inline ssize_t HTS_RESULT_USED hgetln(char *buffer, size_t size, hFILE *fp);
functions.description: Specialization of hgetdelim() that reads a line terminated by '\n'. Writes up to size-1 bytes plus a NUL terminator. Returns bytes read, or negative on error.
requirements: buffer must point to writable memory of at least size bytes
size should be > 0; per note, > 1 to be useful
fp must be a valid hFILE pointer opened for reading
Caller must check for negative return for errors

functions.name: hgets
functions.signature: HTSLIB_EXPORT char *hgets(char *buffer, int size, hFILE *fp) HTS_RESULT_USED;
functions.description: Reads a line (newline-terminated) from the stream into buffer, like fgets(3). NUL-terminates the buffer. Returns buffer on success or NULL on error.
requirements: buffer must point to writable memory of at least size bytes
size must be a positive integer; documented as must be > 1 to be useful
fp must be a valid hFILE pointer opened for reading
Caller must check for NULL return on error

functions.name: hpeek
functions.signature: HTSLIB_EXPORT ssize_t hpeek(hFILE *fp, void *buffer, size_t nbytes) HTS_RESULT_USED;
functions.description: Peeks up to nbytes from the stream without consuming them, limited by the internal buffer size. Returns the number of bytes made available (possibly less than nbytes at EOF), or negative on I/O error. The data remains available for subsequent reads.
requirements: fp must be a valid hFILE pointer opened for reading
buffer must point to writable memory of at least nbytes bytes
nbytes is limited by the internal buffer size (could be as small as ~4 KiB)
Caller must check for negative return for errors

functions.name: hread
functions.signature: static inline ssize_t HTS_RESULT_USED hread(hFILE *fp, void *buffer, size_t nbytes);
functions.description: Reads up to nbytes from the stream into buffer. Returns the number of bytes read, or negative on error. Attempts to satisfy the full request unless limited by EOF or I/O errors.
requirements: fp must be a valid hFILE pointer opened for reading
buffer must point to writable memory of at least nbytes bytes
Caller must handle short reads at EOF and check for negative return on error

functions.name: hputc
functions.signature: static inline int hputc(int c, hFILE *fp);
functions.description: Writes a single byte (the low 8 bits of c) to the stream. Returns the character written, or EOF on error.
requirements: fp must be a valid hFILE pointer opened for writing
Caller must check for EOF return indicating error

functions.name: hputs
functions.signature: static inline int hputs(const char *text, hFILE *fp);
functions.description: Writes a NUL-terminated string to the stream. Returns 0 on success, or EOF on error.
requirements: text must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string
fp must be a valid hFILE pointer opened for writing
Caller must check for EOF return indicating error

functions.name: hwrite
functions.signature: static inline ssize_t HTS_RESULT_USED hwrite(hFILE *fp, const void *buffer, size_t nbytes);
functions.description: Writes nbytes from buffer to the stream. In the absence of I/O errors, the full nbytes will be written. Returns nbytes on success or a negative value on error.
requirements: fp must be a valid hFILE pointer opened for writing
buffer must point to readable memory containing at least nbytes bytes
Caller must check for negative return indicating error

functions.name: hflush
functions.description: Flushes buffered output for a writing stream to the underlying storage, including low-level flush (e.g., fdatasync). Returns 0 on success or EOF on error.
requirements: fp must be a valid hFILE pointer; meaningful for streams opened for writing
Caller must check the return value and errno on failure

functions.name: hfile_mem_get_buffer
functions.description: For hfile_mem-backed streams, returns a pointer to the internal memory buffer and optionally its length via the output parameter. The buffer is owned by the hFILE and must not be freed by the caller. The buffer will be freed when the hFILE is closed.
requirements: file must be a valid hFILE pointer using the hfile_mem backend (otherwise NULL may be returned)
length should point to a size_t for receiving the buffer size (unknown if NULL is permitted)
Caller must not free or modify the returned buffer memory directly
Caller must check for NULL return indicating failure

functions.name: hfile_mem_steal_buffer
functions.description: For hfile_mem-backed streams, transfers ownership of the internal buffer to the caller and returns it, with length optionally set. After calling, the hFILE should not be used for any purpose other than closing. The caller becomes responsible for freeing the buffer.
requirements: file must be a valid hFILE pointer using the hfile_mem backend
After successful call, the caller must free the returned buffer
After this call, the hFILE must not be used except to close it
length should point to a size_t to receive the buffer size (unknown if NULL is permitted)
Caller must check for NULL return indicating failure

functions.name: hfile_list_schemes
functions.signature: HTSLIB_EXPORT int hfile_list_schemes(const char *plugin, const char *sc_list[], int *nschemes);
functions.description: Fills sc_list with the names of known URL schemes, optionally restricted to a specific plugin. On input, *nschemes is the capacity of sc_list; on output, *nschemes is set to the number of entries written. Returns the total number of matching schemes (which may exceed the capacity), or -1 on failure.
requirements: sc_list must point to an array of at least *nschemes pointers to char, allocated by the caller
nschemes must be a valid pointer; its input value supplies capacity, and it will be updated with the number returned in sc_list
plugin may be NULL to list all schemes; use the literal string "built-in" to restrict to built-in schemes
Caller must handle the case where return value > *nschemes (insufficient capacity)
Caller must check for -1 return indicating failure

functions.name: hfile_list_plugins
functions.description: Fills plist with the names of known hFILE plugins. On input, *nplugins is the capacity of plist; on output, *nplugins is set to the number of entries written. Returns the total number of plugins (which may exceed capacity), or -1 on failure.
requirements: plist must point to an array of at least *nplugins pointers to char, allocated by the caller
nplugins must be a valid pointer; its input value supplies capacity, and it will be updated with the number returned in plist
Caller must handle the case where return value > *nplugins (insufficient capacity)
Caller must check for -1 return indicating failure

functions.name: hfile_has_plugin
functions.description: Tests whether a specific hFILE plugin is available. Returns 1 if found, 0 otherwise.
requirements: name must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated plugin name string

functions.name: bgzf_dopen
functions.description: Opens an existing file descriptor as a BGZF/GZIP/uncompressed stream for reading, writing, or appending based on the mode string. Use to wrap an already-opened (binary) file descriptor in a BGZF handle.
requirements: fd must refer to a valid, open file descriptor; the underlying file must be opened in binary mode on platforms where text/binary differ.

mode must match /[rwag][u0-9]+/: 'r' read, 'w' write, 'a' append, optional 'g' with 'w' for gzip compression, optional digit 0–9 for zlib compression level, optional 'u' for uncompressed output (distinct from '0' which is zlib-wrapped uncompressed).
On error returns NULL; caller must check for NULL before use.
When writing with 'g' mode, stream is gzip, not BGZF.

functions.name: bgzf_fdopen
functions.description: Backward-compatible alias of bgzf_dopen to open an existing file descriptor as a BGZF handle. Function-like macro that forwards to bgzf_dopen with the same parameters and behavior.
requirements: This is a macro mapping to bgzf_dopen((fd), (mode)); all requirements of bgzf_dopen apply.
fd must be a valid, open descriptor (binary mode on relevant platforms).
mode must match /[rwag][u0-9]+/ as for bgzf_dopen.
Caller must handle NULL on failure.

functions.name: bgzf_open
functions.description: Opens a file at path as a BGZF/GZIP/uncompressed stream according to the mode string for reading, writing, or appending.
requirements: path must point to a valid file path accessible to the process.
mode must match /[rwag][u0-9]+/ with the same semantics as bgzf_dopen.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check before use.
For correct behavior on Windows or text/binary-differing platforms, files should be opened in binary mode per the library's handling.

functions.name: bgzf_hopen
functions.description: Wraps an existing hFILE stream as a BGZF/GZIP/uncompressed stream for reading or writing according to mode.
requirements: fp must be a valid, initialized hFILE* opened in a compatible mode (read/write) with the intended use.
mode must match /[rwag][u0-9]+/ with the same semantics as bgzf_dopen.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check before use.

functions.name: bgzf_close
functions.description: Closes a BGZF stream and frees all associated resources. Flushes any pending output if open for writing.
requirements: fp must be a BGZF* obtained from bgzf_open/bgzf_dopen/bgzf_hopen (or compatible) and not already closed.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; caller should check return and handle errors (e.g., I/O failure on flush).
After success (and also on failure), fp must not be used again.

functions.name: bgzf_read
functions.description: Reads up to length bytes of uncompressed data from a BGZF/GZIP/uncompressed stream into data. Standard blocking read semantics.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* opened for reading.
data must point to a writable buffer of at least length bytes.
Returns number of bytes read; 0 on EOF; -1 on error. Caller must distinguish these cases.
Subsequent calls continue from the next position unless repositioned by bgzf_seek/bgzf_useek.

functions.name: bgzf_read_small
functions.signature: static inline ssize_t bgzf_read_small(BGZF *fp, void *data, size_t length);
functions.description: Optimized inline helper for small reads: copies directly from the current decompressed block when possible, otherwise falls back to bgzf_read. Intended to reduce overhead for small read lengths.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* opened for reading.
data must point to a writable buffer of at least length bytes.
On fast-path, relies on the current block being loaded and having sufficient remaining bytes; otherwise calls bgzf_read with identical semantics.
Return values match bgzf_read: bytes read, 0 on EOF, -1 on error.

functions.name: bgzf_write
functions.signature: ssize_t bgzf_write(BGZF *fp, const void *data, size_t length);
functions.description: Writes length bytes of data to the BGZF/GZIP/uncompressed stream. If no I/O errors occur, the entire length is written or queued for writing.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* opened for writing or appending as appropriate.
data must point to a readable buffer of at least length bytes.
Returns number of bytes written (expected to be length); negative on error. Caller must check for negative values.
Caller should bgzf_flush or bgzf_close to ensure data is physically written.

functions.name: bgzf_write_small
functions.signature: static inline ssize_t bgzf_write_small(BGZF *fp, const void *data, size_t length);
functions.description: Optimized inline helper for small writes: copies directly into the current uncompressed block buffer when space permits; otherwise defers to bgzf_write.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* opened for writing.
data must point to a readable buffer of at least length bytes.
Fast-path only applies when fp->is_compressed is true and remaining space in the block exceeds length; otherwise behavior is that of bgzf_write.
Return values match bgzf_write: length on success; negative on error.

functions.name: bgzf_block_write
functions.signature: ssize_t bgzf_block_write(BGZF *fp, const void *data, size_t length);
functions.description: Writes length bytes using the active BGZF index to determine uncompressed block boundaries. Ensures written data aligns with index-defined BGZF blocks when present.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* opened for writing.
data must point to a readable buffer of at least length bytes.
Returns number of bytes written (i.e., length) on success; negative on error. Caller must check for negative values.
Intended for use when an index is present/being built; general callers may prefer bgzf_write.

functions.name: bgzf_peek
functions.description: Returns the next byte in the stream without consuming it. Useful for lookahead while parsing.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* opened for reading.
Return values: -1 on EOF; -2 on error; otherwise the next byte as an unsigned value 0–255. Caller must handle these cases appropriately.

functions.name: bgzf_raw_read
functions.description: Reads up to length raw bytes directly from the underlying stream without decompression, bypassing BGZF block handling. For specialized use only.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* opened for reading.
data must point to a writable buffer of at least length bytes.
Bypasses BGZF blocking; caller must ensure this does not corrupt higher-level BGZF state in their use-case.
Returns number of bytes read; 0 on EOF; -1 on error.

functions.name: bgzf_raw_write
functions.signature: ssize_t bgzf_raw_write(BGZF *fp, const void *data, size_t length);
functions.description: Writes length raw bytes directly to the underlying stream without compression or BGZF framing. For specialized use only.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* opened for writing.
data must point to a readable buffer of at least length bytes.
Bypasses BGZF blocking; caller must ensure correctness for their use-case.
Returns number of bytes written; -1 on error.

functions.name: bgzf_flush
functions.description: Flushes any buffered output data to the underlying stream.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* opened for writing.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on error. Caller should check and handle flush failures (e.g., disk full).

functions.name: bgzf_seek
functions.signature: int64_t bgzf_seek(BGZF *fp, int64_t pos, int whence);
functions.description: Seeks to the specified virtual file offset within a BGZF stream for reading. The position should be a value previously returned by bgzf_tell.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* opened for reading (seeking is not permitted on files open for writing).
fp must not be a gzip-compressed stream (seeking not permitted on gzip as opposed to bgzip).
pos must be a virtual offset obtained from bgzf_tell.
whence must be SEEK_SET.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on error (with HTS_RESULT_USED semantics). Caller must check for negative result.

functions.name: bgzf_check_EOF
functions.description: Checks for the presence and correctness of the BGZF end-of-file marker in a file opened for reading.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* opened for reading.
Return values: 1 if EOF marker present and correct; 2 if it cannot be checked (e.g., stream not seekable); 0 if absent; -1 on error (errno set). Caller must handle these cases accordingly.

functions.name: bgzf_compression
functions.description: Returns the compression format of the stream: 0 no_compression, 1 gzip, 2 bgzf (matches enum htsCompression values).
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF*.
Caller should interpret returned small integer per enum htsCompression (0=no_compression, 1=gzip, 2=bgzf).

functions.name: bgzf_is_bgzf
functions.description: Deprecated helper that tests if the named file is BGZF. Returns 1 if BGZF; 0 if not or on I/O error. Prefer bgzf_compression() or hts_detect_format().
requirements: fn must be a valid path string to a readable file.
Caller must handle return 0 for both non-BGZF and I/O error conditions.
Deprecated: callers should migrate to bgzf_compression() or hts_detect_format().

functions.name: bgzf_set_cache_size
functions.description: Sets the internal BGZF read cache size in bytes. Only effective when the library was compiled with -DBGZF_CACHE; otherwise a no-op.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF*.
size is the desired cache size in bytes; 0 disables caching (default).
Has effect only when compiled with BGZF cache support.

functions.name: bgzf_flush_try
functions.description: Flushes the file if the remaining buffer space is smaller than size; otherwise does nothing.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* opened for writing.
size specifies a threshold; if remaining buffer < size, a flush is attempted.
Returns 0 if flushing succeeded or was not needed; negative on error. Caller must check for negative values.

functions.name: bgzf_getc
functions.description: Reads a single byte from a BGZF stream. Faster than bgzf_read for single-byte access.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* opened for reading.
Returns the byte (0–255) on success; -1 on EOF; <= -2 on error. Caller must handle these cases.

functions.name: bgzf_getline
functions.signature: int bgzf_getline(BGZF *fp, int delim, struct kstring_t *str);
functions.description: Reads a line delimited by delim from a BGZF stream into the provided kstring buffer. Faster than repeated bgzf_getc.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* opened for reading.
str must be initialized (valid kstring_t) before calling; function writes the line into it.
delim is the delimiter character to stop at.
Returns length of the string (capped at INT_MAX); -1 on EOF; <= -2 on error. Caller must handle these cases.

functions.name: bgzf_read_block
functions.description: Reads the next BGZF block from the underlying stream into internal buffers. Intended for advanced/low-level use.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF*; typically opened for reading.
Returns non-negative on success as per implementation; negative on error (HTS_RESULT_USED). Exact success return value semantics are not documented here.

functions.name: bgzf_thread_pool
functions.signature: int bgzf_thread_pool(BGZF *fp, struct hts_tpool *pool, int qsize);
functions.description: Enables multi-threaded BGZF encode/decode using a shared thread pool, allowing both encoder and decoder to share worker jobs. Balances usage across the pool.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF*.
pool must point to a valid hts_tpool created by hts_create_threads (or equivalent).
qsize is the job queue size; if 0, it defaults to twice the number of threads in the pool.
Returns an int status (0 on success per typical HTSlib conventions; check library docs/source for exact semantics). Caller must check and handle non-zero as error.

functions.name: bgzf_mt
functions.signature: int bgzf_mt(BGZF *fp, int n_threads, int n_sub_blks);
functions.description: Enables multi-threading for BGZF I/O using an internal pool. n_sub_blks is unused (historically number of blocks per thread).
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF*.
n_threads is the number of threads to use for reading/writing; acceptable ranges are not specified here.
n_sub_blks is unused by current implementations.
Returns int status; caller must check non-zero for errors.

functions.name: bgzf_compress
functions.signature: int bgzf_compress(void *dst, size_t *dlen, const void *src, size_t slen, int level);
functions.description: Compresses a single BGZF block from src into dst using the specified compression level. On return, *dlen is updated to the number of bytes written to dst.
requirements: dst must point to an output buffer of size >= BGZF_MAX_BLOCK_SIZE.
dlen must be a non-NULL pointer to the size of dst on input; on success it is updated to the actual number of bytes written.
src must point to the input data to compress.
slen must be <= BGZF_BLOCK_SIZE.
level is the zlib compression level to use (typical range 0–9).
Returns 0 on success; negative on error. Caller must check for negative values.

functions.name: bgzf_useek
functions.signature: int bgzf_useek(BGZF *fp, off_t uoffset, int where);
functions.description: Seeks to the given uncompressed data offset within a BGZF stream opened for reading.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* opened for reading.
uoffset is the desired offset in the uncompressed data.
where must be SEEK_SET.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on error (HTS_RESULT_USED).
It is not permitted to seek on files open for writing or on gzip-compressed files (as opposed to bgzip).

functions.name: bgzf_utell
functions.description: Returns the current uncompressed data offset position for a BGZF stream opened for reading.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF*; typically opened for reading.
Returns current offset on success; -1 on error. Caller must check for -1.

functions.name: bgzf_index_build_init
functions.description: Enables on-the-fly index building for a BGZF stream. Must be called before any I/O on the handle and before enabling multi-threading with bgzf_mt.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* opened for reading or writing.
Must be called before any data has been read or written on fp.
Must be called before bgzf_mt() on the same handle (threads may start before index is set up).
Returns 0 on success; -1 on error. Caller must check return value.

functions.signature: int bgzf_index_load(BGZF *fp, const char *bname, const char *suffix);

requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF*.
idx must be a valid, readable hFILE* positioned at the start of the index data when called.

Returns 0 on success; -1 on error (HTS_RESULT_USED). Caller must check for -1.

Returns 0 on success; -1 on error (HTS_RESULT_USED). Caller must check for -1.

functions.name: hts_tpool_init
functions.description: Create a thread pool with n worker threads. Returns a pointer to an opaque hts_tpool on success, or NULL on failure. The returned pool must later be freed with hts_tpool_destroy() when no longer needed.
requirements: n is the requested number of worker threads; valid ranges are not specified.
On success, the returned hts_tpool* must be eventually freed via hts_tpool_destroy().
Do not pass the returned pointer to other hts_tpool_* functions after it has been destroyed.

functions.name: hts_tpool_size
functions.description: Return the number of requested threads for a pool p.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer to a pool (e.g., returned by hts_tpool_init).
Behavior is undefined/unknown if p is NULL or already destroyed (not specified).

functions.name: hts_tpool_worker_id
functions.description: Return the worker ID index for the calling thread within the pool (0..nthreads-1), or -1 if not found.
requirements: pool must be a valid pointer to a pool (e.g., returned by hts_tpool_init).
The function returns -1 if the calling thread is not a worker in the pool.

functions.name: hts_tpool_dispatch
functions.description: Enqueue a job for execution in pool p for process queue q. The job entry point is func(arg). Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure. Results (if any) are queued on q for later retrieval in strict order.
requirements: p must be a valid pool and q a process queue associated with that pool.
func must be a valid function pointer taking void* and returning void*.
If results are produced, retrieve them through the result APIs for q; exact semantics depend on q’s configuration (in_only).
Do not call after q or p have been destroyed.

functions.name: hts_tpool_dispatch2
functions.signature: int hts_tpool_dispatch2(hts_tpool *p, hts_tpool_process *q, void *(*func)(void *arg), void *arg, int nonblock);
functions.description: Enqueue a job as with hts_tpool_dispatch, but with nonblocking control over the input queue. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure. If nonblock is +1 and the queue is full, returns -1 and sets errno to EAGAIN. If nonblock is -1, the task is added even if the queue is full (over-size).
requirements: p must be a valid pool and q a process queue associated with that pool.
func must be a valid function pointer taking void* and returning void*.
nonblock controls behavior: 0=block if full; +1=nonblocking (fail with -1, errno=EAGAIN if full); -1=force enqueue even if full.
Do not call after q or p have been destroyed.

functions.name: hts_tpool_dispatch3
functions.signature: int hts_tpool_dispatch3(hts_tpool *p, hts_tpool_process *q, void *(*exec_func)(void *arg), void *arg, void (*job_cleanup)(void *arg), void (*result_cleanup)(void *data), int nonblock);
functions.description: Enqueue a job with nonblocking control and optional cleanup callbacks. exec_func(arg) is the job. job_cleanup() and result_cleanup() are invoked only when discarding jobs/results (e.g., during hts_tpool_process_reset() or hts_tpool_process_destroy()). Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure. With nonblock=+1 and full queue, returns -1 and sets errno=EAGAIN; with nonblock=-1, enqueues even if full.
requirements: p must be a valid pool and q a process queue associated with that pool.
exec_func must be a valid function pointer taking void* and returning void*.
nonblock: 0=block if full; +1=nonblocking (fail with -1, errno=EAGAIN if full); -1=force enqueue even if full.
job_cleanup, if not NULL, must tolerate being called with the original job arg for each discarded pending job.
result_cleanup, if not NULL, must tolerate being called with the data pointer that would be returned by hts_tpool_result_data() for discarded results.
Cleanup callbacks are only called when jobs/results are discarded, not for normal execution.
Do not call after q or p have been destroyed.

functions.name: hts_tpool_wake_dispatch
functions.description: Wake a single thread blocked in dispatch on process queue q so that it returns with errno set to EAGAIN.
requirements: q must be a valid process queue.
Intended to interrupt a blocking dispatch; the woken dispatch call will return with errno=EAGAIN.

functions.name: hts_tpool_process_flush
functions.description: Flush a process queue q: drain its jobs and ensure all worker threads have finished their current tasks for this process. Does not stop workers from executing jobs for other processes. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: q must be a valid process queue associated with a pool.
Only affects tasks associated with q.

functions.name: hts_tpool_process_reset
functions.description: Reset process q to its initial state: remove queued input jobs, disable result notifications, flush remaining work, and discard queued output. Consumers waiting for results remain blocked until new data is queued. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure. If cleanup of discarded data is needed, supply cleanup callbacks via hts_tpool_dispatch3 when the jobs were submitted.
requirements: q must be a valid process queue associated with a pool.
free_results indicates whether to free results (exact semantics of freeing are not fully documented here).
job_cleanup and result_cleanup callbacks (if provided via hts_tpool_dispatch3) will be used for discarding pending jobs/results.

functions.name: hts_tpool_process_qsize
functions.description: Return the process queue size for q.
requirements: q must be a valid process queue.

functions.name: hts_tpool_destroy
functions.description: Destroy a thread pool p, joining worker threads so that they complete their current workload before returning.
requirements: p must be a valid pool previously returned by hts_tpool_init.
All process queues associated with p should have been properly handled; destroying the pool ends its use.
Do not use p or any associated resources after this call.

functions.name: hts_tpool_kill
functions.description: Destroy a thread pool p without waiting for jobs to complete. Intended for rapid termination (e.g., after a fatal error).
requirements: p must be a valid pool previously returned by hts_tpool_init.
Outstanding jobs may not complete; callers must be prepared for abrupt termination of work.
Do not use p or any associated resources after this call.

functions.name: hts_tpool_next_result
functions.description: Nonblocking pop of the next completed job result from process q. Results are returned in strict order. Returns an hts_tpool_result pointer if available, or NULL if none.
requirements: q must be a valid process queue that produces results (not in-only).
Caller is responsible for freeing results via hts_tpool_delete_result() when done.
Order of results is guaranteed to be sequential.

functions.name: hts_tpool_next_result_wait
functions.description: Blocking pop of the next completed job result from process q, waiting if needed. Results are returned in strict order. Returns a result on success, or NULL on error or during shutdown.
requirements: q must be a valid process queue that produces results (not in-only).
Caller must free returned results via hts_tpool_delete_result().
Callers should handle a NULL return as error or shutdown.

functions.name: hts_tpool_delete_result
functions.description: Free a result r. If free_data is non-zero, also free the internal result data (the pointer that would be returned by hts_tpool_result_data()).
requirements: r must be a result obtained from the result APIs.
If free_data is non-zero, the data pointer must be suitable for freeing by this library; callers should not double-free it elsewhere.

functions.name: hts_tpool_result_data
functions.description: Return the data payload of a result r (the actual job result pointer).
requirements: r must be a valid result returned by the result APIs.
Returned pointer lifetime is tied to r unless ownership is transferred by the caller per library usage; exact ownership rules beyond delete_result(free_data) are not further specified.

functions.name: hts_tpool_process_init
functions.description: Create and initialize a process queue associated with pool p. qsize sets the queue size. If in_only is non-zero, the process does not store output results. Returns a process pointer on success or NULL on failure. Must be freed via hts_tpool_process_destroy().
requirements: p must be a valid pool created by hts_tpool_init.
qsize is the queue size; valid ranges/limits are not specified.
If in_only is true, the process does not maintain an output queue; result retrieval functions are not applicable.
The created process must later be destroyed with hts_tpool_process_destroy().
After creation, the process must be attached to the pool scheduler via hts_tpool_process_attach(p, q) before running jobs.

functions.name: hts_tpool_process_destroy
functions.description: Deallocate memory and resources for a process queue q. Must be called before destroying the thread pool.
requirements: q must be a valid process queue created by hts_tpool_process_init.
Must be called before hts_tpool_destroy() on the associated pool.
After this call, q must not be used.

functions.name: hts_tpool_process_empty
functions.description: Return non-zero if there are no items in the process results queue and none pending; otherwise zero.
requirements: q must be a valid process queue.

functions.name: hts_tpool_process_len
functions.description: Return the number of completed jobs in the process results queue for q.
requirements: q must be a valid process queue.

functions.name: hts_tpool_process_sz
functions.description: Return the total number of jobs for q: completed in the results queue plus running and queued to run.
requirements: q must be a valid process queue.

functions.name: hts_tpool_process_shutdown
functions.description: Signal shutdown for process q and wake any threads waiting on its condition variables.
requirements: q must be a valid process queue.
After shutdown, behavior of enqueuing and waiting for results is limited; callers should expect termination of activity for q.

functions.name: hts_tpool_process_is_shutdown
functions.description: Return the shutdown state for process q: 1 indicates normal shutdown; values greater than 1 indicate shutdown due to an error condition.
requirements: q must be a valid process queue.

functions.name: hts_tpool_process_attach
functions.description: Attach process q to the pool scheduler p so it can run jobs. This should be called after creating the process. Processes may be temporarily detached and reattached as needed.
requirements: p must be a valid pool; q must be a process created by hts_tpool_process_init.
Must be called after making a thread process to enable scheduling on q.

functions.name: hts_tpool_process_detach
functions.description: Detach process q from the pool scheduler p to stop running jobs on q while allowing other processes to continue.
requirements: p must be a valid pool; q must be a process previously attached to p.

functions.name: hts_tpool_process_ref_incr
functions.description: Increment the reference count of process queue q. Useful when the queue is managed by multiple external threads so each can decrement independently.
requirements: q must be a valid process queue.
Each increment should be balanced by a corresponding hts_tpool_process_ref_decr().

functions.name: hts_tpool_process_ref_decr
functions.description: Decrement the reference count of process queue q. Complements hts_tpool_process_ref_incr().
requirements: q must be a valid process queue.
Each call should balance a prior hts_tpool_process_ref_incr() from some owner.

Returns query length as hts_pos_t

functions.name: bam_cigar2rlen
functions.description: Computes reference length (consumed reference bases) from BAM-encoded CIGAR array (sum of M,D,N,=,X).
requirements: cigar must have at least n_cigar elements
Ignores invalid ops

functions.name: bam_endpos
functions.description: Returns the coordinate of the first base after the alignment on the reference (0-based). For unmapped/no-ref-consuming CIGAR, returns pos+1.
requirements: b must be valid
CIGAR and core.pos should be set

functions.name: bam_str2flag
functions.description: Parses a string of SAM flag keywords into an integer flag. Returns negative on error.
requirements: str must be a NUL-terminated string of recognized tokens
Caller must handle negative return on error

functions.name: bam_flag2str
functions.description: Creates a newly-allocated string describing set SAM flag keywords for the given flag. Caller must free.
requirements: flag is a bitmask of BAM_F*
Returns malloc-allocated string; caller must free
Returns NULL on failure

functions.name: bam_set_qname
functions.description: Sets the read name (QNAME) in a bam1_t, adjusting internal layout as needed.
requirements: b must be valid; qname must be a valid string ("*" allowed)
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure

functions.name: sam_parse_cigar
functions.signature: ssize_t sam_parse_cigar(const char *in, char **end, uint32_t **a_cigar, size_t *a_mem);
functions.description: Parses a textual CIGAR string into a malloc/realloc-managed uint32_t BAM-encoded array. Updates end to new string position.
requirements: in must point to CIGAR text; may be part of a larger string
a_cigar must point to a buffer pointer; may be NULL for allocation
a_mem must point to capacity counter
On success returns number of ops; -1 on error; end may be NULL

functions.name: bam_parse_cigar
functions.description: Parses a textual CIGAR and sets/replaces the CIGAR field in bam1_t, shifting data as necessary. A "*" CIGAR removes the CIGAR (returns 0).
requirements: b must be a valid record; may be partially populated
in must point to CIGAR text; end may be NULL
Returns number of operators, 0 for "*", or -1 on error

functions.name: sam_idx_init
functions.signature: int sam_idx_init(htsFile *fp, sam_hdr_t *h, int min_shift, const char *fnidx);
functions.description: Initialises index creation on an open SAM/BAM/CRAM file for writing. Must be called after writing header and before data. Use sam_idx_save() to write index.
requirements: fp must be a writable file handle of appropriate type
h must be a header (needed for BAI/CSI)
min_shift 0 for BAI, >0 for CSI (defaults to 14)
fnidx must remain valid until sam_idx_save()
Returns 0 on success, <0 on failure

functions.name: sam_idx_save
functions.description: Writes to disk the index initialised by sam_idx_init().
requirements: fp must have been initialised with sam_idx_init()
Returns 0 on success, <0 on failure

functions.name: sam_index_load
functions.description: Loads a BAM/CRAM index, searching alongside the given filename. Equivalent to sam_index_load3(fp, fn, NULL, HTS_IDX_SAVE_REMOTE).
requirements: fp must be a valid file handle for the data file
fn is the data filename
Returns hts_idx_t* on success; NULL on error; destroy with hts_idx_destroy()

functions.name: sam_index_load2
functions.description: Loads a specific BAM/CRAM index file for a data file.
requirements: fp is the data file handle
fn is data filename; fnidx is explicit index filename or NULL
Returns index pointer or NULL on error; free with hts_idx_destroy()

functions.name: sam_index_load3
functions.signature: hts_idx_t *sam_index_load3(htsFile *fp, const char *fn, const char *fnidx, int flags);
functions.description: Loads or streams an index file with control flags. May save a local copy of remote indexes (except remote CRAM).
requirements: fp is data file handle
fn is data filename; fnidx optional index filename
flags may include HTS_IDX_SAVE_REMOTE and/or HTS_IDX_SILENT_FAIL
Returns index pointer or NULL; free with hts_idx_destroy()

functions.name: sam_index_build
functions.signature: int sam_index_build(const char *fn, int min_shift) HTS_RESULT_USED;
functions.description: Generates and saves an index for the input file. min_shift 0 for BAI, >0 for CSI.
requirements: fn is input data filename
Returns 0 on success; negative on error (-1 general, -2 open fail, -3 format not indexable, -4 create/save index failed)

functions.name: sam_index_build2
functions.signature: int sam_index_build2(const char *fn, const char *fnidx, int min_shift) HTS_RESULT_USED;
functions.description: Builds an index and writes to a specified filename (or derived if NULL).
requirements: fn is input filename; fnidx optional output index filename
Returns 0 on success; negative on error (see sam_index_build codes)

functions.name: sam_index_build3
functions.signature: int sam_index_build3(const char *fn, const char *fnidx, int min_shift, int nthreads) HTS_RESULT_USED;
functions.description: Builds an index using specified number of threads and writes to a specified filename.
requirements: fn input filename; fnidx optional output
nthreads >=1 recommended
Returns 0 on success; negative on error (see sam_index_build codes)

functions.name: sam_itr_queryi
functions.signature: hts_itr_t *sam_itr_queryi(const hts_idx_t *idx, int tid, hts_pos_t beg, hts_pos_t end);
functions.description: Creates an iterator over a region by numeric target id and [beg,end). Supports special HTS_IDX_* tid values.

beg/end ignored for special tid

functions.name: sam_itr_querys

requirements: idx must be valid
hdr required for reference name mapping
region must be a valid region string
Returns iterator or NULL on failure; free with sam_itr_destroy()
SAM files must be BGZF-compressed for iterators

functions.name: sam_itr_regions
functions.signature: hts_itr_t *sam_itr_regions(const hts_idx_t *idx, sam_hdr_t *hdr, hts_reglist_t *reglist, unsigned int regcount);
functions.description: Creates a multi-region iterator from arrays of intervals per reference. Returns each read at most once even if overlapping multiple intervals.

reglist must be filled with ref name in reg, and intervals/count set; other fields unused
Returns iterator or NULL; free with sam_itr_destroy()

functions.name: sam_itr_regarray
functions.signature: hts_itr_t *sam_itr_regarray(const hts_idx_t *idx, sam_hdr_t *hdr, char **regarray, unsigned int regcount);
functions.description: Creates a multi-region iterator from an array of textual region strings (parsed by hts_parse_reg()).
requirements: idx and hdr must be valid
regarray contains regcount strings
Returns iterator or NULL; free with sam_itr_destroy()

functions.name: sam_parse_region
functions.signature: const char *sam_parse_region(sam_hdr_t *h, const char *s, int *tid, hts_pos_t *beg, hts_pos_t *end, int flags);
functions.description: Parses a region string into tid/beg/end according to the header. Returns pointer to the char after the parsed region or NULL on error.
requirements: h must be a valid header
s must be a valid region string
tid, beg, end must be non-NULL pointers
flags control parsing (details in htslib)
Returns non-NULL on success; NULL on failure

functions.name: sam_open_mode
functions.signature: int sam_open_mode(char *mode, const char *fn, const char *format);
functions.description: Fills an hts_open mode string (without options) appropriate for filename and format. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: mode must point to a buffer large enough to hold the resulting mode string
fn is the filename; format may hint format
Returns 0 on success; non-zero on failure

functions.signature: char *sam_open_mode_opts(const char *fn, const char *mode, const char *format);

Returns allocated string on success; NULL on failure; caller must free

functions.name: sam_hdr_change_HD
functions.signature: int sam_hdr_change_HD(sam_hdr_t *h, const char *key, const char *val);
functions.description: Adds or updates a key/value on the @HD line in the header.

key and val are strings; key must be an @HD tag
Returns int status (0 on success; non-zero on error)

h should be the header (fully or partially read)
b must be initialised

functions.name: sam_format1
functions.signature: int sam_format1(const sam_hdr_t *h, const bam1_t *b, kstring_t *str) HTS_RESULT_USED;
functions.description: Formats a BAM record into a SAM text line, written into str.
requirements: h and b must be valid
str must be initialised; its contents will be overwritten/extended
Returns >=0 on success; <0 on error

functions.name: sam_read1
functions.description: Reads the next record from a SAM/BAM/CRAM file into b using header h.
requirements: fp must be open for reading
h should be the header associated with fp
b must be initialised
Returns >=0 on success; -1 on end of stream; < -1 on error

functions.name: sam_write1
functions.signature: int sam_write1(samFile *fp, const sam_hdr_t *h, const bam1_t *b) HTS_RESULT_USED;

h and b must be valid
Returns >=0 on success; negative on error

functions.signature: int sam_passes_filter(const sam_hdr_t *h, const bam1_t *b, struct hts_filter_t *filt);
functions.description: Evaluates whether a record passes a compiled htslib filter expression.
requirements: h and b must be valid
filt must be created via hts_filter_init
Returns 1 if passes, 0 if not, <0 on error

functions.name: bam_aux_first
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the first auxiliary field in a BAM record, or NULL with errno=ENOENT if none.
requirements: b must be valid
Returned pointer is within b->data; do not free
Check errno on NULL

functions.name: bam_aux_next
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the next auxiliary field after s, or NULL on end/error. Sets errno: ENOENT (last), EINVAL (corrupt).
requirements: b must be valid; s must be a pointer returned by aux APIs
Check errno when NULL returned

functions.name: bam_aux_get
functions.description: Finds and returns a pointer to the specified auxiliary tag data. NULL if not present or on error; errno set to ENOENT or EINVAL.
requirements: b must be valid
tag must be a two-character tag
Returned pointer is into b->data; do not free

functions.name: bam_aux2i
functions.description: Converts an integer-type aux tag to int64. Returns 0 and sets errno=EINVAL if not an integer type.
requirements: s must be a tag pointer from bam_aux_get/first/next
Caller must check errno on ambiguous 0

functions.name: bam_aux2f
functions.description: Converts a numeric aux tag to double. Returns 0.0 and sets errno=EINVAL if not numeric.
requirements: s must be a tag pointer
Caller must check errno on ambiguous 0.0

functions.name: bam_aux2A
functions.description: Returns the character value of an 'A' type aux tag. Returns 0 and sets errno=EINVAL if not character type.
requirements: s must be a tag pointer
Caller must check errno

functions.name: bam_aux2Z
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the string content of a 'Z' or 'H' type aux tag. Returns NULL and sets errno=EINVAL if not string type.
requirements: s must be a tag pointer
Returned pointer is within b->data; do not free

functions.name: bam_auxB_len
functions.description: Returns the length of an array-type ('B') auxiliary tag. Returns 0 and sets errno=EINVAL if not array.
requirements: s must be a 'B' tag pointer

functions.name: bam_auxB2i
functions.description: Returns the integer value at index idx from an array-type aux tag. Sets errno=EINVAL for non-integer arrays, ERANGE for out-of-range idx; returns 0 on error.
requirements: s must be 'B' array tag pointer
idx must be < bam_auxB_len(s)
Caller must check errno on 0

functions.name: bam_auxB2f
functions.description: Returns the floating-point value at index idx from an array-type aux tag. Sets errno=EINVAL for non-numeric arrays, ERANGE for out-of-range; returns 0.0 on error.
requirements: s must be 'B' array tag pointer
idx in range
Caller must check errno on 0.0

functions.name: bam_aux_append
functions.signature: int bam_aux_append(bam1_t *b, const char tag[2], char type, int len, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Appends a new auxiliary tag to a BAM record.
requirements: b must be valid; tag two letters; type must be valid (A,cCsSiIfHZB)
data must not point into b itself
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure; errno set (ENOMEM/EINVAL)

functions.name: bam_aux_del
functions.description: Deletes the specified auxiliary tag from a BAM record.
requirements: b must be valid; s must be a pointer to an existing aux field
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure; errno=EINVAL if corrupt

functions.name: bam_aux_remove
functions.description: Deletes the aux field at s and returns a pointer to the following aux field (iterator form). NULL on last or error; errno set (ENOENT/EINVAL).
requirements: b valid; s points to an existing aux field
Check errno on NULL

functions.name: bam_aux_update_str
functions.signature: int bam_aux_update_str(bam1_t *b, const char tag[2], int len, const char *data);
functions.description: Updates or adds a string-type ('Z') aux tag, preserving tag order. Ensures NUL termination as per current HTSlib behavior.
requirements: b must be valid; tag two letters
If len<0, strlen(data) used; otherwise copies exactly len bytes and appends NUL if missing
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure; errno may be EINVAL/ENOMEM

functions.name: bam_aux_update_int
functions.signature: int bam_aux_update_int(bam1_t *b, const char tag[2], int64_t val);
functions.description: Updates or adds an integer-type aux tag (cCsSiI). Preserves tag order.
requirements: b valid; tag two letters
val must be within storable range [-2147483647, 4294967295]; otherwise errno=EOVERFLOW/ERANGE
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure (EINVAL/ENOMEM)

functions.name: bam_aux_update_float
functions.signature: int bam_aux_update_float(bam1_t *b, const char tag[2], float val);
functions.description: Updates or adds a float-type aux tag. Preserves tag order.
requirements: b valid; tag two letters
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure; errno may be EINVAL/ENOMEM

functions.name: bam_aux_update_array
functions.signature: int bam_aux_update_array(bam1_t *b, const char tag[2], uint8_t type, uint32_t items, void *data);
functions.description: Updates or adds an array-type ('B') aux tag with specified subtype and items. Preserves tag order and grows/shrinks record.
requirements: b valid; tag two letters
type must be one of c,C,s,S,i,I,f
data must not point inside b
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure; errno EINVAL/ENOMEM

requirements: state valid; ntype non-NULL or caller ignores count
Returned array remains valid until state is freed; do not free

functions.name: sam_hdr_set
functions.description: Sets/replaces the header on a file handle. Destroys existing header. If dup==0, increments reference count of h; otherwise uses a duplicate.
requirements: fp must be valid
h must be a valid header
dup must be 0 or 1
Returns 0 on success; -1 on error

functions.name: sam_hdr_get
functions.description: Returns the header currently associated with a file handle, or NULL (e.g., if header not yet read).
requirements: fp must be valid
Caller should increment ref count via sam_hdr_incr_ref if retaining beyond fp lifecycle
May return NULL even for valid file if header not read yet

functions.name: fai_build3
functions.signature: int fai_build3(const char *fn, const char *fnfai, const char *fngzi)
functions.description: Builds a .fai index (and optionally a .gzi index) for a FASTA/FASTQ file. Use when you need to explicitly control the output index filenames. If fnfai is NULL, the index name is derived as fn + ".fai"; if fngzi is NULL and the input is bgzip-compressed, a GZI index name is derived as fn + ".gzi".
requirements: fn must point to the FASTA/FASTQ filename.
If fn refers to a bgzip-compressed file and fngzi is NULL, a .gzi will be created alongside fn.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure; callers should check the return code.

functions.name: fai_build
functions.description: Builds a .fai index (and .gzi if the input is bgzip-compressed) for the given FASTA/FASTQ file using default index names. Equivalent to calling fai_build3(fn, NULL, NULL).
requirements: fn must point to the FASTA/FASTQ filename.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure; callers should check the return code.

functions.name: fai_destroy
functions.description: Destroys and frees a faidx_t index object previously returned by fai_load/fai_load3/fai_load_format. Call when the index is no longer needed.
requirements: fai must be a pointer previously obtained from a successful fai_load*/fai_load*_format call or NULL.
After calling, the faidx_t pointer must not be used again.

functions.name: fai_load3
functions.signature: faidx_t *fai_load3(const char *fn, const char *fnfai, const char *fngzi, int flags)
functions.description: Loads a FASTA/FASTQ index for file fn, using explicit paths for the .fai and .gzi if provided. If FAI_CREATE is set in flags and the index is missing, it will be built via fai_build3(). Returns an opaque faidx_t handle on success.
requirements: fn must be the FASTA/FASTQ file path (can be bgzip-compressed).
If fnfai is NULL, the index filename will default to fn + ".fai".
If fngzi is NULL and fn is bgzip-compressed, the bgzip index filename will default to fn + ".gzi".
If flags has FAI_CREATE, missing indexes will be created.
Caller must free the returned faidx_t* with fai_destroy() when done.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check.

functions.name: fai_load
functions.description: Loads the index for fn using default behavior. Equivalent to fai_load3(fn, NULL, NULL, FAI_CREATE|FAI_CACHE). Returns an faidx_t handle on success.
requirements: fn must be the FASTA file path (may be compressed with bgzip).
Caller must free the returned faidx_t* with fai_destroy() when done.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check.

functions.name: fai_load3_format
functions.signature: faidx_t *fai_load3_format(const char *fn, const char *fnfai, const char *fngzi, int flags, enum fai_format_options format)
functions.description: Loads a FASTA or FASTQ index for file fn, explicitly specifying the format. Index file paths can be provided; defaults are used if NULL. With FAI_CREATE, missing indexes are built via fai_build3().
requirements: fn must be the FASTA/FASTQ file path (can be bgzip-compressed).
format must be one of FAI_FASTA or FAI_FASTQ (FAI_NONE is not documented for loading).
If fnfai is NULL, defaults to fn + ".fai".
If fngzi is NULL and fn is bgzip-compressed, defaults to fn + ".gzi".
If flags has FAI_CREATE, missing indexes will be created.
Caller must free the returned faidx_t* with fai_destroy() when done.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check.

functions.name: fai_load_format
functions.description: Loads the index for fn using the specified format and default behavior. Equivalent to fai_load3_format(fn, NULL, NULL, FAI_CREATE|FAI_CACHE, format).
requirements: fn must be the FASTA/FASTQ file path.
format must be FAI_FASTA or FAI_FASTQ.
Caller must free the returned faidx_t* with fai_destroy() when done.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check.

functions.name: fai_fetch
functions.description: Fetches the nucleotide sequence covering a region specified by a region string (e.g. "chr2:20,000-30,000"). Returns a malloc-allocated sequence buffer on success and sets *len to the fetched length; returns NULL on failure. Region names that may be ambiguous can be disambiguated by wrapping with curly braces.
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded faidx_t.
reg must be a NUL-terminated region string; ambiguous names can be quoted with curly braces.
len must be non-NULL; on success set to length; set to -2 if sequence not present; -1 on general error.
Caller must free the returned char* with free().
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check.

functions.name: fai_fetch64
functions.description: 64-bit variant of fai_fetch(). Fetches a region sequence given a region string; returns a malloc-allocated sequence and writes the length to *len. Supports large coordinates via hts_pos_t.
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded faidx_t.
reg must be a NUL-terminated region string; ambiguous names can be quoted with curly braces.
len must be non-NULL; on success set to length; set to -2 if sequence not present; -1 on general error.
Caller must free the returned char* with free().
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check.

functions.name: fai_line_length
functions.description: Returns the line wrap length (excluding newline) for the sequence identified by the region string (e.g. "chr2" or "chr2:..."), or a negative value on error. Useful for reconstructing original FASTA/FASTQ line breaks.
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded faidx_t.
reg must be a NUL-terminated region string.
Callers must check for negative return values indicating error.

functions.name: fai_fetchqual
functions.description: Fetches the quality string for a region from a FASTQ index given a region string. Returns a malloc-allocated quality buffer and sets *len to the length. Region names can be quoted with curly braces like fai_fetch().
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded FASTQ index (via fai_load*_format with FASTQ).
reg must be a NUL-terminated region string; ambiguous names can be quoted with curly braces.
len must be non-NULL; on success set to length; set to -2 if sequence not present; -1 on general error.
Caller must free the returned char* with free().
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check.

functions.name: fai_fetchqual64
functions.description: 64-bit variant of fai_fetchqual(). Fetches the quality string for a region from a FASTQ index using hts_pos_t lengths. Returns a malloc-allocated buffer.
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded FASTQ index.
reg must be a NUL-terminated region string; ambiguous names can be quoted with curly braces.
len must be non-NULL; on success set to length; set to -2 if sequence not present; -1 on general error.
Caller must free the returned char* with free().
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check.

functions.name: faidx_fetch_nseq
functions.description: Deprecated. Returns the number of sequences in the index. Prefer faidx_nseq().
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded faidx_t.
Callers should migrate to faidx_nseq().

functions.name: faidx_fetch_seq
functions.signature: char *faidx_fetch_seq(const faidx_t *fai, const char *c_name, int p_beg_i, int p_end_i, int *len)
functions.description: Fetches the sequence substring for a named region using zero-based coordinates. p_beg_i and p_end_i are zero-based positions; on success returns a malloc-allocated sequence and sets *len to the number of bases returned. Sets *len to -2 if c_name not present, -1 on general error.
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded faidx_t.
c_name must be a NUL-terminated region (sequence) name present in the index.
p_beg_i and p_end_i are zero-based positions.
len must be non-NULL; on success set to fetched length; -2 if c_name not present; -1 on general error.
Caller must free the returned char* with free().
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check.

functions.name: faidx_fetch_seq64
functions.signature: char *faidx_fetch_seq64(const faidx_t *fai, const char *c_name, hts_pos_t p_beg_i, hts_pos_t p_end_i, hts_pos_t *len)
