functions.description: 64-bit variant of faidx_fetch_seq(). Fetches a sequence substring for a named region using zero-based hts_pos_t coordinates. Returns a malloc-allocated sequence and sets *len accordingly.
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded faidx_t.
c_name must be a NUL-terminated region (sequence) name present in the index.
p_beg_i and p_end_i are zero-based (hts_pos_t) positions.
len must be non-NULL; on success set to fetched length; -2 if c_name not present; -1 on general error.
Caller must free the returned char* with free().
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check.

functions.name: faidx_fetch_qual
functions.signature: char *faidx_fetch_qual(const faidx_t *fai, const char *c_name, int p_beg_i, int p_end_i, int *len)
functions.description: Fetches the quality substring for a named FASTQ entry using zero-based coordinates. Returns a malloc-allocated quality string and sets *len to the number of qualities returned. Sets *len to -2 if c_name not present; -1 on general error.
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded FASTQ index.
c_name must be a NUL-terminated sequence name present in the index.
p_beg_i and p_end_i are zero-based positions.
len must be non-NULL; on success set to fetched length; -2 if c_name not present; -1 on general error.
Caller must free the returned char* with free().
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check.

functions.name: faidx_fetch_qual64
functions.signature: char *faidx_fetch_qual64(const faidx_t *fai, const char *c_name, hts_pos_t p_beg_i, hts_pos_t p_end_i, hts_pos_t *len)
functions.description: 64-bit variant of faidx_fetch_qual(). Fetches the quality substring for a named FASTQ entry using zero-based hts_pos_t coordinates. Returns a malloc-allocated string and sets *len.
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded FASTQ index.
c_name must be a NUL-terminated sequence name present in the index.
p_beg_i and p_end_i are zero-based (hts_pos_t) positions.
len must be non-NULL; on success set to fetched length; -2 if c_name not present; -1 on general error.
Caller must free the returned char* with free().
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check.

functions.name: faidx_has_seq
functions.description: Checks if a sequence name exists in the index. Returns 1 if present, 0 if absent.
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded faidx_t.
seq must be a NUL-terminated sequence name.

functions.name: faidx_nseq
functions.description: Returns the number of sequences stored in the index.
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded faidx_t.

functions.name: faidx_iseq
functions.description: Returns the name of the i-th sequence in the index as a string pointer, or possibly NULL on error (not documented).
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded faidx_t.
i identifies the i-th sequence; valid range is not explicitly documented; callers should be prepared for NULL if out of range.

functions.name: faidx_seq_len64
functions.description: Returns the length of the named sequence as an hts_pos_t, or -1 if the sequence is not present.
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded faidx_t.
seq must be a NUL-terminated sequence name.
Callers must check for return value -1 indicating not present.

functions.name: faidx_seq_len
functions.description: Deprecated: returns the length of the named sequence as an int, or -1 if not present. Cannot handle very long sequences. Use faidx_seq_len64() instead.
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded faidx_t.
seq must be a NUL-terminated sequence name.
Callers should prefer faidx_seq_len64().
Callers must check for return value -1 indicating not present.

functions.name: fai_parse_region
functions.signature: const char *fai_parse_region(const faidx_t *fai, const char *s, int *tid, hts_pos_t *beg, hts_pos_t *end, int flags)
functions.description: Parses a region string according to HTS parsing flags, returning the sequence index (tid) and zero-based begin and one-past-end coordinates. Returns a pointer to the end of the parsed input on success, or NULL on failure. Curly braces can be used to disambiguate reference names containing colons.
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded faidx_t.
s must be a NUL-terminated region string.
tid, beg, and end must be non-NULL pointers to receive outputs.
flags controls parsing behavior (see HTS_PARSE_* in hts.h).
Callers must check for NULL return to detect parse failure.

functions.name: fai_adjust_region
functions.signature: int fai_adjust_region(const faidx_t *fai, int tid, hts_pos_t *beg, hts_pos_t *end)
functions.description: Adjusts the supplied 0-based region coordinates to lie within the sequence boundaries for the specified sequence index. If beg > end, beg is set to end. Returns 1 if beg adjusted, 2 if end adjusted, 3 if both adjusted, 0 if unchanged, or -1 if tid is invalid.
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded faidx_t.
tid must be a valid sequence index as returned by fai_parse_region().
beg and end must be non-NULL pointers to 0-based coordinates.
Callers must check the return value for -1 (error) and interpret adjustment codes.

functions.name: fai_set_cache_size
functions.description: Sets the BGZF-layer cache size (in bytes) used by the underlying compressed file associated with the index.
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded faidx_t.
cache_size is a size in bytes; no specific range constraints are documented.

functions.name: fai_thread_pool
functions.signature: int fai_thread_pool(faidx_t *fai, struct hts_tpool *pool, int qsize)
functions.description: Associates a thread pool with the underlying BGZF layer for parallel I/O. If qsize is 0, the job queue size is twice the number of threads in the pool.
requirements: fai must be a valid pointer to a loaded faidx_t.
pool must be a thread pool created via hts_create_threads (from htslib).
qsize controls job queue size; if 0, it defaults to 2× thread count.
Returns an int; callers should check for errors (specific error codes not documented).

functions.name: fai_path
functions.description: Determines and returns the path to the reference index file for a given reference path. If the input uses the "##idx##" URL syntax, the index path is taken directly. For local references, if the index is missing it will be created alongside the reference; for remote references, NULL is returned if the index cannot be found. The returned string must be freed by the caller.
requirements: fa must be a NUL-terminated path to a reference file.
If fa is local and the index file is missing, this call may create the index alongside the reference.
If fa is remote and the index is missing, the function returns NULL.
Caller must free the returned char* with free().
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check.

functions.name: tbx_itr_destroy
functions.signature: unknown (macro wrapper around hts_itr_destroy; exact function prototype is not declared in this header)
functions.description: Destroys an iterator previously created for traversing a tabix index. This is a macro that forwards to hts_itr_destroy. Use it to release resources associated with an iterator produced by tbx_itr_queryi/tbx_itr_querys (or other htslib iterator creators).
requirements: iter must be a valid iterator object created by an htslib iterator creation function (e.g., tbx_itr_queryi/tbx_itr_querys)
Behavior on NULL iter is unknown (not documented here)
Exact return type and error behavior are unknown as the underlying function signature is not in this header

functions.name: tbx_itr_queryi
functions.signature: unknown (macro wrapper around hts_itr_query((tbx)->idx, tid, beg, end, tbx_readrec))
functions.description: Creates an iterator over a genomic interval specified by numeric contig id (tid) and [beg, end) coordinates, using the tabix index within tbx. This macro ultimately calls hts_itr_query with tbx_readrec as the record reader.
requirements: tbx must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid tbx_t with a loaded index (tbx->idx)
tid should refer to a contig present in the index (inferred from purpose)
beg and end should define a valid interval (ordering and bounds not specified here)
The returned iterator must be destroyed with tbx_itr_destroy when no longer needed
Exact iterator type, return semantics, and error codes are unknown from this header

functions.name: tbx_itr_querys
functions.signature: unknown (macro wrapper around hts_itr_querys((tbx)->idx, s, (hts_name2id_f)(tbx_name2id), (tbx), hts_itr_query, tbx_readrec))
functions.description: Creates an iterator for region(s) described by a textual query string s (e.g., chrom:beg-end; exact syntax per hts_itr_querys). It maps names via tbx_name2id and reads records via tbx_readrec.
requirements: tbx must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid tbx_t with a loaded index
s must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string in the format accepted by hts_itr_querys (format details not specified here)
The returned iterator must be destroyed with tbx_itr_destroy
Exact iterator type, return semantics, accepted region string syntax, and error codes are not specified in this header

functions.name: tbx_itr_next
functions.signature: unknown (macro wrapper around hts_itr_next(hts_get_bgzfp(htsfp), itr, r, tbx))
functions.description: Advances the iterator itr and reads the next record from the associated BGZF stream, storing it in r. This macro forwards to hts_itr_next, supplying tbx as the reader context and using tbx_readrec.
requirements: htsfp must be an htsFile* opened on the BGZF-compressed data file corresponding to tbx
itr must be a valid iterator obtained from tbx_itr_queryi/tbx_itr_querys (or compatible)
r must be a pointer to a record/storage object compatible with tbx_readrec (exact type not specified here)
tbx must be the tbx_t corresponding to the opened file
Return type and end-of-iteration/error semantics are not specified in this header

functions.name: tbx_bgzf_itr_next
functions.signature: unknown (macro wrapper around hts_itr_next(bgzfp, itr, r, tbx))
functions.description: Like tbx_itr_next, but takes a BGZF* directly instead of an htsFile*. Advances itr and decodes the next record using tbx_readrec.
requirements: bgzfp must be a valid BGZF* for the underlying data stream
itr must be a valid iterator as created by tbx_itr_queryi/tbx_itr_querys
r must be a pointer to a record/storage object compatible with tbx_readrec (exact type not specified here)
tbx must be the matching tbx_t for the stream
Return type and error semantics are not specified in this header

functions.name: tbx_name2id
functions.description: Maps a reference/sequence name string to its numeric id (tid) using the dictionary stored in the tbx index. Typically used to resolve region names to ids.
requirements: tbx must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid tbx_t with an initialized dictionary
ss must be a non-NULL, null-terminated C string
Return value conventions (e.g., -1 on not found) are not documented here

functions.name: hts_get_bgzfp
functions.description: Returns the underlying BGZF* stream for an htsFile opened on a BGZF-compressed file. Used internally by tbx_itr_next to obtain a BGZF handle.
requirements: fp must be a valid htsFile* that refers to a BGZF-compressed file
Returns NULL on error or non-BGZF files (exact behavior not specified here)

functions.name: tbx_readrec
functions.signature: int tbx_readrec(BGZF *fp, void *tbxv, void *sv, int *tid, hts_pos_t *beg, hts_pos_t *end);
functions.description: Internal helper used by iteration routines to read a single record from fp and extract the sequence id and [beg, end) coordinates according to the tbx configuration. The record content is stored via sv (implementation-specific).
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* positioned at the start of a record
tbxv must point to a valid tbx_t (passed as void*)
sv must point to caller-provided storage appropriate for receiving the decoded record (exact type/format not specified here)
tid, beg, and end must be non-NULL pointers where parsed values will be written
Return value and error codes are not described in this header

functions.name: tbx_index
functions.description: Builds a tabix index over the records in a BGZF-compressed file pointed to by fp, using configuration conf. Returns a newly allocated tbx_t on success; free with tbx_destroy.
requirements: fp must be a valid BGZF* referring to a BGZF-compressed input stream positioned at the start of the file to be indexed
min_shift should be between 0 and TBX_MAX_SHIFT (31) inclusive; exact constraints not explicitly documented here
conf must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid tbx_conf_t describing file column layout and meta settings
Caller must call tbx_destroy() on the returned tbx_t when finished
Error/NULL return conditions beyond allocation/IO failures are not specified here

functions.name: tbx_index_build
functions.signature: int tbx_index_build(const char *fn, int min_shift, const tbx_conf_t *conf);
functions.description: Builds a tabix index for the BGZF-compressed file named fn, using configuration conf and index binning parameter min_shift. Writes the index alongside the data file (default naming).
requirements: fn must be a non-NULL path to an existing BGZF-compressed file
min_shift should be between 0 and TBX_MAX_SHIFT (31) inclusive; exact constraints not explicitly documented here
conf must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid tbx_conf_t
Return values: 0 on success, -1 on general failure, -2 if the input compression is not BGZF (as documented)

functions.name: tbx_index_build2
functions.signature: int tbx_index_build2(const char *fn, const char *fnidx, int min_shift, const tbx_conf_t *conf);
functions.description: Builds a tabix index for file fn and writes it to the path fnidx. Use this to specify a custom index filename.
requirements: fn must be a non-NULL path to an existing BGZF-compressed file
fnidx must be a non-NULL path where the index will be written
min_shift should be between 0 and TBX_MAX_SHIFT (31) inclusive; exact constraints not explicitly documented here
conf must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid tbx_conf_t
Return values: 0 on success, -1 on general failure, -2 if compression is not BGZF

functions.name: tbx_index_build3
functions.signature: int tbx_index_build3(const char *fn, const char *fnidx, int min_shift, int n_threads, const tbx_conf_t *conf);
functions.description: Builds a tabix index for file fn, writing to fnidx, with optional multi-threading via n_threads. This is the most configurable builder.
requirements: fn must be a non-NULL path to an existing BGZF-compressed file
fnidx must be a non-NULL path where the index will be written (or a valid target as defined by implementation)
min_shift should be between 0 and TBX_MAX_SHIFT (31) inclusive; exact constraints not explicitly documented here
n_threads controls parallelism; valid range and semantics are not documented here
conf must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid tbx_conf_t
Return values: 0 on success, -1 on general failure, -2 if compression is not BGZF

functions.name: tbx_index_load
functions.description: Loads or streams a .tbi or .csi index for the data file fn. Equivalent to tbx_index_load3(fn, NULL, HTS_IDX_SAVE_REMOTE). Returns a tbx_t on success; free with tbx_destroy.
requirements: fn must be a non-NULL path to the data file whose index is to be loaded
On success the returned tbx_t must be freed with tbx_destroy()
On failure, returns NULL; detailed error handling behavior not specified here

functions.name: tbx_index_load2
functions.description: Loads or streams a .tbi or .csi index, using fnidx as the explicit index path if non-NULL; otherwise derives the index path from fn. Equivalent to tbx_index_load3(fn, fnidx, HTS_IDX_SAVE_REMOTE).
requirements: fn must be a non-NULL path to the data file
If fnidx is NULL, the index path will be derived from fn; otherwise fnidx must be a valid index path
Returns NULL on error; caller must free a successful result with tbx_destroy()

functions.name: tbx_index_load3
functions.signature: tbx_t *tbx_index_load3(const char *fn, const char *fnidx, int flags);
functions.description: Loads or streams a .tbi or .csi index with additional control via flags. Supports saving local copies of remote indexes and optionally failing silently when not present. Returns a tbx_t on success; free with tbx_destroy.
requirements: fn must be a non-NULL path to the data file
If fnidx is NULL, the index path will be derived from fn; otherwise fnidx must be a valid index path
flags may be a combination of HTS_IDX_SAVE_REMOTE and HTS_IDX_SILENT_FAIL (others per htslib may exist, but only these are documented here)
Returns NULL on error; caller must free a successful result with tbx_destroy()

functions.name: tbx_seqnames
functions.description: Returns an array of sequence/contig name strings from the tabix index, and writes the number of names to *n. The returned array should be freed by the caller, but not the pointed-to strings.
requirements: tbx must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid tbx_t
n must be a non-NULL pointer to an int to receive the count
Caller must free only the returned array container (e.g., with free()); do not free the individual const char* strings

functions.name: tbx_destroy
functions.description: Frees a tbx_t and any resources owned by it (index, dictionaries, etc.). Call this on tbx_t objects returned by tbx_index/tbx_index_load* when no longer needed.
requirements: tbx may be NULL or non-NULL; behavior on NULL is not documented here
After calling, tbx must not be used again

functions.name: bcf_strerror
functions.signature: const char *bcf_strerror(int errorcode, char *buffer, size_t maxbuffer);
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description of one or more bcf error codes into buffer and returns buffer (or NULL on invalid input). Purpose: turn BCF_ERR_* bitfields into comma-separated text. Expected usage: pass a buffer of at least 4 bytes; if errorcode is 0 the buffer will be set to an empty string. Notes: Appends '...' if truncated.
requirements: buffer must be non-NULL and maxbuffer >= 4, otherwise returns NULL
errorcode may be a bitwise-or of BCF_ERR_* codes; 0 yields empty string
Caller owns and provides buffer; content overwritten

functions.name: bcf_hdr_init
functions.description: Creates a new empty BCF/VCF header for reading or writing. Purpose: allocate and initialize bcf_hdr_t. Usage: pass "r" or "w"; when writing, mandatory fileformat and FILTER=PASS lines are added. Returned header must be freed with bcf_hdr_destroy().
requirements: mode must be "r" or "w" (per docs)
On success, caller must later call bcf_hdr_destroy()

functions.name: bcf_hdr_destroy
functions.description: Frees a bcf_hdr_t created by bcf_hdr_init/bcf_hdr_read/bcf_hdr_dup/etc. Safe to call when header is no longer needed.
requirements: h must be a header obtained from HTSlib header APIs or NULL; passing invalid pointers is undefined

functions.name: bcf_init
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new empty variant record object (bcf1_t). Usage: call before populating and writing/reading. Free with bcf_destroy().
requirements: On success, caller must later call bcf_destroy() to free the object

functions.name: bcf_destroy
functions.description: Deallocates a bcf1_t object allocated by bcf_init or returned by bcf_dup. Frees both struct and internal buffers.
requirements: v must be a valid pointer previously returned by bcf_init/bcf_dup/bcf_copy or NULL; invalid pointers are undefined

functions.name: bcf_empty
functions.description: Frees memory owned by the bcf1_t internals but not the bcf1_t object itself. Purpose: reuse an existing bcf1_t without freeing it.
requirements: v must be a valid bcf1_t*
Object itself remains allocated; caller retains ownership and may reuse it

functions.name: bcf_clear
functions.description: Resets a bcf1_t to be ready for the next read; primarily internal. Clears state flags and internal buffers as needed.
requirements: v must be a valid bcf1_t*

functions.name: bcf_hdr_read
functions.description: Reads and parses a VCF/BCF header from the open htsFile. Returns a populated header or NULL on failure. Free with bcf_hdr_destroy().
requirements: fp must be an htsFile opened for reading in VCF/BCF mode
On success, caller must later call bcf_hdr_destroy()

functions.name: bcf_hdr_set_samples
functions.signature: int bcf_hdr_set_samples(bcf_hdr_t *hdr, const char *samples, int is_file);
functions.description: Configures the header to include or exclude specified samples for efficient parsing. Purpose: subset genotype parsing to selected samples. Usage: samples can be a comma-separated list or filename (depending on is_file), with optional leading '^' to exclude; '-' includes all; NULL excludes all. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error, or a positive index of the first missing sample.
requirements: hdr must be the header obtained from bcf_hdr_read
samples format: 'LIST|FILE' selects; '^LIST|FILE' excludes; '-' include all; NULL exclude all
is_file must be 1 if samples refers to a file; 0 for comma list
Caller must check return value; positive return indicates offending sample index

functions.name: bcf_subset_format
functions.description: Subsets FORMAT/sample fields in a record according to hdr->keep_samples (as set by bcf_hdr_set_samples). Needed when iterating via bcf_itr_next, where automatic subsetting isn’t applied. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: hdr must be the header used with the record and configured by bcf_hdr_set_samples
rec must be an unpacked or decodable bcf1_t for which subsetting is desired
Caller must check return value for errors

functions.name: bcf_hdr_write
functions.description: Writes a header to an output htsFile (VCF/BCF). Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.
requirements: fp must be opened for writing in VCF/BCF mode
h must be a valid header; if samples were added, ensure bcf_hdr_sync() has occurred (automatically performed on first write)
Caller must check return value

functions.name: vcf_parse
functions.description: Parses a single VCF text line (without trailing newline) into a bcf1_t record. Works on textual VCF only. Returns 0 on success; <0 on error.
requirements: s->s must contain a single VCF line without trailing '\n' or '\r'
h must be a compatible header defining tags used in the line
v must be a valid bcf1_t* ready to populate

functions.name: vcf_open_mode
functions.signature: int vcf_open_mode(char *mode, const char *fn, const char *format);
functions.description: Completes an HTS open mode string based on filename and desired format (vcf|bcf|vcf.gz). Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure. Purpose: help construct mode strings for hts_open.
requirements: mode must be a writable, preallocated char buffer large enough for final mode string
fn must be a valid filename string
format should be one of "vcf", "bcf", or "vcf.gz" (per docs)
Caller must check return value

functions.name: vcf_format
functions.signature: int vcf_format(const bcf_hdr_t *h, const bcf1_t *v, kstring_t *s);
functions.description: Formats a bcf1_t record into VCF text and appends to a kstring. Opposite of vcf_parse. Usually use vcf_write instead. Returns 0 on success; <0 on error.
requirements: h must be the header corresponding to v
v must be sufficiently unpacked (bcf_unpack) to format
s must be an initialized kstring
Caller must check return code

functions.name: bcf_read
functions.description: Reads the next VCF/BCF record into v. Returns 0 on success; -1 on end-of-file; < -1 on critical error. Non-critical issues set v->errcode (BCF_ERR_*).
requirements: fp must be opened for reading and positioned on data after header
h must be header returned from bcf_hdr_read for this file
v must be a valid bcf1_t*
Caller must inspect return value and also check v->errcode for non-fatal issues before writing out

functions.name: bcf_unpack
functions.description: Unpacks/decode parts of a BCF/VCF record into the bcf1_t::d fields, as requested by 'which' bitmask (BCF_UN_*). Safe to call repeatedly; previously-unpacked parts are skipped. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: b must be a valid bcf1_t* containing a record
which must be a combination of BCF_UN_* flags; use BCF_UN_ALL for all
Call before accessing v->d fields

functions.name: bcf_dup
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of a record. Internally syncs src (bcf_sync1) first. The returned copy behaves like one read via bcf_read; caller should call bcf_unpack() as needed. Free with bcf_destroy().
requirements: src must be a valid record
Caller must bcf_destroy() the returned record
Caller should call bcf_unpack() on the returned copy before accessing decoded fields

functions.name: bcf_copy
functions.description: Copies content of src record into dst record, returning dst. Purpose: reuse an existing object. Caller should bcf_unpack() as needed after copy.
requirements: dst and src must be valid bcf1_t*
dst must be allocated; on success, dst contents are overwritten
Caller should bcf_unpack(dst, ...) before accessing decoded fields

functions.name: bcf_write
functions.description: Writes one VCF/BCF record to an output htsFile. Output type determined at open. Returns 0 on success; -1 on error.
requirements: fp must be opened for writing
h must be the header used to open the output and compatible with v
v must have consistent internal buffers (sync is handled internally when using bcf_update_* APIs)
Caller must check return value

functions.name: vcf_hdr_read
functions.description: Reads a VCF-format header specifically (VCF only). Typically use bcf_hdr_read(). Returns a new header or NULL on failure.
requirements: fp must be an htsFile opened for reading VCF
Caller must free with bcf_hdr_destroy()

functions.name: vcf_hdr_write
functions.description: Writes a header in VCF text format. Prefer bcf_hdr_write(). Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.
requirements: fp must be opened for writing VCF
h must be a valid header prepared for output
Caller must check return value

functions.name: vcf_read
functions.description: Reads a single VCF record (text) into v. Prefer bcf_read(). Returns 0 on success; -1 on EOF; < -1 on error.
requirements: fp must be opened for reading VCF
h must be header for this file
v must be valid

functions.name: vcf_write
functions.description: Writes a single record in VCF text format. Prefer bcf_write(). Returns 0 on success; -1 on error.
requirements: fp must be opened for writing VCF
h must be matching header
v must be valid
Caller must check return

functions.name: bcf_readrec
functions.signature: int bcf_readrec(BGZF *fp, void *null, void *v, int *tid, hts_pos_t *beg, hts_pos_t *end);
functions.description: Internal helper used by iterator macros to read the next BCF record from a BGZF stream. Fills record and region outputs. Returns status code for iterator. For internal use by iterators.
requirements: fp must be a BGZF* for a BGZF-compressed file
v must point to a bcf1_t
tid, beg, end must be valid pointers for outputs

functions.name: vcf_write_line
functions.description: Writes a raw VCF text line to fp, ensuring it ends with a newline. Does not validate content. Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure. Use with care.
requirements: fp must be opened for writing
line must point to text; function ensures trailing '\n'
Caller must check return value; content correctness is caller’s responsibility

functions.name: bcf_hdr_dup
functions.description: Creates a deep copy of an existing header. Returns new header or NULL on failure. Free with bcf_hdr_destroy().
requirements: hdr must be a valid header
Caller must free returned header

functions.name: bcf_hdr_combine
functions.description: Deprecated: copy lines from src to dst if not present. Returns 0 on success, or a bitset error (1 = conflicting definitions of tag length, others TBD). Prefer bcf_hdr_merge().
requirements: dst and src must be valid headers
Caller must handle deprecated status and error bit meanings

functions.name: bcf_hdr_merge
functions.description: Merges src header into dst, creating or updating dst as needed. Use in a loop to merge multiple headers. Returns merged header (possibly newly allocated) or NULL on failure.
requirements: dst may be NULL on first call; subsequent calls pass previous return
src must be a valid header
Caller must free final merged header with bcf_hdr_destroy()

functions.name: bcf_hdr_add_sample
functions.description: Adds a new sample name to a header. After all additions, call bcf_hdr_sync() (usually performed automatically on first write). Returns 0 on success; negative on error.
requirements: hdr must be a writable header intended for output
sample must be non-NULL valid sample name string
Caller should call bcf_hdr_sync() before operations requiring updated internal arrays if not performing a write

functions.name: bcf_hdr_set
functions.description: Reads a VCF header from file fname and updates the given header with its contents. Returns 0 on success; negative on error.
requirements: hdr must be a valid header
fname must refer to a readable file containing a VCF header
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_hdr_format
functions.signature: int bcf_hdr_format(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, int is_bcf, kstring_t *str);
functions.description: Appends a textual representation of the header into str. If is_bcf==0, IDX fields are omitted. Returns 0 on success; negative on error. Preferred over deprecated bcf_hdr_fmt_text for large headers.
requirements: hdr must be valid
str must be an initialized kstring
is_bcf 0 to discard IDX fields; non-zero to retain IDX fields
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_hdr_fmt_text
functions.description: Deprecated: returns a newly-allocated C string containing formatted header text and sets *len to length (excluding NUL). If is_bcf==0, omits IDX fields. Use bcf_hdr_format() instead. Caller must free returned string.
requirements: hdr must be valid
len must be a valid pointer to int for output
Caller must free returned string
Prefer bcf_hdr_format() for huge headers

functions.name: bcf_hdr_append
functions.description: Appends a new textual header line to the header. Returns 0 on success; negative on error.
requirements: h must be a valid header in writable context
line must be a properly formatted header line string starting with ## or #CHROM as appropriate
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_hdr_printf
functions.description: Formats a header line using printf-style formatting and appends it to the header. Returns 0 on success; negative on error.
requirements: h must be a valid header
format must be a valid printf-style format string with matching variadic args
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_hdr_get_version
functions.description: Returns the VCF version string stored in the header (e.g., "VCFv4.2"). Pointer is owned by the header; do not free.
requirements: hdr must be valid; returned pointer remains valid while hdr lives

functions.name: bcf_hdr_set_version
functions.description: Sets the version string in the header (e.g., "VCFv4.3"). Returns 0 on success; <0 on error.
requirements: hdr must be valid and writable
version should be a valid VCF version string
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_hdr_remove
functions.signature: void bcf_hdr_remove(bcf_hdr_t *h, int type, const char *key);
functions.description: Removes header lines of a given type (BCF_HL_*) optionally filtered by key (tag name). If key is NULL, removes all lines of that type.
requirements: h must be a valid header
type must be one of BCF_HL_*
key may be NULL or a valid tag for the type

functions.name: bcf_hdr_subset
functions.signature: bcf_hdr_t *bcf_hdr_subset(const bcf_hdr_t *h0, int n, char *const* samples, int *imap);
functions.description: Creates a new header with only the specified samples (and in the specified order). Unmatched sample names are ignored. Returns new header or NULL on failure. Caller frees with bcf_hdr_destroy().
requirements: h0 must be a valid source header
samples array length is n; may reorder samples
imap if non-NULL is filled with mapping from samples[] index to original sample index
Caller should compare n vs bcf_hdr_nsamples(out_hdr) to detect unmatched samples

functions.name: bcf_hdr_seqnames
functions.description: Returns a newly-allocated array of pointers to internal contig name strings and sets *nseqs to the count. Caller must free the array but not the names. Indices may not match bcf1_t.rid; use bcf_hdr_id2name/bcf_seqname.
requirements: h must be valid
nseqs must be a valid pointer for output
Caller must free the returned array (not the strings)

functions.name: bcf_hdr_parse
functions.description: Internal-facing: parses textual header content in htxt and populates hdr. Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.
requirements: hdr must be a valid header
htxt must be a modifiable C string containing header text
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_hdr_sync
functions.description: Synchronizes the header’s internal dictionaries and arrays (id/sample/contig) after modifications. Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.
requirements: h must be a valid header possibly modified
Caller must check return value, especially before using id/sample/contig arrays

functions.name: bcf_hdr_parse_line
functions.description: Parses a single textual header line, returning a bcf_hrec_t or NULL. On return, *len indicates status: 0 not a header line (doesn’t start with "##"), -1 failure (OOM), >0 malformed with full line length. Caller frees with bcf_hrec_destroy() unless added to header.
requirements: h must be a valid header
line must point to one or more header lines
len must be a valid pointer for status/length output
On success, caller owns returned hrec until added to header

functions.name: bcf_hrec_format
functions.description: Serializes a header record to text and appends to str. Returns 0 on success; <0 on error.
requirements: hrec must be a valid header record
str must be an initialized kstring
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_hdr_add_hrec
functions.description: Adds a header record to a header. On success, ownership of hrec is transferred to hdr (and hrec may be freed if a duplicate). Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.
requirements: hdr must be a valid header
hrec must be a heap-allocated bcf_hrec_t* not used elsewhere
After success, caller must not use hrec pointer

functions.name: bcf_hdr_get_hrec
functions.signature: bcf_hrec_t *bcf_hdr_get_hrec(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, int type, const char *key, const char *value, const char *str_class);
functions.description: Finds a header record by type and key/value. For generic lines (BCF_HL_GEN), value may be NULL; for structured, key is typically "ID" and value the identifier; str_class selects BCF_HL_STR subclasses (e.g., "ALT","SAMPLE"). Returns matching record or NULL.
requirements: hdr must be valid
type must be one of BCF_HL_*
key/value/str_class usage must match header line kind

functions.name: bcf_hrec_dup
functions.description: Duplicates a header record. Returns a new independent copy or NULL on failure. Caller must free via bcf_hrec_destroy() if not added to a header.
requirements: hrec must be a valid header record
Caller must free returned record when no longer needed

functions.name: bcf_hrec_add_key
functions.signature: int bcf_hrec_add_key(bcf_hrec_t *hrec, const char *str, size_t len);
functions.description: Adds a new key field name to a structured header record. Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.
requirements: hrec must be a valid structured record
str must point to the key name; len is its length
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_hrec_set_val
functions.signature: int bcf_hrec_set_val(bcf_hrec_t *hrec, int i, const char *str, size_t len, int is_quoted);
functions.description: Sets a value for the i-th key in a structured header record. Optionally wraps the value in quotes. Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.
requirements: hrec must be valid and must already contain at least i+1 keys
i must be a valid key index
str/len define the value; is_quoted non-zero to quote

functions.name: bcf_hrec_find_key
functions.description: Finds the index of 'key' in the structured header record; returns index or negative on failure.
requirements: hrec must be valid
key must be a non-NULL string

functions.name: hrec_add_idx
functions.description: Adds/sets the IDX attribute on a header record. Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.
requirements: hrec must be valid
idx must be a non-negative integer index as used in IDX fields
Caller must check return code

functions.name: bcf_hrec_destroy
functions.description: Frees a header record and its associated dynamic allocations. Use when a record is no longer needed or if bcf_hdr_add_hrec() failed. Do not call on records owned by a header (unless removed).
requirements: hrec must be a valid pointer returned by bcf_hdr_parse_line/bcf_hrec_dup/etc., and not owned by a header anymore

functions.name: bcf_subset
functions.signature: int bcf_subset(const bcf_hdr_t *h, bcf1_t *v, int n, int *imap);
functions.description: Subsets a record’s sample-dependent FORMAT data to the n samples specified by imap mapping (index in output -> original index). Used to drop/reorder samples in a single record. Returns 0 on success; negative on error.
requirements: h must be the header for v
v must be a valid record with FORMAT/sample fields
n and imap define the desired sample order and count; imap size must be n
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_translate
functions.description: Translates dictionary/tag IDs in a record from src_hdr’s namespace to be consistent with dst_hdr. Useful when combining records from multiple files. Returns 0 on success; negative on error.
requirements: dst_hdr and src_hdr must be valid headers with appropriate dictionaries
src_line must be a valid record using src_hdr’s IDs
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_get_variant_types
functions.description: Deprecated: computes the set of variant types present in rec and returns a bitmask of VCF_* types (or 0 for VCF_REF). Prefer bcf_has_variant_types().
requirements: rec must be a valid record (ideally with alleles decoded)

functions.name: bcf_get_variant_type
functions.description: Deprecated: returns the variant type for a specific allele index; one of VCF_REF, VCF_SNP, VCF_MNP, VCF_INDEL, VCF_OTHER, VCF_BND, VCF_OVERLAP. Prefer bcf_has_variant_type().
requirements: rec must be valid
ith_allele must be a valid allele index for rec

functions.name: bcf_has_variant_types
functions.signature: int bcf_has_variant_types(bcf1_t *rec, uint32_t bitmask, enum bcf_variant_match mode);
functions.description: Checks presence of variant type(s) in a record according to mode (exact/overlap/subset). Returns bitwise-and of present types and bitmask (>0 present; 0 not present), or -1 on error. Use with VCF_* bitmask; test VCF_REF via exact mode.
requirements: rec must be valid
bitmask is OR of VCF_* constants (or VCF_REF alone)
mode must be one of bcf_variant_match values
Caller must check return value; -1 indicates error

functions.name: bcf_has_variant_type
functions.signature: int bcf_has_variant_type(bcf1_t *rec, int ith_allele, uint32_t bitmask);
functions.description: Checks if a given allele’s variant type matches any in bitmask (or exactly VCF_REF if bitmask==VCF_REF). Returns bitwise-and (>0 present), 0 if not, or -1 on error.
requirements: rec must be valid
ith_allele must be in range
bitmask is OR of VCF_* or VCF_REF alone
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_variant_length
functions.description: Returns the number of bases affected by the variant for the specified allele (negative for deletions), or bcf_int32_missing on error.
requirements: rec must be valid and have REF/ALT alleles
ith_allele must be a valid allele index

functions.name: bcf_is_snp
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the record represents a SNP (all alleles length-1 and single-base changes), 0 otherwise.
requirements: v must be a valid record with alleles available

functions.name: bcf_update_filter
functions.signature: int bcf_update_filter(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, bcf1_t *line, int *flt_ids, int n);
functions.description: Sets the FILTER column to the provided list of numeric filter IDs (header dictionary indices). If n==0 removes all filters. Returns 0 on success; negative on error.
requirements: hdr must be the header used for dictionary lookup
line must be a valid record
flt_ids must point to n integers (IDs returned by bcf_hdr_id2int with BCF_DT_ID)
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_add_filter
functions.signature: int bcf_add_filter(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, bcf1_t *line, int flt_id);
functions.description: Adds a filter to the FILTER column. If flt_id is PASS, removes all existing filters; if adding non-PASS, removes existing PASS. Returns 0 on success; negative on error.
requirements: hdr must be valid
line must be valid
flt_id must be a valid ID from header (e.g., bcf_hdr_id2int)
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_remove_filter
functions.signature: int bcf_remove_filter(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, bcf1_t *line, int flt_id, int pass);
functions.description: Removes a specific filter from FILTER. If pass==1 and no filters remain, sets FILTER to PASS. Returns 0 on success; negative on error.
requirements: hdr must be valid
line must be valid
flt_id must be a valid filter ID
pass must be 0 or 1
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_has_filter
functions.description: Checks if FILTER contains the named filter. Returns 1 if present, 0 if absent, or -1 if the filter tag does not exist. "PASS" and "." are interchangeable.
requirements: hdr must be valid
line must be valid
filter must be a NUL-terminated tag string

functions.name: bcf_update_alleles
functions.signature: int bcf_update_alleles(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, bcf1_t *line, const char **alleles, int nals);
functions.description: Updates REF and ALT columns from an array of allele strings (alleles[0] is REF). Returns 0 on success; negative on error.
requirements: hdr must be valid
line must be valid
alleles must have nals entries; alleles[0] is REF, others ALT
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_update_alleles_str
functions.signature: int bcf_update_alleles_str(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, bcf1_t *line, const char *alleles_string);
functions.description: Updates REF and ALT columns from a comma-separated string starting with REF. Returns 0 on success; negative on error.
requirements: hdr must be valid
line must be valid
alleles_string must be 'REF,ALT1,ALT2,...'
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_update_id
functions.signature: int bcf_update_id(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, bcf1_t *line, const char *id);
functions.description: Sets the ID column to the provided string. Returns 0 on success; negative on error.
requirements: hdr must be valid
line must be valid
id may be NULL or a valid ID string per VCF conventions
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_add_id
functions.signature: int bcf_add_id(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, bcf1_t *line, const char *id);
functions.description: Adds an ID to the ID column if not already present (semicolon-separated). Returns 0 on success; negative on error.
requirements: hdr must be valid
line must be valid
id must be a non-NULL ID string
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_update_info
functions.signature: int bcf_update_info(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, bcf1_t *line, const char *key, const void *values, int n, int type);
functions.description: Sets or updates an INFO field. Pass values array and count with the appropriate type (BCF_HT_INT/REAL/FLAG/STR). Pass NULL or n==0 to remove the tag. Returns 0 on success; negative on error. Note: updating/removing END/SVLEN recalculates rlen; update pos before END/SVLEN to get correct rlen.
requirements: hdr must be valid and define 'key' with matching type
line must be valid
key must be an INFO tag string
values points to array matching 'type' (or may be NULL to remove); n is number of items
For FLAG, values may be optional; n controls set/remove
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_update_format_string
functions.signature: int bcf_update_format_string(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, bcf1_t *line, const char *key, const char **values, int n);
functions.description: High-level update for a per-sample FORMAT string field using an array of NUL-terminated strings (one per sample). Returns 0 on success; negative on error.
requirements: hdr must be valid and define FORMAT key
line must be valid
values must have one entry per sample in the record/header; shorter strings OK
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_update_format
functions.signature: int bcf_update_format(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, bcf1_t *line, const char *key, const void *values, int n, int type);
functions.description: Sets or updates a per-sample FORMAT field with raw data array and type (INT/REAL/STR). n is total number of items across all samples; missing values must be padded with appropriate end/missing sentinels. If n==0, removes the tag. Returns 0 on success; negative on error. Note: with VCFv4.5, rlen may depend on LEN FORMAT; update pos before LEN if needed.
requirements: hdr must be valid and define the FORMAT key
line must be valid
values must point to the correctly typed array across all samples; pad missing with bcf_*_missing or bcf_*_vector_end
n must match the total elements expected (vectorized across samples)
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_get_fmt
functions.description: Returns a pointer to FORMAT field data for key in the given record, or NULL if absent. Provides direct access to raw typed data.
requirements: hdr must be valid
line must be valid (unpacked to at least FORMAT if needed)
key must be a NUL-terminated FORMAT tag string

functions.name: bcf_get_info
functions.description: Returns a pointer to INFO field data for key in the record, or NULL if absent.
requirements: hdr must be valid
line must be valid (unpacked to INFO if needed)
key must be a NUL-terminated INFO tag string

functions.name: bcf_get_fmt_id
functions.description: Returns a pointer to FORMAT field data by numeric header index (ID). No validation of id beyond presence in record; avoids header lookup.
requirements: line must be valid
id must be a valid header index for a FORMAT tag (typically from bcf_hdr_id2int)

functions.name: bcf_get_info_id
functions.description: Returns a pointer to INFO field data by numeric header index (ID). No header lookup performed.
requirements: line must be valid
id must be a valid header index for an INFO tag

functions.name: bcf_get_info_values
functions.signature: int bcf_get_info_values(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, bcf1_t *line, const char *tag, void **dst, int *ndst, int type);
functions.description: Retrieves INFO values of a given type into a caller-managed buffer (reallocating as needed). Returns number of values (>=0) on success; -1 no such tag in header; -2 type clash; -3 tag not present in record; -4 other failure. For strings returns character count (excluding NUL); for flag returns 1/0 and stores nothing.
requirements: hdr must be valid and define the tag
line must be valid
tag must be a NUL-terminated INFO key
dst must be a pointer to a buffer pointer; may point to NULL to allocate
ndst must point to an int storing current allocated size; updated on reallocation
type must match desired output (BCF_HT_INT/REAL/STR/FLAG)
Caller must free/reuse *dst as allocated

functions.name: bcf_get_format_string
functions.signature: int bcf_get_format_string(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, bcf1_t *line, const char *tag, char ***dst, int *ndst);
functions.description: Retrieves a per-sample FORMAT string field as an array of char* pointing into a newly-allocated collapsed string block. Returns number of strings (>0) on success; negative on error. Caller must free dst[0] (the block) and dst.
requirements: hdr must be valid and define tag as FORMAT/STR
line must be valid
dst must point to a char** variable; function allocates array and backing block
ndst points to watermark size (may be grown)
Caller must free dst[0] then dst when done

functions.name: bcf_get_format_values
functions.signature: int bcf_get_format_values(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, bcf1_t *line, const char *tag, void **dst, int *ndst, int type);
functions.description: Retrieves per-sample FORMAT values of given type into caller-managed buffer (reallocating as needed). Returns number of written values on success; negative on error. Use returned count to iterate valid entries.
requirements: hdr must be valid and define the tag
line must be valid
dst must be a pointer to a buffer pointer; may be NULL to allocate
ndst must point to current allocated size watermark; updated as needed
type must be BCF_HT_INT/REAL/STR matching desired output
Caller must free or reuse *dst as allocated

functions.name: bcf_hdr_id2int
functions.signature: int bcf_hdr_id2int(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, int type, const char *id);
functions.description: Looks up a string ID (INFO/FORMAT/FILTER or contig/sample depending on 'type') in the header dictionaries and returns its numeric index, or -1 if not found.
requirements: hdr must be valid
type must be one of BCF_DT_ID, BCF_DT_CTG, BCF_DT_SAMPLE
id must be a NUL-terminated key string

functions.name: bcf_fmt_array
functions.signature: int bcf_fmt_array(kstring_t *s, int n, int type, void *data);
functions.description: Converts a typed BCF array into textual VCF form and appends to string s. Returns 0 on success; -1 on OOM.
requirements: s must be an initialized kstring
n is number of items in data
type must be a BCF_BT_* element type
data must point to array of the specified type and length

functions.name: bcf_fmt_sized_array
functions.description: Formats a BCF-sized array given by ptr (which encodes size/type) into text and appends to s, returning pointer to the byte after the array in the input stream. Useful when iterating raw BCF blocks.
requirements: s must be an initialized kstring
ptr must point to a valid BCF sized-array encoding

functions.name: bcf_enc_vchar
functions.signature: int bcf_enc_vchar(kstring_t *s, int l, const char *a);
functions.description: Encodes a variable-length char array into BCF format and appends to s. Returns 0 on success; <0 on error.
requirements: s must be an initialized kstring with capacity growth allowed
a must point to at least l bytes of data

functions.name: bcf_enc_vint
functions.signature: int bcf_enc_vint(kstring_t *s, int n, int32_t *a, int wsize);
functions.description: Encodes a variable-length integer array into BCF format and appends to s. n is total items (<=0 encodes NULL), wsize is vector length (<=0 treated as n). Returns 0 on success; <0 on error. Note: n must be an exact multiple of wsize.
requirements: s must be an initialized kstring
If n>0, a must point to n int32_t values
If wsize>0, n must be a multiple of wsize
Caller must check return code

functions.name: bcf_enc_vfloat
functions.description: Encodes a variable-length float array into BCF format and appends to s. n<=0 encodes NULL. Returns 0 on success; <0 on error.
requirements: s must be an initialized kstring
If n>0, a must point to n float values
Caller must check return code

functions.name: bcf_index_load2
functions.description: Loads a BCF index from a specified index filename. Returns index pointer or NULL on error. Only works for BCF files; consider synced_bcf_reader for VCF.
requirements: fn must be the data filename; fnidx must be the index filename
Files may be local or remote as supported by HTSlib
Caller must free index with hts_idx_destroy() when done

functions.name: bcf_index_load3
functions.signature: hts_idx_t *bcf_index_load3(const char *fn, const char *fnidx, int flags);
functions.description: Loads a BCF index with extra flags. Returns index pointer or NULL on error. Flags: HTS_IDX_SAVE_REMOTE (cache remote), HTS_IDX_SILENT_FAIL (suppress errors).
requirements: fn is data filename; fnidx index filename
flags is a bitwise combination of HTS index flags
Caller must free index with hts_idx_destroy() when done

functions.name: bcf_index_build
functions.description: Builds and writes an index for a VCF(.gz) or BCF file. min_shift>0 for CSI (recommended 14), 0 for TBI (not for BCF). Returns 0 on success; negative on error (-1 failed, -2 open failed, -3 format not indexable, -4 save failed).
requirements: fn must be an existing VCF(.gz) or BCF filename
For BCF, only CSI index (min_shift>0) can be generated
Caller must check return code and handle negative error meanings

functions.name: bcf_index_build2
functions.signature: int bcf_index_build2(const char *fn, const char *fnidx, int min_shift);
functions.description: Builds an index for a VCF/BCF file and writes it to fnidx (or derives from fn if NULL). Returns 0 on success; negative on error with same codes as bcf_index_build.
requirements: fn must exist and be indexable
fnidx may be NULL to auto-name output; otherwise writable path
min_shift rules as in bcf_index_build
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_index_build3
functions.signature: int bcf_index_build3(const char *fn, const char *fnidx, int min_shift, int n_threads);
functions.description: Builds an index for VCF/BCF using up to n_threads decoder threads. Returns 0 on success; negative on error (same codes as build2).
requirements: fn must exist and be indexable
fnidx may be NULL or output filename
min_shift as above; BCF requires CSI
n_threads must be >=1 (implied)
Caller must check return code

functions.name: bcf_idx_init
functions.signature: int bcf_idx_init(htsFile *fp, bcf_hdr_t *h, int min_shift, const char *fnidx);
functions.description: Initializes index creation for a file being written (VCF/BCF). Must be called after header write and before any records. fnidx must remain valid until bcf_idx_save. Returns 0 on success; <0 on failure.
requirements: fp must be an htsFile opened for writing VCF/BCF
h must be the header for the file (needed for BAI/CSI)
min_shift is CSI bin size (CSI default 14)
fnidx must point to a filename string that remains valid until bcf_idx_save
Call only after writing header and before writing records

functions.name: bcf_idx_save
functions.description: Finalizes and writes the index initialized with bcf_idx_init to disk. Returns 0 on success; <0 on failure.
requirements: fp must be the same file handle previously passed to bcf_idx_init and still open
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_format_gt_v2
functions.signature: int bcf_format_gt_v2(const bcf_hdr_t *hdr, bcf_fmt_t *fmt, int isample, kstring_t *str);
functions.description: Formats the GT (genotype) field for a single sample into a string (supports VCF 4.4 and prefixed phasing rules). Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure. Preferred over legacy bcf_format_gt.
requirements: fmt must be a FORMAT field for GT (obtained from bcf_get_fmt)
isample must be the sample index within fmt
str must be an initialized kstring for output
hdr may be NULL but improves version-aware formatting; pass header for VCFv4.4 behaviors
Caller must check return value

functions.name: bcf_trim_alleles
functions.description: Remove ALT alleles from a VCF record that are not used in any genotype fields. Use when you want to drop unused alternates and consistently update the record. Returns the number of removed alleles on success or a negative error code (-1: allele index out of bounds; -2: could not remove alleles).
requirements: header must be a valid pointer to the header corresponding to line (used for BCF_DT_ID dictionary lookups).
line must be a valid VCF/BCF record obtained from vcf_parse1 (initialized and populated).
The record’s genotype (FORMAT/GT) and related fields should be present/consistent to allow determining unused alleles.
Callers must handle negative return values as errors and non-negative values as the count of removed alleles.
The function may modify the record by removing alleles; callers should not assume prior allele indexes remain valid after the call.

functions.name: bcf_remove_alleles
functions.signature: int bcf_remove_alleles(const bcf_hdr_t *header, bcf1_t *line, int mask);
functions.description: Remove ALT alleles from a VCF record according to an integer bit mask. Bit i indicates whether allele i is to be removed (exact mapping beyond ALT-only removal is not documented here). Deprecated in favor of bcf_remove_allele_set due to integer mask overflow for many alleles. Returns 0 on success, <0 on error.
requirements: This API is deprecated; prefer bcf_remove_allele_set for records with many alleles.
header must be a valid pointer to the header corresponding to line (used for BCF_DT_ID dictionary lookups).
line must be a valid VCF/BCF record obtained from vcf_parse1 (initialized and populated).
mask encodes alleles to remove; if the record has more than 31 alleles the integer bit mask can overflow and must not be used.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; negative indicates failure.
The function will modify the record by removing alleles; any stored allele indexes must be refreshed after the call.

functions.name: bcf_remove_allele_set
functions.signature: int bcf_remove_allele_set(const bcf_hdr_t *header, bcf1_t *line, const struct kbitset_t *rm_set);
functions.description: Remove ALT alleles from a VCF record according to a bitset of allele indexes. Uses a kbitset_t to avoid integer mask overflow. Returns 0 on success or -1 on failure. Automatically updates Number=A, Number=R, and Number=G INFO and FORMAT fields to remain consistent after allele removal.
requirements: header must be a valid pointer to the header corresponding to line (used for BCF_DT_ID dictionary lookups).
line must be a valid VCF/BCF record obtained from vcf_parse1 (initialized and populated).

rm_set must be a valid kbitset_t with bits set for the allele indexes to remove; indexes are zero-based as typical for allele arrays, but whether the reference allele (index 0) can be removed is not specified here (unknown).
The record will be modified; callers must not rely on previous allele ordering or indexes after removal.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: bcf_calc_ac
functions.signature: int bcf_calc_ac(const bcf_hdr_t *header, bcf1_t *line, int *ac, int which);
functions.description: Compute allele counts (number of REF and ALT alleles) for a record. Fills ac with counts for each allele, where ac has length line->n_allele. The calculation may use INFO/AN,AC and/or genotype fields depending on which flags (e.g., BCF_UN_INFO, BCF_UN_FMT). Returns 1 on success, 0 if the counts could not be determined.
requirements: header must be a valid pointer to the header corresponding to line (used for dictionary and metadata lookups).
line must be a valid VCF/BCF record obtained from vcf_parse1 (initialized and populated).
ac must point to writable storage of at least line->n_allele integers.
which controls data sources: permitting use of INFO/AC,AN (BCF_UN_INFO) and/or splitting/using individual FORMAT fields (BCF_UN_FMT). The specific flag values are defined elsewhere (in vcf.h).
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success; 0 indicates the counts could not be determined.
Any preexisting contents of ac will be overwritten.

functions.name: bcf_gt_type
functions.signature: int bcf_gt_type(bcf_fmt_t *fmt_ptr, int isample, int *ial, int *jal);
functions.description: Determine the genotype type for a sample from the GT FORMAT field. Returns one of GT_HOM_RR, GT_HET_RA, GT_HOM_AA, GT_HET_AA, GT_HAPL_R, GT_HAPL_A, or GT_UNKN. If ial is non-NULL and a non-reference allele is present, *ial is set to the index (1-based per description) of the first non-reference allele. If jal is non-NULL and the genotype is GT_HET_AA, *jal is set to the index of the second ALT allele.
requirements: fmt_ptr must refer to the record’s GT FORMAT field (a valid bcf_fmt_t for FORMAT/GT) with decodable genotype values.
isample must be a valid 0-based sample index within the number of samples present in the record.
ial may be NULL or must point to writable int storage; on output may receive the first non-reference allele index for the sample as described.
jal may be NULL or must point to writable int storage; on output is set only for GT_HET_AA to the second ALT allele index as described.
Callers must interpret the return value against the defined GT_* constants (GT_HOM_RR, GT_HET_RA, GT_HOM_AA, GT_HET_AA, GT_HAPL_R, GT_HAPL_A, GT_UNKN).
Behavior if the GT field is missing or malformed is not specified here; callers should be prepared for GT_UNKN (unknown).

functions.name: bcf_sr_init
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a synced BCF/VCF reader controller (bcf_srs_t). Use to coordinate streaming across one or more VCF/BCF inputs. Free it with bcf_sr_destroy() when finished.
requirements: Must be paired with bcf_sr_destroy() to avoid memory/resource leaks.
Returned pointer must be checked for NULL on allocation failure (not explicitly stated, but typical).

functions.name: bcf_sr_destroy
functions.description: Destroy and free a bcf_srs_t created by bcf_sr_init(), closing any associated readers and resources.
requirements: readers must be a valid pointer previously returned by bcf_sr_init().
Do not use the readers pointer after calling this function.

functions.name: bcf_sr_strerror
functions.description: Return a human-readable error message string corresponding to an error code (e.g., values from bcf_sr_error or readers->errnum). Intended for reporting errors encountered by the synced reader API.
requirements: errnum should be a valid error code as produced by this API (e.g., bcf_srs_t.errnum).
String ownership/lifetime is not specified; treat as unknown (do not free unless documented elsewhere).

functions.name: bcf_sr_set_opt
functions.description: Set an option controlling the behavior of the synced reader. Options include requiring an index, pairing logic, and overlap handling for regions/targets. Usage: call before adding readers or as appropriate to adjust behavior.
requirements: readers must be a valid initialized bcf_srs_t pointer.
opt must be one of: BCF_SR_REQUIRE_IDX, BCF_SR_PAIR_LOGIC, BCF_SR_ALLOW_NO_IDX, BCF_SR_REGIONS_OVERLAP, BCF_SR_TARGETS_OVERLAP.

Varargs depend on opt; details are not fully specified here. Inferred: BCF_SR_PAIR_LOGIC expects an int bitmask composed of BCF_SR_PAIR_* flags; BCF_SR_REGIONS_OVERLAP and BCF_SR_TARGETS_OVERLAP expect an int value 0,1, or 2; other options may be toggles (int). Exact vararg types/usage beyond this are unknown in this header.
Returns int status (unspecified exact values); caller should check for failure.

functions.name: bcf_sr_set_threads
functions.description: Allocate a thread pool of size n_threads for use by the synced reader to enable multi-threaded decoding/encoding.
requirements: files must be a valid initialized bcf_srs_t pointer.
n_threads specifies the size of the thread pool; valid range and behavior for 0 or negative values are not specified here.
Returns 0 on success, <0 on error; caller must check the return value and handle errors.

functions.name: bcf_sr_destroy_threads
functions.description: Deallocate thread-pool resources previously set on this synced reader, if owned by the reader.
requirements: files must be a valid initialized bcf_srs_t pointer.
Only deallocates threads if they are owned by the synced reader (ownership rules beyond this are not specified).
Safe timing for calling relative to active I/O is not specified; avoid calling while operations may still be using the pool.

functions.name: bcf_sr_add_reader
functions.description: Open a new VCF/BCF reader on file fname and add it to the synced reader set. Honors settings like filters and pairing/require-index logic applied to the bcf_srs_t.
requirements: readers must be a valid initialized bcf_srs_t pointer.
fname must reference an accessible VCF/BCF (optionally bgzip/tabix) file.
If bcf_sr_set_targets() is used, it MUST be called before the first call to bcf_sr_add_reader().
Settings such as apply_filters are applied at initialization (during add_reader).
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value and may inspect readers->errnum for details.

functions.name: bcf_sr_add_hreader
functions.signature: int bcf_sr_add_hreader(bcf_srs_t *readers, htsFile *file_ptr, int autoclose, const char *idxname);
functions.description: Add a new reader using an already-open htsFile handle. Optionally auto-close the file when the reader is destroyed. Allows specifying an explicit index filename.
requirements: readers must be a valid initialized bcf_srs_t pointer.
file_ptr must be a valid, already opened htsFile pointing to a VCF/BCF (or tabix-indexed text) file.
autoclose controls ownership: 1 to close file with reader, 0 to leave it open.
If idxname is NULL, the index is located via file_ptr->fn using the default index filename; in that case, the index file must exist under the default name.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: bcf_sr_remove_reader
functions.description: Remove and close the ith reader from the synced reader set.
requirements: files must be a valid initialized bcf_srs_t pointer.
i must refer to an existing reader index within the current set; valid range is not stated here but is implied to be [0, nreaders).
After removal, the index positions of remaining readers may shift (behavior not specified here).

functions.name: bcf_sr_next_line
functions.description: Advance to the next genomic position across all synchronized readers. Returns the number of readers that have a line at the current position; use bcf_sr_has_line/readers->has_line to determine which readers have data and bcf_sr_get_line to retrieve each record.
requirements: readers must be a valid initialized bcf_srs_t with at least one reader added.
Caller must use the provided macros to check per-reader availability (bcf_sr_has_line) before dereferencing bcf_sr_get_line.
Return value should be checked; 0 indicates no readers at current position (end or filtered).
Behavior depends on pairing logic and targets/regions settings.

functions.name: bcf_sr_seek
functions.signature: int bcf_sr_seek(bcf_srs_t *readers, const char *seq, hts_pos_t pos);
functions.description: Seek all readers to a selected genomic position. If seq is NULL, seek to the start. Coordinates are 0-based.
requirements: readers must be a valid initialized bcf_srs_t pointer with readers added.
seq is the sequence name to seek to, or NULL to seek to the start of the data.
pos must be a 0-based coordinate.
Returns int status (unspecified exact values here); caller must check for success.

functions.name: bcf_sr_set_samples
functions.signature: int bcf_sr_set_samples(bcf_srs_t *readers, const char *samples, int is_file);
functions.description: Set the active set of samples for subsequent reading/processing. The samples argument may be a filename with one sample per line, a column-separated list, or '-' to use a list common to all files. If the first character is '!', all but the listed samples are included.
requirements: readers must be a valid initialized bcf_srs_t pointer.
samples must be one of: a path to a file of sample names, a column-separated list of samples, or '-' for a shared list across files.
If samples begins with '!', the selection is inverted (exclude listed samples).
is_file must be 0 for a list, 1 for a file.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return code.

functions.name: bcf_sr_set_targets
functions.signature: int bcf_sr_set_targets(bcf_srs_t *readers, const char *targets, int is_file, int alleles);
functions.description: Initialize target regions. Both targets and regions cause bcf_sr_next_line() to skip unlisted positions, but targets stream entire files (no index jumping). Targets support allele-based prioritization via a column index and may be logically complemented using a leading '^' on the targets string.
requirements: Must be called BEFORE the first call to bcf_sr_add_reader().
readers must be a valid initialized bcf_srs_t pointer.
targets is either a comma-separated list of regions (chr or chr:from-to) when is_file==0, or a tabix-indexed file with regions (<chr,pos> or <chr,from,to>) when is_file==1.
Coordinates are 1-based and inclusive in the input region specifications.

alleles, if non-zero, is interpreted as a 1-based column index in a tab-delimited file listing alleles; behavior is a prioritization aid only and duplicate positions in targets files are not supported.
Targets may be prefixed with '^' to indicate logical complement (skip listed sequences).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: bcf_sr_set_regions
functions.signature: int bcf_sr_set_regions(bcf_srs_t *readers, const char *regions, int is_file);
functions.description: Initialize regions for indexed jumping. Regions use the index to jump to positions, whereas targets stream and skip. Calling this after readers are initialized will reposition readers and discard previously set regions.
requirements: readers must be a valid initialized bcf_srs_t pointer.
regions is either a comma-separated list (chr or chr:from-to) when is_file==0, or a tabix-indexed file with regions (<chr,pos> or <chr,from,to>) when is_file==1.
Coordinates in the provided region specifications are 1-based and inclusive.
Calling after readers have been initialized will reposition the readers and discard all previous regions.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: bcf_sr_regions_init
functions.signature: bcf_sr_regions_t *bcf_sr_regions_init(const char *regions, int is_file, int chr, int from, int to);
functions.description: Create and initialize a regions iterator object for region lists provided either inline or via VCF/BED/tab-delimited (possibly tabix-indexed) files. Uncompressed files are held in memory; bgzip-compressed and tabix-indexed files are streamed.
requirements: regions may be a comma-separated list of regions (chr | chr:pos | chr:from-to | chr:from-) when is_file==0, or a VCF, BED, or tab-delimited file when is_file==1.

For tab-delimited files, column indexes chr/from/to specify chromosome, start, end columns; positions are 1-based and inclusive. If end is absent, supply 'from' in place of 'to'. If 'to' is negative, first abs(to) is attempted; if that fails, 'from' is used instead.
Chromosome names containing ':' or '-' must be wrapped in curly braces, e.g., {weird-chr-name:1-2}:1000-2000.
The returned pointer must be freed with bcf_sr_regions_destroy() when no longer needed.

functions.name: bcf_sr_regions_destroy
functions.description: Destroy and free a bcf_sr_regions_t created by bcf_sr_regions_init().
requirements: regions must be a valid pointer previously returned by bcf_sr_regions_init().
Do not use the regions pointer after calling this function.

functions.name: bcf_sr_regions_seek
functions.description: Seek the regions iterator to the specified chromosome block. On success, sets reg->seq appropriately and reg->start/reg->end to -1.
requirements: regions must be a valid initialized bcf_sr_regions_t pointer.
chr is the chromosome name to seek to.
Returns 0 on success or -1 on failure; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: bcf_sr_regions_next
functions.description: Advance the regions iterator to the next region. On success, fills reg->seq, reg->start, and reg->end with 0-based inclusive genomic coordinates; when no region is available, they are set to NULL, -1, -1.
requirements: reg must be a valid initialized bcf_sr_regions_t pointer.
Returns 0 on success and -1 when all regions have been read; caller must check the return value before using reg->seq/start/end.

functions.name: bcf_sr_regions_overlap
functions.signature: int bcf_sr_regions_overlap(bcf_sr_regions_t *reg, const char *seq, hts_pos_t start, hts_pos_t end);
functions.description: Check whether the 0-based inclusive interval [start, end] overlaps any configured regions. Designed for ascending-order coordinate queries.
requirements: reg must be a valid initialized bcf_sr_regions_t pointer.
seq must be a valid sequence name; start and end are 0-based inclusive coordinates.
Coordinate queries must be provided in ascending order.
Returns 0 if the position is in regions; -1 if not in regions but more regions exist; -2 if not in regions and there are no more regions left. Caller must handle each return code appropriately.

functions.name: bcf_sr_regions_flush
functions.description: Call the user-provided missed_reg_handler repeatedly to process any remaining regions that were skipped without a counterpart in VCFs. Flushes all remaining records.
requirements: regs must be a valid initialized bcf_sr_regions_t pointer.
A missed_reg_handler callback should be set on regs to handle flushed regions; behavior is undefined if no handler is set (not specified here).
Returns 0 on success, <0 on error; caller must check and handle errors.

functions.name: regidx_parse_bed
functions.signature: int regidx_parse_bed(const char *line, char **chr_beg, char **chr_end, hts_pos_t *beg, hts_pos_t *end, void *payload, void *usr)
functions.description: Parses one input line in BED-like format to extract a chromosome name and 0-based coordinates. Accepts either a single CHROM field or whitespace-separated CHROM FROM TO where the interval is 0-based, right-open in the input (TO is not included). The parser sets chr_beg/chr_end to the first/last characters of the chromosome name within the input line and computes 0-based, inclusive beg/end coordinates for the index (typically end becomes TO-1). Leading spaces are ignored and lines starting with '#' are skipped. On success returns 0; return -1 to skip a record (e.g., blank/comment/unsupported), or -2 on fatal error. If payload_size was non-zero in regidx_init, payload points to writable storage for the parser to fill; any allocations made by the parser will be released by the regidx_free_f provided to regidx_init when the index is destroyed.
requirements: line must point to a NUL-terminated string; leading spaces are permitted; lines beginning with '#' are ignored.
Expected formats: 'CHROM' or whitespace-separated 'CHROM FROM TO' where FROM and TO are 0-based, right-open in the input.
On success, set chr_beg and chr_end to point within line to the first and last characters of the chromosome name, inclusive.
Set beg and end to 0-based, inclusive coordinates appropriate for the index.
Return values: 0 on success; -1 to skip the record; -2 on fatal error.

If regidx_init was called with non-zero payload_size, payload points to a buffer of that size for parser use; any memory allocated by the parser must be releasable by the regidx_free_f callback at regidx_destroy time.
usr is the opaque user pointer supplied to regidx_init and must be passed through unchanged.

functions.name: regidx_parse_tab
functions.signature: int regidx_parse_tab(const char *line, char **chr_beg, char **chr_end, hts_pos_t *beg, hts_pos_t *end, void *payload, void *usr)
functions.description: Parses one input line in a simple tab/whitespace-delimited format to extract a chromosome and a 1-based position. Accepts either a single CHROM field or whitespace-separated CHROM POS (1-based, inclusive). Sets chr_beg/chr_end to the first/last characters of the chromosome name and computes 0-based, inclusive beg/end coordinates (typically beg=end=POS-1). Leading spaces are ignored and lines starting with '#' are skipped. Returns 0 on success, -1 to skip a record, or -2 on fatal error. If payload_size was non-zero in regidx_init, payload is available for parser use and will be freed via regidx_free_f on destroy.
requirements: line must be a NUL-terminated string; leading spaces allowed; lines starting with '#' are ignored.
Expected formats: 'CHROM' or whitespace-separated 'CHROM POS' where POS is 1-based, inclusive.
On success, set chr_beg and chr_end to delimit the chromosome substring within line.
Set beg and end to 0-based, inclusive coordinates (e.g., for a single position, beg=end=POS-1).
Return values: 0 on success; -1 to skip the record; -2 on fatal error.
If regidx_init was called with non-zero payload_size, payload points to a buffer of that size; any extra allocations must be compatible with the regidx_free_f provided to regidx_init.
usr is the user pointer from regidx_init.

functions.name: regidx_parse_reg
functions.signature: int regidx_parse_reg(const char *line, char **chr_beg, char **chr_end, hts_pos_t *beg, hts_pos_t *end, void *payload, void *usr)
functions.description: Parses region strings like CHROM, CHROM:POS, CHROM:FROM-TO, or CHROM:FROM- (open-ended), where coordinates are 1-based and inclusive in the input. Sets chr_beg/chr_end to the chromosome substring within the line and computes 0-based, inclusive beg/end for indexing. Leading spaces are ignored and lines starting with '#' are skipped. Returns 0 on success, -1 to skip, -2 on fatal error. If payload_size was non-zero in regidx_init, payload is provided for parser use; allocations will be freed via the regidx_free_f callback on destroy.
requirements: line must be a NUL-terminated string; leading spaces allowed; lines beginning with '#' are ignored.
Supported forms: 'CHROM', 'CHROM:POS', 'CHROM:FROM-TO', 'CHROM:FROM-' (all 1-based in input).

On success, set chr_beg and chr_end to delimit the chromosome substring; set beg and end to 0-based, inclusive coordinates (e.g., POS-1; FROM-1 to TO-1; open-ended TO mapped appropriately by the parser).
Return values: 0 on success; -1 to skip the record; -2 on fatal error.
If regidx_init used non-zero payload_size, payload points to writable storage of that size; any parser allocations must be releasable by regidx_free_f.
usr is the application-provided pointer from regidx_init.

functions.signature: int regidx_parse_vcf(const char *line, char **chr_beg, char **chr_end, hts_pos_t *beg, hts_pos_t *end, void *payload, void *usr)
functions.description: Parses one VCF-format line to extract CHROM and POS/interval, producing 0-based, inclusive beg/end coordinates and chr_beg/chr_end pointers into the line. Leading spaces are ignored and lines starting with '#' (e.g., VCF headers) are skipped. Returns 0 on success, -1 to skip a record, -2 on fatal error. If payload_size was non-zero in regidx_init, payload is provided for parser use with cleanup via regidx_free_f on index destruction. Detailed field handling depends on the implementation (not specified here).
